units.la: CUM ante annos prope sedecim, inter caetera veterum monumenta peruestigata, in farragine quoq; Gratiani, quam librum Decretorum vocant, incidissem, eamq; perlustrarem, quam ille ex Veterum conciliorum Decretis, scriptisq; & dictis patrum collegit, & in unum corpus sua quadam methodo compositam, redegit, inveni multa, quae mihi cum veteri Apostolica & syncériore doctrina convenire, & cum multis, quae hodie ecclesiae tanquam Catholica & orthodoxa obtrudũtur, imo sub nomine ecclesiae aguntur, usurpantur & venditantur, plurimum disconvenientiae habere deprehendebantur. Confirmatum ergo ex lectione horum cepi paucula ex illis, mihi hoc est, in meos pri-vatos usus colligere & excerpere. Ea demum in certa quoq; capita & titulos digesi, ut quid ex Decretis de eiusmodi rebus haberi posset, in promptu esset. Hunc libellum diu apud me se-pultum, tandem amici quidam mei, viri docti & pij, apud me visum[?], utilem existimauerunt, si per typos euulgaretur[?]. Inter quos erat & so-cer ille meus, senex venerandus, Ioannes Gla-uerus, mihi merito charus & singulariter ho-norandus. Cuius iudicio, utpote seni multiscio religionis & purioris[?] studiosissimo, & diu in Re-publica feliciter versato plurimum tribui. Usus itaque bonorum & doctorum virorum iudicio & consilio, cum id illis adprobaretur, passus sum illum prælo subijci. Si quæ ergo inde utilitas ad aliquem redeat, est quòd mihi gratuler & Domino gratias agam. Exiguus est, nec mihi multo labore aut arte constitit, multa tamen continet lectu non inutilia. Neque verò quenquam [illegible, ~2 letters] suggillare aut provocare volo, satis mihi est, quòd si quis aueat cognoscere quid in Decretorum libris sit, quod cum nostræ ætatis doctrina conueniat, illud hic habeat quasi in In dice expositum. Et ut omnes tanto moderatius de nobis & ecclesiarum nostrarū doctrina iudi-cēt, cum videant nos in primarijs dogmatibus nihil à doctrina veteris ecclesiae dissere. Ideoq; iniquè nos haereseos insimulari. Si enim haeretica sunt quae nos docemus, haeretica etiam erunt ista omnia, quae hic ex Decretis annotata sunt, & sic haereseos etiam illi proprium suum Ius maxima ex parte accusabunt. Nec etiam haec collegi, ut istis tantum, quantū sacris Prophetarum & Apostolorū scriptis tribuam, ex quibus solis tanquā purissimis fontibus doctrina sana petenda est, sed ut appareat haec non aliena esse à doctrina illorum, & proinde multos dum in nos furiunt, proprio suo se conficere gladio, sibi ipsis in multis contradicere & contra agere, dum in nobis condemnant, quod in ipsorum-met Decretis positum est. Quid enim cupimus aut quaerimus nos aliud, quàm hanc ipsam doctrinam, haec ipsa dogmata, ex ipsis hic Decretis excerpta, apud omnes valere, ab omnibus exerceri, apud omnes in usu esse? Ita facile tandem ad Christianam res redigi possent concordiam. Scio alioqui testimonia vetustatis quaedam[?] in hoc libello nostro adductâ, licet per se satis clara & pia sint, à versipellibus, inter paleas reputari, & produci quidè ab ipsis quoq; in me-dium, mox tamen sophisticè torqueri, luxari contrariisq; obscurari, & tantum non expungi sententiis. Qui tamen viri pij & prudentes sa-piunt, non patiuntur huiusmodi nebulas suis of-fundere oculis, ut pro non dictis habeant, quæ disertè à veteribus sunt dicta, aut pro exoletis & obelo iugulandis iudicent, quæ congruunt cū sententiis scripturarum, & per se satis sunt probabilia & clara.
units.tr: About sixteen years ago, while searching through the ancient records, I came upon the medley of Gratian, which they call the Book of Decrees. As I went through it, I found that he had gathered from the decrees of the ancient councils and from the writings and sayings of the Fathers, and had arranged them into one body by a certain method of his own. I found much that seemed to agree with the old apostolic and purer teaching, but to differ very widely from much that is today forced upon the Church as Catholic and orthodox, or indeed carried on, used and peddled under the name of the Church. Having been stirred up by reading these, I began to gather and excerpt a few of them for my own private use, and I set them out under certain chapters and headings, so that what the Decrees might offer on such matters would be ready to hand, as if in the Index. This little book lay buried with me for a long time, until certain friends of mine, learned and pious men, who had seen it, judged it useful, provided it were made public in print. Among them was my father-in-law, that venerable old man Johannes Glaverus, justly dear to me and singularly to be honoured. I attribute much weight to his judgment, since he is an old man of wide experience in religion, very zealous for its purity, and long and successfully engaged in public affairs. So, using the judgment and counsel of good and learned men, and since they approved of it, I allowed it to be put to the press. If any use comes of it to anyone, I shall rejoice on that account and give thanks to the Lord. It is small, and it has cost me no great labour or skill, yet it contains much that is not useless to read. I do not wish to disparage or provoke anyone; it is enough for me if anyone who wishes to know what there is in the books of the Decrees that agrees with the teaching of our own age will find it here, set out as in an index. And I hope that everyone will judge us and the teaching of our churches more moderately, seeing that we differ in nothing essential from the doctrine of the ancient Church. It is therefore unjust to accuse us of heresy. For if what we teach is heretical, then all these things noted here from the Decrees will be heretical too, and in this way they would condemn for heresy most of what is their own law. Nor have I gathered these things so as to grant to them as much authority as to the holy writings of the Prophets and Apostles, from which alone sound doctrine must be sought as from the purest fountains, but so that it may appear that these things are not foreign to the teaching of those men, and that many of them, while they rage against us, are destroying themselves with their own sword, contradicting themselves in many points and acting against themselves, when they condemn in us what is laid down in their own Decrees. For what else do we desire or seek, than that this very doctrine and these very tenets, excerpted here from their own Decrees, should prevail with all, be practised by all, and be in use among all? So at last matters could easily be brought back to Christian concord. I know, moreover, that some testimonies of antiquity cited in this little book of ours, although in themselves clear enough and pious, will be reckoned by crafty men as chaff among the wheat; and they may indeed bring them forward, but soon twist them by sophistry, distort them, obscure them by contrary senses, and almost wipe them out. Yet the pious and prudent men who are wise do not allow such mists to be cast over their eyes, so that they should count as unsaid what the ancients have plainly said, or judge as obsolete and to be marked with the obelus what agrees with the sayings of Scripture and is in itself sufficiently probable and clear.

units.la: Vobis verò viri amplissimi & domini mei perpetua mihi obseruantia colendi, quicquid id operis est, ascribere & dedicare volui. Præci-puè quòd eiusmodi studijs & lectione rerum antiquarū apprimè vos delectari sciam, sed & de eiusmodi rebus præ cæteris optimè iudicare posse. Deinde vt animum simul meum erga vos testarer gratificādi inseruiendiq; vobis semper paratissimū: quippe qui me & meos omnes sem-per psequuti sitis amore singulari, & nunc quoq; affectum & studium illud erga me vestrum con-stanter retineatis. Præterea quòd merito vos debita prosequor obseruantia, idq; vestras illas ob virtutes eximias, diuinitus & liberaliter vobis concessas, prudentiam puto, agendi dexte ritatem, eruditionem, eloquentiam iustitiamq; & quòd inter hæc excellit, veræ & synceræ religionis amore eiusq; propagandæ studium singulare. In quibus vt pergatis quàm possum maximè hortor, Dominum interim Deum nostrum obsecrans, vt dona ista sua in vobis & confirmet & augeat ad sui nominis gloriam totiusq; Reipub. nostræ salutem & incolumitatem. Bene valete. Dominus & vobis & familijs vestris benedicere dignetur, & ab omni præseruare malo. Datæ Bernæ in Helvetia 5. Maij. Anno salutis nostræ M. D. LXXII.
units.tr: To you, most distinguished men and my lords, whom I am bound always to honour, I wished to dedicate and ascribe whatever this work is. Chiefly because I know you take special delight in such studies and in reading ancient things, and are also able to judge such matters better than others. Next, so that I might at the same time bear witness to my goodwill towards you, always most ready to oblige and serve you, since you have ever embraced me and all mine with singular affection, and still constantly maintain that same goodwill and zeal towards me. Moreover, I rightly pay you the respect I owe, and I think this is for those outstanding virtues of yours, divinely and generously bestowed upon you: prudence, skill in conducting affairs, learning, eloquence and justice, and, what surpasses all these, love of true and pure religion and a singular zeal for spreading it. I urge you as strongly as I can to persevere in these things, meanwhile beseeching the Lord our God to confirm and increase these gifts in you, to the glory of his name and the safety and well-being of our whole Commonwealth. Farewell. May the Lord deign to bless you and your families, and keep you from every evil. Given at Bern in Helvetia, 5 May, in the year of our salvation 1572.

units.la: Debueras Domini iampridem cedere Verbo Tu, qui Romulea Præsul in vrbe sedes. At quia cœlestis tibi verbi oracula sordent, I, morere, en proprio cæsus ab ense iaces.
units.tr: You ought long ago to have yielded to the Word of the Lord, you prelate who sit in the Romulean city. But since the heavenly oracles of the word are cheap in your eyes, go and die; behold, you lie struck down by your own sword.

units.la: DE DOCTRINA.
units.tr: OF DOCTRINE.

units.la: CAPVT. I.
units.tr: CHAPTER I.

units.la: Non aliud docendum aut sentiendu esse, quàm quod à beato Petro, & reliquis Apostolis traditum est. Marcellus Papa.
units.tr: Nothing other is to be taught or thought than what has been handed down by the blessed Peter and the rest of the Apostles. Pope Marcellus.

units.la: ROGAMUS vos fratres dilectissimi, vt non aliud doceatis, neque sentiatis, quàm quod à beato Petro, & reliquis Apostolis à patribus accepistis.
units.tr: We beseech you, most beloved brethren, that you teach and think nothing other than what you have received from the fathers, handed down by the blessed Peter and the rest of the Apostles.

units.la: Non ex proprio corde docendum, vel ex humano sensu, sed ex scripturis sanctis, & ea quæ Spiritus sanctus docet. Hieronymus.
units.tr: Teaching must not proceed from one's own heart or from human judgment, but from the holy Scriptures and from what the Holy Spirit teaches. Jerome.

units.la: Dist.36. Si quis vult.) Hæc duo sunt Pontificis opera, vt à Deo discat legendo scripturas diuinas, & sæpius meditando, aut populū doceat. Sed illa doceat, quæ à Deo ipse didicerat, non ex proprio corde vel humano sensu sed quæ spiritus sanctus docet. Substantiam sacerdotij esse Sacram Scripturam. Ex VII. Synodo.
units.tr: Dist. 36, "Si quis vult." These two things are the work of the bishop: to learn from God by reading the divine Scriptures and by meditating on them very often, and to teach the people. But he should teach those things which he himself has learned from God, not from his own heart or human judgment, but what the Holy Spirit teaches. That the substance of the priesthood is Holy Scripture. From the Seventh Synod.

units.la: Dist.38. Omnes Psallentes.) Substantia summi sacerdotij nostri, sunt eloquia diuinitus tradita, id est, vera diuinarum scripturarum disciplina, quemadmodum magnus perhibet Dionysius.
units.tr: Dist. 38, "Omnes psallentes." The substance of our supreme priesthood consists in the words divinely handed down, that is, in the true discipline of the divine Scriptures, as the great Dionysius affirms.

units.la: Vide plura eiusmodi infra de examine eorum qui ad sacros ordines admittendi.
units.tr: See more of this kind below, concerning the examination of those who are to be admitted to holy orders.

units.la: DE SACRA SCRIPTVRA. CAPVT II.
units.tr: ON HOLY SCRIPTURE. CHAPTER II.

units.la: De authoritate Scripturae sanctae. Augustinus.
units.tr: On the authority of Holy Scripture. Augustine.

units.la: Dist.9. Ego solis.) Ego solis eis scriptorum (alias scripturarum) libris, qui iam Canonici appellantur, didici hunc timorem honorem referre, (alias deferre) vt nullum eorum scribendo errasse audeam credere, aut si aliquid in eis offendero, quod videatur cotrariu veritati, nihil aliud existime, quam mendosum esse Codicem, vel non assecutum esse interprete, quod dictum est, vel, me minime intellexisse non am bigam. Alios autem ita lego, vt quantalibet sanctitate, quantaue doctrina polleant, non ideo verum putem quia ipsi ita senserunt, sed quia mihi per alios authores, vel Canonicos, vel probabiles rationes, quod à vero nō abhorreat persuadere potuerunt.
units.tr: Dist. 9, Ego solis.) I have learned to show this reverence and respect only to those books of the Scriptures which are now called canonical, so that I dare not believe that any of their writers erred. If I find anything in them that seems to contradict the truth, I conclude either that the manuscript is faulty, or that the translator did not render what was said, or that I have not understood it at all. I read other authors in such a way that, however holy and learned they may be, I do not consider a thing true merely because they held it, but because they have persuaded me, by other authors who are canonical or by probable arguments, that it does not depart from the truth.

units.la: Et Paulo post ibidem. Quis nesciat.) Quis nesciat Sacram Scripturam Canonicam, tam veteris quam noui testamenti, certis terminis suis contineri, eamq; posterioribus omnibus Episcoporum literis ita præponi, vt de illa omnino dubitari & disceptari non possit, vtrum verum vel vtrum rectum sit, quicquid in ea scripturn fit vel constiterit esse : Episcoporum autem literas, quæ post confirmatum Canonem, vel scriptæ sunt, vel scribuntur, & per sermonem forte sapientiorum in ea re cuiuslibet peritioris, & per aliorum Episcoporum grauiorem authoritatem, doctioremq; prudentiam, & per Concilia licere reprehendi, si quid in eis forte à veritate deuiatum est.
units.tr: Shortly after, in the same place, Quis nesciat.) Who does not know that the canonical Holy Scripture, of both the Old and the New Testament, is confined within its fixed limits, and is placed above all the later letters of bishops in such a way that one may not at all doubt or dispute whether whatever is written or shown to be in it is true and right? But the letters of bishops, whether written before or after the canon was settled, may be criticised, if anything in them has perhaps departed from the truth, both by the judgement of wiser men in this matter or of anyone more skilled, and by the weightier authority and more learned prudence of other bishops, and by councils.

units.la: Item ibidem C. Noli frater.) Noli frater contra diuina tam multa, tam præclara, tā indubitata testimonia colligere velle calumnias ex Episcoporum scriptis, siue nostrorum, sicut Hilarij, siue Cypriani, & Agrippini, antequā pars Donati separaretur, primoq; hoc genus literarum, ab authoritate Canonum distinguendum est. Non enim sic legūtur, tanquā ita ex eis testimonium proferatur, vt contra sentire non liceat, sicubi forte aliter sapuerint, quàm veritas postulat. In eo quippe numero sumus, ut non dedignemur, etiam nobis dictum ab Apostolo accipere: Etsi quid aliter sapitis,hoc quoque vobis Deus revelabit.
units.tr: Likewise in the same place, C. Noli frater.) Brother, do not try to gather from the writings of bishops, whether ours, such as Hilary, or Cyprian, or Agrippinus (before the party of Donatus separated), such slanders against so many divine, so distinguished and so undoubted testimonies. This class of writings must first be distinguished from the authority of the canons. For they are not read in such a way that a testimony is drawn from them so that one may not disagree with them, wherever they have perhaps thought otherwise than the truth requires. We are indeed of such a number that we do not disdain to take to ourselves what the Apostle said: "If in anything you think otherwise, God will reveal this also to you."

units.la: Ibidem.C.Noli meis.) Noli meis literis quasi Canonicis scripturis deseruire, sed in illis, & quae non credebas, cum inueneris, incunctanter crede:[?]in istis autem, quod certum nō habe-bas, nisi certu intellexeris, noli firmum tenere.
units.tr: In the same place, C. Noli meis.) Do not submit to my letters as if they were canonical Scriptures; but where you have found things in them that you did not believe, believe them without hesitation. In those things, however, which you did not hold as certain, do not hold them firmly unless you have understood them clearly.

units.la: Scripturam rectè debere intelligi. Hier.
units.tr: That Scripture ought to be rightly understood. Jerome.

units.la: Dist. 37.Vino.) Vino inebriantur, qui scrip-turas sacras male intelligunt atque peruertunt. Sicera, qui abutuntur seculari sapiētia,& diale-cticorum tendiculis. Quae non tam tendicula sunt appellanda quam phantasmata, idest, Umbræ quædam & imagines, quae cito pereunt, & resoluuntur. Idem. Secundum tropologiam Pseudoprophetas eos debemus accipere, qui aliter scripturarum verba accipiunt, quàm Spiritus Sanctus sonat, & diuinos eos, qui conie-ctura mentis suae, incerta futurorum quasi vera pronunciant, absque diuinorum authoritate verborum. Idem. Quicunque scripturas nō ita intelligunt, ut rei veritas habet, vuam acer-bam comedunt.
units.tr: Dist. 37, Vino.) Those who misunderstand and pervert the sacred Scriptures are made drunk with wine. Those who abuse secular wisdom and the snares of the dialecticians are made drunk with strong drink. These are to be called not so much snares as phantoms, that is, certain shadows and images, which quickly perish and dissolve. Idem. According to the tropological sense we ought to understand as false prophets those who take the words of Scripture otherwise than the Holy Spirit sounds them, and as diviners those who, by the conjecture of their own mind, pronounce uncertain future things as if they were true, without the authority of the divine words. Idem. Whoever does not understand the Scriptures as the truth of the matter has them eats a bitter thing.

units.la: Non aliunde, sed ex ipsis scripturis, veri-tatis sensum capiendū esse. Clementis PP.
units.tr: That the sense of the truth must be taken not from elsewhere, but from the Scriptures themselves. Pope Clement.

units.la: Dist.37.C.Relatum.) Lex Dei cùm legitur non secundum propriam ingenij virtutem vel intelligentiam legatur vel doceatur. Sunt enim multa verba in scripturis diuinis, quæ possunt trahi ad eum sensum, quem sibi vnusquisque sponte præsumpserit, sed non oportet. Non e-nim sensum extrinsecus alienum & extraneum debetis quærere, vt quoquo modo ipsū ex scri-pturarum authoritate confirmetis, sed ex ipsis scripturis sensum capere veritatis oportet.
units.tr: Dist. 37, C. Relatum.) When the law of God is read, it should not be read or taught according to one's own natural ability or understanding. For there are many words in the divine Scriptures which can be drawn to whatever sense each person has presumed of his own accord, but this should not be done. For you ought not to seek a sense foreign and alien from outside, so that you may somehow confirm it by the authority of the Scriptures, but it is necessary to take the sense of the truth from the Scriptures themselves.

units.la: Scripturarum sensum ex linguis ori-ginalibus eruendum.
units.tr: That the sense of the Scriptures must be drawn out from the original languages.

units.la: Dist.9.C.) Vt veterum librorū fides de He-bræis voluminibus examinanda est, ita nouo-rū veritas, Græci sermonis normam desiderat.
units.tr: Dist. 9, C.) Just as the faith of the old books must be examined by the Hebrew volumes, so the truth of the new books requires the standard of the Greek language.

units.la: Dist.19.C.)De quibus causis nulla soluendi ligandiq; authoritas, in libris veteris & noui Testamenti, & quatuor euangeliorum cum totis scriptis Apostolorum non appareat, ad diui-na recurrite scripta Græca.
units.tr: Dist. 19, C.) For which reasons no authority for loosing and binding appears in the books of the Old and New Testament, or in the four Gospels together with all the writings of the Apostles, return to the divine writings in Greek.

units.la: DE PATRIBVS EORVMQVE scriptis. Augusti. CAPVT. III.
units.tr: On the Fathers and their writings. Augustine. Chapter III.

units.la: Dist.9.C.Negare.) Negare non possum nec debeo, sicut in ipsis maioribus, ita multa esse in tam multis opusculis meis, quæ possunt iusto iudicio, & nulla temeritate culpari.
units.tr: Dist.9.C.Negare.) I cannot and ought not deny that, just as in the greatest men, so in my own many small works there are many things that may rightly be found fault with by sound judgment, and not by rashness.

units.la: Neque quorūlibet.) Neq; quorū libet disputationes,quáuis Catholicorū & laudatorū hominū veluti scripturas Canonicas habere debemus,vt nobis non liceat salua honorificentia,quæ illis debetur hominibus,aliquid in eorū scriptis improbare atque respuere, si fortè inuenìremus quòd aliter senserint, quàm veritas habet,diuino adiutorio vel ab alijs intellecta vel à nobis. Talis ego sum in scriptis aliorum,quales volo esse intellectores meorum.
units.tr: Neque quorūlibet.) Nor ought we to treat the disputations of any men whatsoever, even Catholic and praised men, as if they were canonical Scripture, so that we may not, while preserving the honour owed to those men, disapprove of and reject something in their writings, if perhaps we find that they thought otherwise than the truth is, whether it has been understood by others or by us with divine help. I am such in the writings of others as I want my readers to be with mine.

units.la: De scriptis incertis, quomodo legenda sunt.
units.tr: On uncertain writings, and how they are to be read.

units.la: Santa Romana.) Scripta de inuentione sanctæ Crucis Dominicæ, & alia scripta de inuentione capitis beati Ioannis Baptistæ, nouellæ quidem reuelationes sunt,& nonnulli eas Catholici legunt, sed cum hæc ad Catholicorum manus peruenerint, beati Pauli Apostoli sententia præcedat: Omnia probate,quod bonum est, tenete.
units.tr: Santa Romana.) The writings on the finding of the holy Cross of the Lord, and other writings on the finding of the head of blessed John the Baptist, are indeed novel revelations, and some Catholics read them. But when these come into Catholic hands, the saying of the blessed Apostle Paul must go first: Prove all things; hold fast what is good.

units.la: De Canonibus Apostolorum.
units.tr: On the Canons of the Apostles.

units.la: ) Apostolorū Canones, qui per Clementem Pontificem Romanum,sicut quidam afferunt ,dicūtur esse translati, sunt quinquaginta. Hos non recipiendos, sed inter Apocrypha deputatos Isidorus scribit dicens: Canones qui dicuntur Apostolorum, seu quia eos dem nec sedes Apostolica recepit,nec sanǝti pa tres illis assensum præbueruit, pro eo quod ab hæreticis sub nomine Apostolorum compositi dignoscuntur , quamuis in eis vtilia inuenian- tur,tamen ab authoritate Canonica atque Apo stolica eorum gesta constat esse remota, atque inter Apocrypha deputata.
units.tr: ) The Canons of the Apostles, which are said by some to have been translated through Clement, the Roman Pontiff, are fifty. Isidore writes that these are not to be received but are counted among the Apocrypha, saying: "The canons which are called the Apostles'" are not received by the apostolic see, nor have the holy Fathers given them assent, because they are recognised as having been composed by heretics under the name of the Apostles. Although useful things are found in them, it is nevertheless clear that their contents are remote from canonical and apostolic authority, and they are counted among the Apocrypha.

units.la: Zepherinus Papa,mox 60. ex eis sententias recipiendas dicit, Leo,omnes, exceptis quin- quaginta.
units.tr: Pope Zephyrinus says that soon sixty of them are to be received; Leo says all of them, except the fifty.

units.la: Dist. 32. C. Præter.) dicitur,quôd Canoni- bus Apostolorum Orientalis, & ex parte tan- tum Romana vtatur ecclesia.
units.tr: Dist. 32. C. Præter.) It is said that the Eastern church uses the Canons of the Apostles, and the Roman church only in part.

units.la: DE CONCILIIS.
units.tr: DE CONCILIIS.

units.la: CAPVT IIII.
units.tr: CAPVT IIII.

units.la: Concilia quædam in ipsis Decretis dam- nata.
units.tr: Certain councils condemned in the Decrees themselves.

units.la: Dist.15.C. Sancta Romana.)Imprimis Ari- minensem synodum à Constätino Cæsare Co stantini filio congregatam, mediante Tauro præfecto,ex tunc & in æternum confitemur es se damnatam.
units.tr: Dist.15.C. Sancta Romana.) First of all, we confess that the synod of Ariminum, gathered by Constantius Caesar, son of Constantine, through the agency of the prefect Taurus, has been condemned from then on and for ever.

units.la: Concilia quomodo Concilianda. Isidori.
units.tr: How councils are to be judged. Of Isidore.

units.la: Dist.50.) Domino sancto.) Quotiescunq; in gestis Conciliorum discors sententia inuenitur; illius concilij sententia magis teneatur; cuius antiquior & potior existit authoritas.
units.tr: Dist.50.) Domino sancto.) Whenever a conflicting opinion is found in the acts of councils, the opinion of that council is to be held which has the older and greater authority.

units.la: Iudices qui debeant esse. Ex Cocilio Niceno.
units.tr: Who ought to be judges. From the Council of Nicaea.

units.la: 11.q.1.C.Iudices.) Iudices autem esse non debent,nisi quos qui impetitur, elegerit.
units.tr: 11.q.1.C.Iudices.) Judges, moreover, ought not to be anyone except those whom the person being attacked has chosen.

units.la: Neminem simul accusatorem & iudicem esse posse.
units.tr: That no one can be both accuser and judge.

units.la: 4.q.4.C.) Nullus unquam præsumat accusator simul esse & iudex, vel testis, quoniā in om-ni iudicio, quatuor personas semper necesse est esse; id est iudices electos, accusatores idoneos defensores congruos, atq; testes legitimos. Iudices autem debent uti æquitate, testes veritate; accusatores intentione ad amplificandam cau-sam, defensores extenuatione ad minuendam causam.
units.tr: 4.q.4.C.) Let no one ever presume to be accuser and judge at once, or witness as well, since in every trial four persons must always be present: namely, chosen judges, suitable accusers, fitting defenders, and lawful witnesses. Judges ought to use equity, witnesses truth, accusers intention to magnify the case, and defenders extenuation to diminish it.

units.la: Et mox C. sequente. Accusatores & accusa-ti, æqua audiantur ratione iuxta quod ordo exi-git. Accusatores vero & iudices non iidē sint; sed per se accusatores, per se iudices, per se te-stes, per se accusati, unusquisq; in suo ordine.
units.tr: And soon after, in the following chapter: Accusers and the accused are to be heard on equal terms, as the order requires. Accusers and judges are not to be the same persons; accusers are to be accusers by themselves, judges by themselves, witnesses by themselves, the accused by themselves, each in his own rank.

units.la: Quód qui inimici sunt, iudices esse non possint. Nicolai Papæ.
units.tr: That those who are enemies cannot be judges. Of Pope Nicholas.

units.la: Quod suspecti. Quòd suspecti & inimici iudices esse nó debeát, & ipsa ratio dictat, & plurimis probatur exemplis. Nam quid gratius & amabilius dare quis inimico poterit, quâ si ei ad impetendum commiserit, quem laedere forte voluerit? Quod prouidè Constantinopolitana Synodus Canonum suorum sex-to dinoscitur prohibere Capitulo. Veniamus & ad sanctá Chalcedonensem Synodû, & quid nobis de ipso Anastasio Pelenonum referat Episcopo, audiamus. Is enim antistes tertio euocatus quia non occurrit, à suo Patriarcha Canonicè codemnatus extiterat, sed solù, quia cum vocaretur ad synodum, quòd inimicus esset eius ipse qui iudicabat, clamauit, à sancta Chalcedonense Synodo ad causas illatas sibi examinandas reseruatur, & nisi denuo conuinceretur, recipere propriam iudicatur ecclesiam. Si Anastasius à Patriarcha suo depositus, quia de inimicitia eius conquestus est, iteratò ad iudicium reuocandû dirigitur, & si manifesta sibi officiant crimina, tamen suæ ecclesiæ reddi præcipitur, quanto magis Ignatius, qui non à Patriarcha, sed potius ipse existens Patriarcha, minime debuit ecclesia propria priuari, & inimicis & suspectis iudicibus decernentibus expoliari[?] Veniat & facundissimus noster pater Papa Gelasius, hæreticorum expugnator fortissimus,& quid de Constantinopolitanis Episcopis (more solito) tunc ægrotantibus dixit, etiā tunc nobis edisserat. Quæro inquit iudicium quod prætendunt, vbi nam possit agitari, an apud ipsos (qui) ijdē inimici sint, & TESTES, & REI, & IVDICES? Sed tali iudicio nec humana debent committi negotia. Quod si in iudicio, vbi ijdē sunt inimici qui iudices, nec humana committi debent iudicia, quanto minus diuina, id est, ecclesiastica[?] qui sapiens est, intelligat.
units.tr: That suspect persons and enemies ought not to be judges is dictated by reason itself and is proved by very many examples. For what gift could anyone give to an enemy more welcome and more pleasing than to commit to him the task of attacking the man he perhaps wishes to harm? The Synod of Constantinople wisely forbids this in the sixth of its canons. Let us also come to the holy Synod of Chalcedon, and let us hear what it tells us about Anastasius, bishop of Pelenonum. This prelate, summoned a third time, did not appear, and so he was canonically condemned by his own patriarch. But because, when he was called to the synod, he cried out that the very man who was judging him was his enemy, he was reserved by the holy Synod of Chalcedon for the examination of the charges brought against him, and it was ruled that unless he was convicted again, he should recover his own church. If Anastasius, deposed by his patriarch because he complained of the patriarch's enmity, is nonetheless ordered to be called back again to judgment, and if the crimes against him are manifest yet he is commanded to be restored to his own church, how much more should Ignatius, who was not deposed by a patriarch but was himself a patriarch, not have been deprived of his own church, and not have been stripped of it at the decision of enemy and suspect judges? Let our most eloquent father, Pope Gelasius, the most valiant conqueror of heretics, also come forward; let him explain to us what he said, as is his custom, about the bishops of Constantinople who were then sick. "I ask," he says, "the trial they demand, where can it be conducted? Among those who are themselves enemies, and at once witnesses, defendants and judges? Yet human affairs ought not to be entrusted to such a trial. If in a trial where the enemies are the judges human judgments ought not to be committed, how much less divine, that is ecclesiastical, judgments?" Let him who is wise understand this.

units.la: Et reuera hinc Iustinianus Imperator pius legibus suis promulgasse dinoscitur; dicens, liceat ei, quoniā suspectum sibi iudicē putat, antequā lis inchoetur, eum recusare, ut ad alium recur-ratur. Nā quodámodo naturale est, suspectorū iudicum insidias declinare, & inimicorum iudicium velle refugere. Hinc sanctus Ioannes Os aureum, Concilij contra se congregati renuit intrare collegium. Patet ergo, quòd etsi manifesta sunt crimina alicuius, tamen accusatione inimici condemnandus non est.
units.tr: And indeed, the pious Emperor Justinian is known to have promulgated this in his laws, saying: let it be permitted to one who thinks a judge suspect to him, before the suit is begun, to reject him, so that the case may be referred to another. For it is in some measure natural to avoid the snares of suspect judges and to wish to escape the judgment of enemies. Hence holy John Chrysostom refused to enter the council gathered against him. It is clear, therefore, that even if someone's crimes are manifest, he is not to be condemned on the accusation of an enemy.

units.la: Nuper inimicos, accusatores vel te-stes esse non posse. Anacletus Papa.
units.tr: That recent enemies cannot be accusers or witnesses. Pope Anacletus.

units.la: Ibidem. C. Accusatores.) Accusatores & testes esse nō possunt, qui ante hesternum diē aut nudius tertius inimici fuerunt, ne irati nocere cupiant, ne læsi se vlcisci velint. Inoffensus igitur accusatorū & testium affectus quærendus est, & non suspectus.
units.tr: Ibid. C. Accusers.) Those who were enemies until yesterday or the day before cannot be accusers or witnesses, lest in anger they wish to do harm, or, having been injured, wish to take revenge. Therefore a disposition of accusers and witnesses that is free from offence must be sought, and one that is not suspect.

units.la: In absentes sententiam non ferendam.
units.tr: That sentence is not to be passed against absent persons.

units.la: 3.q.9.C.) Caueant iudices ecclesiæ,ne absen[?] te eo cuius causa ventilatur, sententiam prose-rant,quia irrita erit.&c.
units.tr: 3.q.9.C.) Church judges should take care not to pronounce sentence in the absence of him whose cause is being heard, because it will be void, etc.

units.la: Et mox ibidem.C.Omnia quæ aduersus ab-sentes in omni negotio aut loco arguuntur aut iudicantur,euacuentur omnino, quoniam ab-sentem nullus addicit, nec vlla lex damnat.
units.tr: And soon after, in the same place, C.: All that is argued or judged against absent persons in any matter or place is to be wholly annulled, since no one adjudges an absent man, and no law condemns him.

units.la: Item.C.Non oportet quemlibet iudicari vel damnari ,priusquam legitimos habeat presen-tes accusatores , locúmq; defendendi accipiat ad abluenda crimina.
units.tr: Likewise, C.: It is not right for anyone to be judged or condemned before he has lawful accusers present and is given a place to defend himself and wipe away the charges.

units.la: Item. C. Absente aduersario, non audiatur accusator,nec absente alia parte, sententia à iudice dicta , nullam obtineat firmitatem
units.tr: Likewise, C.: If the opponent is absent, the accuser is not to be heard; and if the other party is absent, a sentence pronounced by a judge shall have no force.

units.la: Item.C.Necesse est secundum sacrarum scrip-turarum documentum,ac secundum iustitiæ tramitem, & accusatum & accusatorem simul adesse,& vnam partè quantacúmque & quali-cunq; prædita sit authoritate, sic prorsus audi-ri , vt alteri parti nullum præiudicium irroge-tur.
units.tr: Likewise, C.: According to the teaching of the holy Scriptures and the path of justice, it is necessary that both the accused and the accuser be present together, and that one party, however great and of whatever quality its authority, be heard in such a way that no prejudice is done to the other party.

units.la: DE SYNODIS BIS IN ANNO celebrandis. CAPVT V.
units.tr: Concerning synods to be held twice a year. Chapter 5.

units.la: Dist.18.C. De Concilijs. ) Sancti patres salu-briter ordinauerunt, vt scilicet bini conuentus per annos singulos habeantur,in quibus de omnibus querelis, quæ inter diuersos ecclesiæ ordines nasci assolent iudicetur.
units.tr: Dist. 18, c. De Concilijs. The holy Fathers wisely ordained that two assemblies be held each year, in which all disputes that commonly arise among the different orders of the Church are to be judged.

units.la: Ité. C.Propter ecclesiasticas.Sufficere nobis visum est, bis in anno per singulas provincias Episcoporum Concilium fieri.
units.tr: Again, c. Propter ecclesiasticas. It seemed sufficient to us that a council of the bishops be held twice a year in each province.

units.la: Item C. Pervenit .Statuit hæc ergo sancta Synodus,secundum regulas patrum, bis in anno in unum convenire per singulas provintias Episcopos, ubi singula quæ emerserint,corrigantur.
units.tr: Again, c. Pervenit. This holy synod therefore decrees, according to the rules of the Fathers, that the bishops of each province come together twice a year, where whatever matters have arisen may be corrected.

units.la: DE CONSTITUTIONIBUS humanis. CAPUT VI.
units.tr: ON HUMAN CONSTITUTIONS. CHAPTER VI.

units.la: Quòd stare non possit,quod contra Euangelicam vel Propheticam doctrinam fa-ctum fuerit.
units.tr: That what has been done contrary to the Evangelical or Prophetic doctrine cannot stand.

units.la: 25.q.1.C.Omne quod.) Rubrica habet.Stare non valet quod contra Euangelicam vel Propheticam doctrinam seu constitutionem factū fuerit.
units.tr: 25.q.1.C.Omne quod.) The rubric reads: What has been done contrary to the Evangelical or Prophetic doctrine or constitution cannot stand.

units.la: Pseudoprophetas & divinos esse,qui aliquid tanquam verum pronuntiant, absque divinorum authoritate Verborum. Dist.37. C. Vino.) Secundum tropologiam pseudoprophetas eos debemus accipere, qui aliter scripturarum verba accipiunt, quam Spiritus Sanctus sonat, & diuinos eos,qui coiectu ra mentis suae incerta futurorum quasi vera pronuntiant, abfq; diuinorum auctoritate verborum.
units.tr: Pseudoprophets and diviners are those who pronounce something as true without the authority of divine words. Dist.37. C. Vino.) In a tropological sense we should understand as pseudoprophets those who take the words of Scripture otherwise than the Holy Spirit sounds them, and as diviners those who, by the conjecture of their own mind, pronounce uncertain future things as if they were true, without the authority of divine words.

units.la: Papam non posse condere leges contra disertam Christi & Apostolorum doctrinam. Vrbani Papae.
units.tr: That the Pope cannot make laws contrary to the express doctrine of Christ and the Apostles. Of Pope Urban.

units.la: 25.q.1.C.Sunt quidâ.) Vbi vero aperte Dominus vel eius Apostoli & eos sequentes sancti patres, sententialiter aliquid diffinierunt, ibi non nouam legê Romanus Pontifex dare, sed potius quod praedicatum est vsque ad animam & sanguinem confirmare debet. Si enim quod docuerunt Apostoli & prophetae destruere (quod absit) niteretur, non sententiam dare, sed magis errare conuinceretur.
units.tr: 25.q.1.C.Sunt quidâ.) But where the Lord or his Apostles, and the holy Fathers who followed them, have clearly defined something by settled judgment, there the Roman Pontiff ought not to give a new law, but rather to confirm what has been preached even unto life and blood. For if he should strive to destroy (which God forbid) what the Apostles and prophets taught, he would not be giving a judgment, but would be proved to be in error.

units.la: Papam contra statuta patrum nihil codere posse. Zosimi Papae.
units.tr: That the Pope can enact nothing against the statutes of the Fathers. Of Pope Zosimus.

units.la: 25.q.C.Contra.) Contra statuta patrum constituere aliquid vel mutare, nec huius quidem sedis potest authoritas.
units.tr: 25.q.C.Contra.) Not even the authority of this see can establish or change anything against the statutes of the Fathers.

units.la: Decretales non debere aliquid Euangelicis praeceptis contrarium habere.
units.tr: Decretals ought not to contain anything contrary to the evangelical precepts.

units.la: Dist.19.) Postquam multis Capitibus & authoritatibus Patrum Gratianus ostendit, Decretales [?]retales Romanæ sedis epistolas ab omnibus suscipiendas esse, tandem C.Ita Dominus, subiungit: Hoc autem intelligendū est, de illis sanctionibus vel decretalibus Epistolis, in quibus nec præcedentium patrum decretis, NEC EVANGELICIS PRAECEPTIS ALI-QVID CONTRARIVM INVENI-TVR.
units.tr: Dist.19.) After Gratian has shown, by many chapters and the authorities of the Fathers, that the decretal letters of the Roman see are to be received by all, he finally adds, in C. Ita Dominus: This, however, must be understood of those decrees or decretal letters in which NOTHING CONTRARY EITHER TO THE DECREES OF THE PRECEDING FATHERS NOR TO THE EVANGELICAL PRECEPTS IS FOUND.

units.la: Non prohibendum quod scriptura non prohibet.
units.tr: What Scripture does not forbid must not be forbidden.

units.la: 27.q.2. C. Lex diuina.) Nam cur prohibeatur, quod prohibendum nunquam sancta scriptura declarat?
units.tr: 27.q.2. C. Lex diuina.) For why should that be forbidden which holy Scripture never declares to be forbidden?

units.la: De onere constitutionum humanarum. Augusti.
units.tr: On the burden of human constitutions. Of Augustine.

units.la: Dist.12.C.Omnia.) Ipsam religionem, quam in paucissimis, & manifestissimis celebrationū sacramentis misericordia Dei voluit esse liberam, seruilibus oneribus premunt, adeò vt tolerabilior fit conditio Iudæorum, qui etiam tempus libertatis non cognouerunt, legalibus tamen sacramentis, non humanis præsumptionibus subijciuntur.
units.tr: Dist.12.C.Omnia.) They weigh down with servile burdens the very religion which the mercy of God willed to be free, in the very few and most plain celebrations of the sacraments, so that the condition of the Jews is more tolerable: they have not known even a time of liberty, yet they are subjected to legal sacraments, not to human presumptions.

units.la: Constitutiones excludendæ.
units.tr: Constitutions to be excluded.

units.la: Dist. 9. C. Sacra.) Constitutiones ergo vel ecclesiasticæ vel sæculares, si naturali iure contrariæ probantur, penitus sunt excludendæ.
units.tr: Dist. 9. C. Sacra.) Therefore constitutions, whether ecclesiastical or secular, if they are proved contrary to natural law, must be utterly excluded.

units.la: SENTENTIAE DE CONSVETVDInibus. CAPVT VII.
units.tr: SENTENTIAE DE CONSUETUDINIBUS. CAPUT VII.

units.la: Veritati consuetudo cedat.
units.tr: Let custom yield to truth.

units.la: Dist. 8. C. Veritate.) Veritate manifestata cedat consuetudo veritati. Plane quis dubitet veritati, manifeste consuetudinem cedere? Item nemo consuetudinem rationi & veritati praeponat, quia consuetudinem ratio & veritas semper excludit.
units.tr: Dist. 8, C. Veritate.) When the truth has been made manifest, custom must yield to truth. Who could doubt that custom plainly gives way to truth? Likewise, no one should put custom before reason and truth, because reason and truth always exclude custom.

units.la: Item. C. Si.) Si consuetudinem fortasis opponas, aduertendum est, quod Dominus dicit, Ego sum via, Veritas, & vita. Non dixit, Ego sum consuetudo, sed Veritas. Et certe ut beati Cypriani vtamur sententia, quaelibet consuetudo quantumuis vetusta, quantumuis vulgata, veritati omnino est postponenda, & VSVS QVI VERITATI EST CONTRARIVS, EST ABOLENDVS.
units.tr: Likewise, C. Si.) If you should perhaps set custom against us, it must be noted that the Lord says, "I am the way, the truth, and the life" (John 14). He did not say, "I am custom," but "truth." And certainly, to use the opinion of the blessed Cyprian, whatever custom, however ancient and however widespread, must wholly be set after the truth, and "every custom that is contrary to the truth is to be abolished."

units.la: Item. C. Mala autem consuetudo no minus quam perniciosa corruptela abijcienda & vitada est, quae nisi citius radicitus euellatur, in priuilegiorum ius ab impijs assumitur, & incipiunt praeuaricationes, & variae praesumptiones celerrime non compressae pro legibus venerari, & priuilegiorum more perpetuo celebrari.
units.tr: Likewise, C. Mala autem consuetudo: an evil custom, no less than a harmful corruption, must be cast off and avoided. Unless it is quickly torn up by the roots, it is taken up by the impious as a right of privileges, and transgressions begin, and various presumptions, not quickly suppressed, are soon revered as laws and celebrated perpetually as privileges.

units.la: Item. C. Qui contempta.) Reuelatione igitur facta veritatis, veritati cedat consuetudo, quia & Petrus qui circumcidebat, cesit Paulo veritatem prædicanti. Igitur cum Christus veritas sit, magis veritatem quàm consuetudinem sequi debemus, quia consuetudinem ratio & veritas semper excludit.
units.tr: Likewise, C. Qui contempta.) Therefore, once the truth has been revealed, custom must yield to truth, because Peter also, who was circumcising, yielded to Paul preaching the truth. Therefore, since Christ is the truth, we ought to follow the truth rather than custom, because reason and truth always exclude custom.

units.la: Item. C. Frustra quidam qui ratione conuincuntur, consuetudinem nobis obijciunt, quasi consuetudo maior sit veritate.
units.tr: Likewise, C. Those who are refuted by reason in vain throw custom at us, as if custom were greater than truth.

units.la: Item. C. Consuetudo, quæ apud quosdam irrepserat, impedire non debet, quo minus præualeat veritas & vincat. Nam CONSVETVDO SINE VERITATE, VETVSTAS ERRORIS EST, propter quod relicto errore sequamur veritatem.
units.tr: Likewise, C. A custom which had crept in among certain people ought not to hinder truth from prevailing and conquering. For "custom without truth is the antiquity of error," on account of which, leaving error aside, let us follow the truth.

units.la: Item. C. Si solus Christus audiendus est, non debemus attendere, quid aliquis ante nos faciendum putauerit, sed quid prius, qui ante omnes est Christus prior fuerit. Neque enim huius consuetudinem sequi oportet, sed Dei veritatem, cum per Esaiam prophetam loquatur & dicat, Sine causa colunt me, mandata & doctrinas hominum docentes.
units.tr: Likewise, C. If Christ alone is to be heard, we ought not to attend to what someone before us thought should be done, but to what Christ, who is before all, has said first. For we must not follow his custom but the truth of God, since he speaks through the prophet Isaiah and says, "In vain do they worship me, teaching the commandments and doctrines of men."

units.la: Dist. 11. C. Consuetudinem laudamus, quæ tamen contra fidem Catholicam nihil vsurpare dignoscitur.
units.tr: Dist. 11, C. We praise custom, which is nevertheless recognized as claiming nothing against the Catholic faith.

units.la: CAPVT IIII.
units.tr: CHAPTER IV.

units.la: Dist.63.C.Quia.) Gratianus ait: Si nonnulli ex praedecessoribus & maioribus nostris fecerunt aliqua, quae illo tempore potuerunt esse sine culpa, & postea vertuntur in errorem & superstitionem, sine tarditate aliqua, & cum magna authoritate à posteris destruantur. Adducit etiam exemplum Ezechiae regis, qui confregit serpentem aeneum à Mose erectum cum populus illum venerari coepisset.
units.tr: Dist. 63, C. Quia.) Gratian says: If some of our predecessors and elders did certain things which at that time could have been without fault, and afterwards they turn into error and superstition, these must be destroyed without any delay, and with great authority, by their successors. He also adduces the example of King Hezekiah, who broke in pieces the bronze serpent erected by Moses when the people had begun to worship it.

units.la: 35.q.9.C. Quod quis.) Rubrica habet: corrigendum est, quod illicitè admittitur, aut à praedecessoribus admissum inuenitur. Et sequitur: Quod quis commisit illicitè, aut à praedecessoribus suis inuenerit admissum, si propriū periculum vult vitare, damnabit.
units.tr: 35 q. 9, C. Quod quis.) The rubric reads: What has been admitted unlawfully, or is found to have been admitted by predecessors, must be corrected. And it continues: Whoever has committed something unlawfully, or has found it admitted by his predecessors, shall condemn it, if he wishes to avoid his own peril.

units.la: Sententiam Romanae sedis in melius mutare licere:
units.tr: That the sentence of the Roman see may be changed for the better:

units.la: Sic sonat Rubrica 35.q.9.C.) Sententiam Romanae sedis non negamus posse in melius commutari.
units.tr: Thus the rubric of 35 q. 9, C., sounds: We do not deny that the sentence of the Roman see can be changed for the better.

units.la: Altaria in quibus non certae sanctorū reliquiae sint, euertenda esse.
units.tr: That altars under which there are no certain relics of saints are to be overthrown.

units.la: De Consecrat. Dist. 1. Placuit.) Ex Concilio Aphricano. Placuit vt altaria quæ passim per agros & per villas, tanquam memoriæ martyrum constituuntur, in quibus nullum corpus, aut reliquiæ martyris conditæ probantur, ab Episcopis, qui ijsdem locis præsunt, si fieri potest, euertantur. Si autem hoc propter tumultus populares non sinitur, plebes admoneantur, ne illa loca frequentent, vt qui recte sapiût, nulla ibi superstitione deuincti teneâtur. Et ideo nulla memoria martyrum probabiliter accipiatur, nisi aut vbi corpus, & reliquiæ certæ sunt, aut vbi origo alicuius habitationis vel possessionis, vel passionis fidelissima origine tradi-tur. Nam quæ per somnia, aut per inanes quasi reuelationes quorumlibet hominum, vbi-cunque constituuntur altaria, omnino reprobantur.
units.tr: De Consecratione, Dist. 1, Placuit.) From the Council of Africa. It has been resolved that altars which are set up everywhere in the fields and villages, as memorials of martyrs, and under which no body or relics of a martyr are proved to be laid, shall be overthrown by the bishops who preside over those places, if this can be done. But if this is not permitted because of popular disturbances, the people are to be warned not to frequent those places, so that those who think rightly may not be held bound by any superstition there. And therefore no memorial of martyrs is to be accepted as genuine, unless either where the body and relics are certain, or where the origin of some dwelling or possession, or of a martyrdom, is handed down with most faithful testimony. For altars set up wherever on account of dreams, or empty so-called revelations of any men, are altogether to be rejected.

units.la: DE GRATIA, REMISSIONE peccatorum, & sola fide iustificante.
units.tr: On grace, the remission of sins, and justification by faith alone.

units.la: CAPVT IX.
units.tr: CHAPTER IX.

units.la: Gratiam nō esse, quæ gratis datur vel accipitur.
units.tr: That grace is not grace if it is given or received for nothing.

units.la: 1. q. 1. Gratia.) Leo Papa. Gratia, si non gratis datur, vel accipitur, gratia non est.
units.tr: 1. q. 1. Grace.) Pope Leo. If grace is not given or received freely, it is not grace.

units.la: Contra venditores gratiæ. Bedæ.
units.tr: Against the sellers of grace. Bede.

units.la: 1.q. 3. Non solùm.) Non solùm venditores sunt columbarum, & domum Dei faciunt domum negotiationis, qui sacros ordines largiendo, pretium pecuniæ vel laudis, vel etiam honoris inquirunt: Verum hi quoq; qui gradum vel gratiam in ecclesiam spiritualem, quam Domino largiente perceperunt, non simplici intentione, sed cuiuslibet humanæ causa retributionis exercent, &c.
units.tr: 1. q. 3. Not only.) Not only are they sellers of doves, and do they make the house of God a house of trade, who, bestowing holy orders, seek the price of money or of praise, or even of honour; but also those who exercise the rank or grace in the spiritual Church, which they have received by the Lord's gift, not with a simple intention but for the sake of some human reward, etc.

units.la: Graviter peccare eum qui Dominica debita sine pœnitentia dimittat.
units.tr: That he sins gravely who remits the Lord's debts without repentance.

units.la: 23.q.4. Si quis,) Si is qui prælatus est debitori Dominico culpas impunè dimittit, non mediocriter profecto offendit, qui debita cœlestis regis & Domini, sua præsumptione resoluit[?]. Ea namque quæ in nos committuntur, facilè possumus dimittere, ea verò quæ in Deum commissa sunt, cum magna discretione, nec sine pœnitentia possumus relaxare.
units.tr: 23. q. 4. If anyone,) If a man set over a debtor of the Lord remits faults with impunity, he surely offends no little, since by his own presumption he dissolves the debts owed to the heavenly King and Lord. For the wrongs committed against us we can easily forgive, but the things committed against God we cannot relax with great discretion, nor without repentance.

units.la: Indulgentiam sine pœnitentia præstare peccatis, non esse curare sed occidere. Cleri Romani ad Cyprianum.
units.tr: To grant indulgence to sins without repentance is not to heal but to kill. The Roman clergy to Cyprian.

units.la: Dist.50.C. Absit) Absit à Romana ecclesia, vigorem suum tam prophana facilitate dimit-tere, & neruos seueritatis (euersa fidei maiesta-te) te) dissoluere, vt cum adhuc non tantùm iace-ant in peccatis,sed etiam cadant,euersorum fra-trum ruinæ properata nimis remedia communicationum,vtique non profutura præstentur. Vbi enim poterit pœnitentiæ medicina procedere,si etiam ipse medicus intercepta pœnitentia indulget periculis? Hoc est non curare, sed si verum dicere volumus,occidere est.
units.tr: Dist. 50. C. Absit) Far be it from the Roman Church to relax its vigour with such profane ease and to dissolve the sinews of severity (the majesty of the faith being overthrown), so that, while they still lie not only in sins but even fall, hasty remedies of communion for the ruin of fallen brothers are offered, which assuredly will not profit. For where can the medicine of repentance take effect, if the physician himself, with repentance cut off, indulges the dangers? This is not to heal, but, if we wish to speak the truth, it is to kill.

units.la: Impœnitentibus veniam concedi non posse.
units.tr: That pardon cannot be granted to the impenitent.

units.la: Dist. 50. C. Si quis. Si quis præposter a festinatione temerarius remissionem peccatorum cunctis putat se dare posse, aut audet Domini præcepta rescindere, non tantùm nihil prodest,sed obest lapsis. Prouocasse enim iram Dei est,non seruasse sententiam,nec misericordiam piissimi Domini deprecari, sed contempto Domino de sua facilitate præsumere.
units.tr: Dist. 50. C. Si quis. If anyone, rash from a headlong and preposterous haste, thinks he can give the remission of sins to all, or dares to annul the Lord's precepts, he not only does no good but does harm to the fallen. For it is to provoke the wrath of God, not to keep his sentence, nor to implore the mercy of the most merciful Lord, but to presume upon his facility while despising the Lord.

units.la: Non meritis hominum, sed virtute Spiritus sancti & à Spiritu sancto peccata dimittit. Augustin. in Serm. de remiss. peccat.
units.tr: That sins are forgiven not by the merits of men, but by the power of the Holy Spirit and by the Holy Spirit. Augustine, in the sermon on the remission of sins.

units.la: 1 q. 1. Vt euidenter. Vt euidenter ostendaret Dominus à Spiritu sancto quem donauit fidelibus suis, dimitti peccata, non meritis hominum, quodam loco sic ait, Accipite Spiritum sanctum, & continuo subiecit, Si cui dimiseritis peccata, remittuntur ei, hoc est, Spi-ritus sanctus, dimittit, non nos.
units.tr: 1 q. 1. That clearly. That the Lord might clearly show that sins are forgiven by the Holy Spirit, whom he gave to his faithful, and not by the merits of men, he says in a certain place: Receive the Holy Spirit; and immediately adds: Whosoever sins you remit, they are remitted to him. That is, the Holy Spirit forgives, not we.

units.la: Solùm Christum dimittere peccata.
units.tr: That Christ alone forgives sins.

units.la: Sic habet Rubrica.
units.tr: Thus the rubric has it.

units.la: De Consecrat. Dist.4. Nemo.) Nemo tollit peccata mundi, nisi solus Christus, qui est agnus tollens peccata mundi. Tollit autem & dimittendo quæ facta sunt, ubi & originale continetur, & adiuvando ne fiant, & perducendo ad vitam, ubi fieri omnino non possunt.
units.tr: De Consecrat. Dist. 4. No one.) No one takes away the sins of the world except Christ alone, who is the Lamb taking away the sins of the world. He takes them away, moreover, by forgiving what has been done, in which original sin is also contained, and by helping that they may not be done, and by leading to life, where they cannot be done at all.

units.la: Pœnam & culpam per Christum sub-latam esse.
units.tr: That punishment and guilt were taken away through Christ.

units.la: De Confecr. Dist.4. Filius Dei.) Filius Dei carnem peccati suscepit, & pœnam sine culpa, ut in carne peccati & culpa solueretur & pœ-na.
units.tr: De Consecr. Dist. 4. The Son of God.) The Son of God took on the flesh of sin, and punishment without guilt, so that in the flesh of sin both guilt and punishment might be dissolved.

units.la: Solam fidem habere veniæ promis-sionem, & sola fide peccata relaxari.
units.tr: That faith alone holds the promise of pardon, and that sins are relaxed by faith alone.

units.la: De Pœnitent. Dist.2. Charitas est qua.) Inter alia ex Augustino. Quod si charitas à fide Christianorum seiungi nequit, cui scilicet SO-LA VENIA promittitur, quomodo qui charitatem non habuerit, fidem Christianorum habuit, id est, in Christum credidit[?]
units.tr: De Poenit. Dist. 2. Charity is that which.) Among other things from Augustine: If charity cannot be separated from the faith of Christians, to which pardon alone is promised, how does one who has not had charity have the faith of Christians, that is, believed in Christ?

units.la: Et mox. Hoc est enim manducare panem vivum, quod credere in Christum, id est, amando tendo tendere in ipsum. Cum ergo reprobrus in eum non credit, quem non manducavit, & ita fidem Christianorum (QUA SOLA PEC-CATA RELAXANTUR) non habuit, quomodo, si vivit Dominus, cui omne judicium dedit pater, judicium perpetuae damnationis effugiet?
units.tr: And soon after: For this is to eat the living bread, which is to believe in Christ, that is, to strive toward him by loving him. Therefore, when the reprobate does not believe in him, he has not eaten him, and thus has not had the faith of Christians (BY WHICH ALONE SINS ARE RELAXED); how, if the Lord lives, to whom the Father has given all judgment, will he escape the judgment of everlasting damnation?

units.la: Justitiam non esse, ubi fides non est.
units.tr: That there is no righteousness where there is no faith.

units.la: 24.q.1.Ubi.) Ubi fana[?] fides non est, non potest esse justitia, quia justus ex fide vivit.
units.tr: 24. q. 1. Where.) Where faith is not [sound?], there cannot be righteousness, because the just lives by faith.

units.la: Non nisi per fidem Christi ab ira nos liberari.
units.tr: That we are freed from wrath only through faith in Christ.

units.la: De Conf.Dist.4.Firmissimo.) Eramus enim natura filii irae, sicut & caeteri, à qua nullus liberabitur, NISI per fidem mediatoris, hominis Jesu Christi.
units.tr: De Conf. Dist. 4. Most firmly.) For we were by nature children of wrath, as the others also, from which no one will be freed EXCEPT through faith in the Mediator, the man Jesus Christ.

units.la: DE SACRAMENTIS. CAPUT X.
units.tr: DE SACRAMENTIS. CAPUT X. (On Sacraments. Chapter 10.)

units.la: Sacramentum quid sit.
units.tr: What a sacrament is.

units.la: De Con. Dist.2. Sacrificium.) Sacramentum, id est, sacrum signum.
units.tr: De Con. Dist.2. Sacrificium.) A sacrament, that is, a holy sign.

units.la: Item, Sacramentum est invisibilis gratiae vi-sibilis forma.
units.tr: Likewise, a sacrament is the visible form of invisible grace.

units.la: Signum quid sit.
units.tr: What a sign is.

units.la: Ibidem. Signum est res praeter speciem quâ ingerit sensibus, aliud aliquid faciens ex se in cognitionem venire.
units.tr: Ibidem. A sign is a thing which, beyond the appearance it presents to the senses, causes something else from itself to come into knowledge.

units.la: De figuratis locutionibus.
units.tr: On figurative expressions.

units.la: De. Con. Dist.4. Quæris.) Sæpe ita loqui-mur, ut pascha appropinquante crastinam, vel perdissenam, vel perendissenam, Domini pas-sionem dicamus, cum ille ante multos annos passus sit, nec omnino nisi semel ipsa passio facta sit. Nempe ipso die Dominico dicimus, Hodie Dominus surrexit, cum ex quo resurrexe-rit, tot anni transierunt. Cur nemo tam ineptus est, ut ita nos loquentes, arguat nos esse mentitos, nisi quia istos dies, secundum illorum, quibus hæc gesta sunt, similitudinem nuncupa-mus, ut dicatur ipsa dies, quæ non est ipsa revo-lutione temporis, sed similis eius, & dicatur illo die fieri propter Sacramenti celebrationem, quod non illo, sed iam olim factum est in alio?
units.tr: De Con. Dist.4. Quæris.) We often speak in such a way that, when Easter is approaching, we say that the Lord's passion is tomorrow, or the day after, or the day after that, though he suffered many years ago, and the passion itself happened only once. Indeed, on the Lord's day itself we say, "Today the Lord rose," though many years have passed since he rose. Who is so foolish as to accuse us of lying when we speak like this, unless it is because we name these days by their likeness to the days on which these things were done, so that the day itself is said to be this day, which is not the very revolution of time but a likeness of it, and it is said to happen on that day because of the celebration of the sacrament, which did not happen then but long ago in another time?

units.la: Sacramentum sine Verbo nihil esse quam elementum. Augusti. Homil.80.
units.tr: Without the Word, the sacrament is nothing but an element. Augustine, Homily 80.

units.la: i.q.1. Detrahe.) Detrahe Verbum ab aqua, quid erit nisi aqua? Accedit Verbum ad elemen-tum & fit Sacramentum. Unde ista tanta vir-tus aquæ, ut corpus tangat, & cor abluat, nisi fa-ciente verbo? non quia dicitur, sed quia cre-ditur.
units.tr: i.q.1. Detrahe.) Take the Word away from the water, and what is it but water? The Word comes to the element and it becomes a sacrament. Whence comes that great power of the water, that it touches the body and cleanses the heart, except by the working of the Word? Not because it is spoken, but because it is believed.

units.la: In Sacramentis aliud videri, & a-liud intelligi.
units.tr: That in the sacraments one thing is seen and another understood.

units.la: De Con.Dist.2. Qui manducant.) Quod videtur, panis est, quod etiam oculi renunciant. Quod autem fides postulat instruenda, panis est corpus Christi, calix sanguis. Ista ideo dicuntur Sacramenta, quia in eis aliud videtur, & aliud intelligitur. Quod videtur speciem habet corporalem, quod intelligitur, fructum habet spiritualem.
units.tr: De Con. Dist.2. Qui manducant.) What is seen is bread, which the eyes also report. But what faith requires to be taught is that the bread is the body of Christ, and the cup the blood. These are therefore called sacraments because in them one thing is seen and another is understood. What is seen has a bodily appearance; what is understood has a spiritual fruit.

units.la: Aliud esse Sacramentum, aliud operationem Spiritus sancti. Augusti.
units.tr: That the sacrament is one thing, and the working of the Holy Spirit another. Augustine.

units.la: 1.q.1. Multæ autem.) Cum aliud sit Sacramentum, quod habere etiam Simon Magus potuit, & aliud prophetia, quæ in malis hominibus etiam fieri solet, ut in Saul, aliud operatio eiusdem Spiritus sancti, quam nisi boni habere non possunt.
units.tr: 1.q.1. Multæ autem.) Since the sacrament is one thing, which even Simon Magus was able to have, and prophecy is another, which often happens even in evil men, as in Saul, and the working of the same Holy Spirit is another, which only good people can have.

units.la: 1.q.1. Etiam.) Aliud est Sacramentum ab effectu Sacramenti.
units.tr: 1.q.1. Etiam.) The sacrament is one thing, and the effect of the sacrament is another.

units.la: Sacramenta omnibus communia esse, sed non comunem gratiam: Gratianus ait.
units.tr: The sacraments are common to all, but the grace is not common: Gratian says.

units.la: De Pœnit. Dist. 4. Peccatum.) Etsi in aliqui-bus communia omnibus sunt omnia Sacramenta, sed non communis gratia, ita & nunc baptismus est communis, sed non virtus bap-tismi. Dominum non nisi per seipsum dare gratiam.
units.tr: De Pœnit. Dist.4. Peccatum.) Although in some cases all the sacraments are common to all, the grace is not common; so now baptism is common, but the power of baptism is not. The Lord gives grace only through himself.

units.la: De Con. Dist. 4. Sacramentum gratiæ dat Deus etiam per malos, ipsam verò gratiam, non nisi per seipsum, vel per sanctos suos. Et glosa marginalis addit, imò per seipsum semper, nunquam per ministrum hominem.
units.tr: De Con. Dist.4. God gives the sacrament of grace even through wicked men, but grace itself only through himself or through his saints. And the marginal gloss adds: indeed always through himself, never through a human minister.

units.la: In Sacramentis, neque eum qui plantat, esse aliquid, neque eum qui rigat, sed Deus qui dat incrementum: ex Hieronymo in Micheam.
units.tr: In the sacraments, neither he who plants is anything, nor he who waters, but God who gives the increase: from Jerome on Micah.

units.la: 1.q.1. Cum enim in Sacramentis neque qui plantat, neque qui rigat sit aliquid, sed qui incrementum dat Deus, quis operatur in eis, si Dominus qui incrementum dat, in eis non lucet, sed est otiosus?
units.tr: 1.q.1. For since in the sacraments neither he who plants nor he who waters is anything, but God who gives the increase, who is at work in them, if the Lord who gives the increase does not shine in them, but is idle?

units.la: Sacramenta sine charitate nullam apud Deum iustitiam præstare.
units.tr: Sacraments without love produce no righteousness before God.

units.la: De Pœnit. Dist. 2. Si enim inquit. Qui si charitatem Dei non habent, ante Dei oculos aqua tantum regenerantur, non Spiritu sancto. Opera enim seu Sacramentorum participatio, nisi ex charitate procedant, apud Deum nec iustitiam nec innocentiam præstant.
units.tr: De Pœnit. Dist.2. Si enim, he says. Those who do not have the love of God are regenerated before God's eyes by water only, not by the Holy Spirit. For works, or the participation in the sacraments, unless they proceed from love, provide before God neither righteousness nor innocence.

units.la: Aurum Sacramenta non quærunt.
units.tr: Sacraments do not seek gold.

units.la: Ambr. de Off.
units.tr: Ambrose, On the Duties.

units.la: 12.q.2. Aurum. Aurum Sacramenta non quęrunt, neque auro placent quæ auro non emun-tur. Ornatus sacrorum, redemptio captiuorum est, & vera illa sunt vasa pretiosa, quæ redimunt animas à morte, ille verus thesaurus est Domini, qui operatur, quod sanguis eius operatus est.
units.tr: 12.q.2. Gold. Sacraments do not seek gold, nor are they pleased with gold; those things are not bought with gold. The adornment of the sacred vessels is the ransoming of captives, and those are the true precious vessels which redeem souls from death. That is the true treasure of the Lord, which works what his blood has worked.

units.la: Precium pro Sacramentis non deberé exigi. Ex VI. Synodo.
units.tr: That no price should be demanded for the sacraments. From the Sixth Synod.

units.la: 1.q.1. Nullus Episcopus.) Nullus Episcopus aut presbyter aut diaconus, qui sacram dispen-sat communionem, à percipiente gratiam communionis, aliquod pretium exigat, neque enim venditur gratia, neque pro pretio gratiam Spi-ritus sancti damus, sed dignis muneribus sine defraudatione participare concedimus. Si quis verò eorum qui connumerantur in clero, ab eo cui sacram communionem dispensat, aliquod pretium exegerit, deponatur sicut imitator Simoniacæ fraudis.
units.tr: 1.q.1. No bishop. No bishop, presbyter or deacon who dispenses the holy communion shall demand any price from the one who receives the grace of communion, for grace is not sold, nor do we give the grace of the Holy Spirit for a price, but we allow worthy people to partake of it without any fraud. But if any of those who are counted among the clergy demands some price from the one to whom he dispenses the holy communion, he shall be deposed as an imitator of the fraud of Simon.

units.la: Et mox ex Concilio Toletano XI. Quic-quid invisibilis gratiæ consolatione tribuitur, nunquam quæstibus vel quibuslibet præmiis venundari penitus debet, dicente Domino, Quod gratis accepistis, gratis date.
units.tr: And soon after, from the Eleventh Council of Toledo: Whatever is given through the consolation of invisible grace must never at all be sold for profits or any kind of rewards, since the Lord says, "You have received freely, give freely."

units.la: Item ex Concilio Triburiensi ibidem. Di-ctum est, solere in quibusdam locis pro perceptione chrismatis nummos dari, similiter pro baptismo & communione. Hoc Simoniacæ hæ- resis esse testata est sancta Synodus[?], & anathe- matizauit, & vt de cætero, nec pro ordinatione, nec pro chrismate vel baptismo, vel pro balsa- mo, nec pro sepultura vel communione quic- quam exigatur, statuit, sed gratis dona Christi gratuita dispensatione donentur.
units.tr: Likewise from the Council of Tribur, in the same place: It has been said that in some places it is customary to give coins for receiving chrism, and likewise for baptism and communion. The holy Synod has declared this to be the heresy of Simony and has anathematized it, and has decreed that henceforth nothing shall be demanded for ordination, nor for chrism or baptism, nor for balsam, nor for burial or communion; but the gifts of Christ shall be given freely, by free dispensation.

units.la: DE BAPTISMO.
units.tr: ON BAPTISM.

units.la: CAPVT XI.
units.tr: CHAPTER XI.

units.la: Idem esse in nomine Trinitatis & in nomine Christi baptizare. Nicol. Papa.
units.tr: That baptizing in the name of the Trinity and baptizing in the name of Christ are the same. Pope Nicholas.

units.la: De Con. Dist. 4. A quodam.) A quodam Iu- dæo, nescitis vtrum Christiano an pagano, multos in patria vestra baptizatos asseritis, & quid inde fit agendum consulitis. Hi profecto, si in nomine sanctæ Trinitatis, vel tantum in no- mine Christi (sicut in Actibus Apostolorum le- gitur) baptizati sunt, (vnum quippe idemque est, vt sanctus Ambrosius exponit) quia non il- lorum, sed eius est, rebaptizari non debent.
units.tr: De Con. Dist. 4. A quodam.) To a certain Jew, whether a Christian or a pagan you do not know, you report that many have been baptized in your homeland, and you ask what ought to be done about them. Certainly, if they were baptized in the name of the holy Trinity, or only in the name of Christ (as is read in the Acts of the Apostles), for the two are one and the same, as Saint Ambrose explains, they ought not to be baptized again, because the baptism is not theirs but his.

units.la: Mox tamen ibidem C. Si revera:) iubentur rebaptizari, qui tantum in nomine Domini baptizati sunt.
units.tr: Immediately afterwards in the same place, C. Si revera: They are ordered to be baptized again who were baptized only in the name of the Lord.

units.la: Nihil referre vtrum semel vel ter baptizandus immergatur. De Con. Dist.4. De trina.) De trina mersione baptismatis, nihil responderi verius potest, quàm quod ipsi sensistis, quia in una fide nihil officit sanctæ ecclesiæ consuetudo diuersa.
units.tr: It makes no difference whether the one to be baptized is immersed once or three times. De Con. Dist. 4. De trina. Concerning the triple immersion of baptism, nothing more true can be answered than what you yourselves have said: that in the one faith the differing custom of the holy Church does no harm.

units.la: Et mox: Reprehensibile esse nullatenus potest, infante in baptismate, vel ter vel semel immergere, quoniam etiam in tribus mersionibus personarum trinitas, & in una potest diuinitatis singularitas designari.
units.tr: And shortly after: It can by no means be blameworthy, when an infant is baptized, to immerse it either three times or once, since in the three immersions the Trinity of persons, and in the one immersion the singleness of the Godhead, can be signified.

units.la: Olim in festo Paschæ & Pentecostes tantùm baptizatum esse.
units.tr: That formerly baptism was given only at the feasts of Easter and Pentecost.

units.la: De Con. Dist.4. Non ratione.) Non ratione authoritatis alicuius, sed sola temeritate præsumitur, ut passim & liberè in natiuitate Christi, seu apparitione, nec non Apostolorum seu martyrum festiuitatibus innumeræ plebes baptizentur, cum sibi priuilegium hoc apud nos & apud ecclesias omnes Dominicum pascha defendat specialiter cum sancta pentecoste.
units.tr: De Con. Dist. 4. Non ratione.) It is not on the basis of any authority but by mere rashness that countless peoples are presumed to be baptized everywhere and freely at the Nativity or Epiphany of Christ, and at the feasts of the Apostles and martyrs, when among us and in all the churches the Lord's Pascha, together with holy Pentecost, especially claims this privilege for itself.

units.la: Et mox. Duo tempora, id est, pascha & pentecostes ad baptizandum à Romano Pontifice legitimè sunt præfixa.
units.tr: And shortly after: Two seasons, that is, Easter and Pentecost, have been lawfully fixed by the Roman Pontiff for baptizing.

units.la: Non aquam sed Verbum vel Verbū in aqua mundare.
units.tr: That it is not the water but the Word that cleanses, or the Word cleanses in the water.

units.la: De Con. Dist.4. Aliud est.) Item. Iam vos mundi estis propter Verbū quod locutus sum vobis. Quare non ait, mundi estis propter baptismum quo abluti estis,sed ait,propter verbū quod locutus sum vobis, nisi quia etiam in aqua Verbum mundat.
units.tr: De Con. Dist. 4. Aliud est.) Likewise: Now you are clean because of the word that I have spoken to you. Why does he not say, "You are clean because of the baptism in which you were washed," but says, "because of the word that I have spoken to you," unless because the Word cleanses even in the water?

units.la: Non tam ablutione corporis quàm fi-de cordis baptisma constare.
units.tr: That baptism consists not so much in the washing of the body as in the faith of the heart.

units.la: De Con. Dist.4. Verus.) Verus baptismus constat non tam ablutione corporis,quàm fide cordis,sicut Apostolica doctrina tradidit,dicés: Fide mundans corda eorū. Et alibi, Saluos facit baptismus,non carnis depositio sordium,sed etiam conscientiæ bonæ interrogatio in Deum.
units.tr: De Con. Dist. 4. Verus.) True baptism consists not so much in the washing of the body as in the faith of the heart, as Apostolic doctrine has taught, saying: "Cleansing their hearts by faith." And elsewhere: Baptism saves, not the putting away of the filth of the flesh, but the appeal of a good conscience toward God.

units.la: Ministros ministerialiter tantùm ba-ptizare, Christū autem per potestatem.
units.tr: That ministers baptize only ministerially, but Christ baptizes by his own power.

units.la: De Con. Dist.4. Aliud.) Aliud est baptizare per ministerium,aliud baptizare per potestaté.
units.tr: De Con. Dist. 4. Aliud.) It is one thing to baptize through a minister, and another thing to baptize through one's own power.

units.la: Et mox. Per hanc enim potestatem, quam Christus solus tenuit sibi,&in neminem ministrorum transfudit, quàmuis per ministros baptizare dignatus sit, per hanc inquam stat unitas ecclesiæ,quæ significatur in columba,de qua dictum est: Una est columba mea, una est matris suæ electa. Si enim,ut jam dixi fratres mei, transferretur à Domino potestas ad ministros, tot baptismata essent, quot ministri essent, & jam unitas baptismi non staret. Baptismum communem esse, sed non virtutem baptismi.
units.tr: And shortly after: For it is through this power, which Christ alone held for himself and transferred to none of his ministers, though he deigned to baptize through ministers, that the unity of the Church is maintained, which is signified in the dove, of which it is said: "My dove is one, the chosen one of her mother." For if, as I have already said, my brothers, the power were transferred by the Lord to ministers, there would be as many baptisms as there were ministers, and the unity of baptism would no longer stand. That baptism is common, but the power of baptism is not.

units.la: De Pœn.it. Dist.4. Peccatum.) Etsi in aliqui-bus comunia omnibus sunt omnia Sacramen-ta, sed non communis gratia, ita & nunc baptismus est communis, sed non virtus baptismi.
units.tr: De Poen.it. Dist. 4. Peccatum.) Although all the sacraments are in some respects common to all, yet grace is not common; so also now baptism is common, but the power of baptism is not.

units.la: Non damnari fideles, qui à baptismo necessitate excluduntur. Augusti.[?]
units.tr: That the faithful are not condemned who are excluded from baptism by necessity. Augustine[?]

units.la: De Conf. Dist. 4. Baptismi vicem.) Etiam atque etiam considerans inuenio, non tantum passione Christi id quod baptismo deerat, pos-se supplere, sed etiam fidem confessionemque cordis, si forte ad celebrandum mysterium baptismi in angustiis temporū succurri nō potest.
units.tr: De Conf. Dist. 4. Baptismi vicem.) Considering again and again, I find that not only the Passion of Christ can supply what was lacking in baptism, but also faith and confession of the heart, if perhaps in the straits of the times the celebration of the mystery of baptism cannot be provided.

units.la: Et mox. Quantum itaque valeat, etiam sine visibili Sacramento baptismi, quod ait Aposto-lus, Corde creditur ad iustitiam, ore autem con-sessio fit ad salutem, in illo latrone declaratum est, sed nunc impletur inuisibiliter, cum mysterium baptismi, non contemptus religionis, sed articulus necessitatis excludit.
units.tr: And shortly after: How much, then, faith without the visible sacrament of baptism avails, which the Apostle declares, "With the heart one believes unto righteousness, and with the mouth confession is made unto salvation," was shown in that thief; but now it is fulfilled invisibly, when the necessity, not any contempt of religion, excludes the mystery of baptism.

units.la: Non reiterandum esse baptisma, quod in nomine Trinitatis ministratum est.
units.tr: That baptism administered in the name of the Trinity is not to be repeated.

units.la: De Con. Dist. 4. Si qui.) Si qui apud illos hæreticos baptizati sunt, qui in sanctæ Trinitatis confessione baptizant, & veniunt ad Catholieam[?] fidem, recipiantur quidem ut baptizati, ne sanctæ Trinitatis invocatio vel confessio annulletur.
units.tr: De Con. Dist. 4. Si qui.) If any who have been baptized among those heretics who baptize in the confession of the holy Trinity come to the Catholic faith, they are indeed to be received as baptized, lest the invocation or confession of the holy Trinity be annulled.

units.la: Multis hoc capitibus agitur per totam distinctionem illam.
units.tr: This is treated in many chapters throughout that whole distinction.

units.la: Ibidem C. Rebaptizare.) Rebaptizare hære-ticū hominem, qui hæc sanctæ Trinitatis signa suscepit, quæ Christiana tradidit disciplina, omnino peccatum est, rebaptizare autem Ca-tholicum, immanissimum scelus est.
units.tr: Ibidem C. Rebaptizare.) To rebaptize a heretical man who has received these signs of the holy Trinity, which Christian discipline has handed down, is altogether a sin; but to rebaptize a Catholic is a most monstrous crime.

units.la: CAPVT XII. DE ÇOENA DOMINI.
units.tr: CHAPTER XII. CONCERNING THE LORD'S SUPPER.

units.la: A quibus Missa instituta sit.
units.tr: By whom the Mass was instituted.
