units.la: De Con.Dist.1. Iacobus.) Iacobus frater Do-mini secundum carnem, cui primum credita est Hierosolymitana ecclesia, & Basilius Cæsa-riensis Episcopus (cuius claritas per totum or-bem refulsit) in scripturis addiderunt nobis Missæ celebrationem.
units.tr: De Con. Dist. 1. Iacobus.) James, the brother of the Lord according to the flesh, to whom the Church of Jerusalem was first entrusted, and Basil, Bishop of Caesarea (whose renown shone throughout the whole world), in their writings added to us the celebration of the Mass.

units.la: Eucharistiam non ab homine, sed à Deo sanctificationem accipere. Gregor. 1.q.1. Non noçet.) Eucharistia & omnia quæcunq; in altari ponuntur, non ab homine, sed à Deo sanctificationem accipiunt.
units.tr: That the Eucharist receives its sanctification not from man but from God. Gregory, 1. q. 1. Non noceat.) The Eucharist, and all things whatsoever that are placed on the altar, receive their sanctification not from man but from God.

units.la: In Cœna Domini nihil faciendum ef-fe,nisi quod Dominus prior fecit.
units.tr: In the Lord's Supper nothing is to be done except what the Lord did first.

units.la: De Con. Dist.2. Scriptura.) Scriptura dicit, ut quotiescunque calicem in commemorationem Domini & pasionis eius offerimus , id quod constat Dominum fecisse,faciamus,
units.tr: De Con. Dist. 2. Scriptura.) Scripture says that as often as we offer the cup in remembrance of the Lord and of his passion, we should do what the Lord is known to have done.

units.la: Et mox. C. In sacramento.) In sacramento corporis & sanguinis Domini nihil amplius offeratur, quam quod ipse Dominus tradidit.
units.tr: And soon after. C. In sacramento.) In the sacrament of the body and blood of the Lord nothing more is to be offered than what the Lord himself delivered.

units.la: Item. C. Cum omne. Manifestum est,& euidés exemplum veritatis euangelicæ illuxit, quod præter panem & vinum aliud offerri non licet.
units.tr: Likewise. C. Cum omne. It is plain, and the clear example of the gospel truth shines forth, that nothing may be offered besides bread and wine.

units.la: Quid sit corpus Christi manducare, & sanguinem eius bibere,
units.tr: What it is to eat the body of Christ and drink his blood.

units.la: De Con. Dist.2. Quid est.) Quid est Christū manducare? Non hoc est solum in sacramento corpus eius accipere, multi enim indignè accipiunt, de quibus ait Apostolus, Qui manducat & bibit calicem Domini indignè, iudicium sibi manducat & bibit. Sed quomodo manducandus est Christus? quomodo ipse dixit: Qui enim manducat carnem meam, & bibit sanguinem meum, in me manet & ego in eo, & si indignè accipit Sacramentum, acquirit tormentum magnum.
units.tr: De Con. Dist. 2. Quid est.) What is it to eat Christ? It is not merely to receive his body in the sacrament, for many receive it unworthily, of whom the Apostle says: "He who eats and drinks the cup of the Lord unworthily eats and drinks judgement to himself." But how is Christ to be eaten? As he himself said: "For he who eats my flesh and drinks my blood abides in me, and I in him." And if a man receives the sacrament unworthily, he acquires a great torment.

units.la: Et mox C, sequente. Ut quid paras dentem & vetrem? Crede & manducasti. Credere enim in eum, hoc est panem vivum manducare. Qui credit in eum, manducat eum. Item C.Credere.) Credere in Iesum Christum, hoc est manducare panem viuum. Qui credit, manducat. Inuisibiliter saginatur, quia inuisibiliter renascitur, & qui manducat carnem meam, & bibit sanguinem meum, habet vitam æternam.
units.tr: And soon after, in the following chapter. Why do you prepare teeth and belly? Believe, and you have eaten. For to believe in him is to eat the living bread. He who believes in him eats him. Likewise. C. Credere.) To believe in Jesus Christ is to eat the living bread. He who believes eats. He is fed invisibly, because he is reborn invisibly, and he who eats my flesh and drinks my blood has eternal life.

units.la: Et mox ibidem C. Qui discordat à Christo, nō manducat carnem eius, nec bibit sanguiné, etiamsi tantæ rei sacramentum ad iudicū suæ perditionis quotidie accipiat.
units.tr: And soon after, in the same chapter: He who is at odds with Christ does not eat his flesh nor drink his blood, even if he receives daily the sacrament of so great a thing to the judgement of his own perdition.

units.la: Non carnaliter sed spiritualiter Christi corpus & sanguinem debemus comedere.
units.tr: We ought to eat the body and blood of Christ not carnally but spiritually.

units.la: Sic sonat rubrica De Con. Dist. 2. C. Prima quidem.
units.tr: Thus the rubric sounds, De Con. Dist. 2. C. Prima quidem.

units.la: Spiritualiter intelligenda esse verba Domini, quæ de manducatione corporis sui loquitur.
units.tr: The words of the Lord, in which he speaks of the eating of his body, are to be understood spiritually.

units.la: Ibidem ) Cum enim diceret, Nisi quis manducauerit carnem meam, & biberit sanguinem meum, non habebit vitā æternā. Illi verò non intelligentes dixerunt ad inuicem, Durus est hic sermo, quis eum potest manducare? (aliàs audire) Dicentes, Durus est hic sermo, separauerunt se ab illo, & remansit cum duodecim discipulis. Di-scedentibus illis, instruxit eos qui remanserunt, Spiritus est inquit, qui viuificat, caro nihil prodest, verba quæ locutus sum ad vos, spiritus & vita sunt. Intellexistis spiritualiter, spiritus & vita sunt. Intellexistis carnaliter, etiā sic illa spiritus & vita sunt, sed tibi non sunt spiritus & vita, qui spiritualiter non intelligis. Spiritualiter intelligite quæ locutus sum. Non hoc corpus quod videtis, manducaturi estis, & bibituri il-lū sanguine, quem effusuri sunt, qui me crucifigent. Sacramentum aliquod vobis cōmendaui, spiritualiter intellectū viuificat vos, caro autē non prodest quicquam.
units.tr: In the same place. For when he said, "Unless a man eats my flesh and drinks my blood, he shall not have eternal life," they, not understanding, said to one another, "This is a hard saying; who can eat it?" (or, in another reading, "hear it"). Saying, "This is a hard saying," they separated themselves from him, and he remained with the twelve disciples. When they had departed, he instructed those who remained: "It is the Spirit who gives life; the flesh profits nothing. The words that I have spoken to you are spirit and life." You have understood spiritually: they are spirit and life. You have understood carnally: even so those words are spirit and life, but they are not spirit and life to you, who do not understand spiritually. Understand spiritually what I have said. You are not going to eat this body that you see, nor to drink that blood which those who will crucify me are going to shed. I have commended to you a sacrament; understood spiritually, it gives you life, but the flesh profits nothing.

units.la: Manducare Christū, esse credere in Christum.
units.tr: To eat Christ is to believe in Christ.

units.la: De pœnit. Dist. 2. Charitas.) Hoc est enim manducare panē viuum, quod credere in Christū, id est, amando tendere in ipsum.
units.tr: De poenit. Dist. 2. Charitas.) For this is to eat the living bread: to believe in Christ, that is, to strive toward him in love.

units.la: Distinguendū esse inter naturā verbi & corporis Christi.
units.tr: One must distinguish between the nature of the Word and the body of Christ.

units.la: De Con. Dist. 2. C. Si credis.) Si credis à Christo carnē esse susceptam, & offeras transfiguratum corpus in altari, nec tamen distinguis naturam verbi & corporis Christi, dicitur tibi, si recte offeras, recte autem nō diuidas, peccasti.
units.tr: De Con. Dist. 2. C. Si credis.) If you believe that the flesh was taken up by Christ, and you offer on the altar the transfigured body, yet do not distinguish the nature of the Word from the body of Christ, it is said to you: if you offer rightly, but do not divide rightly, you have sinned.

units.la: Verbum Christi æque magnum esse ac corpus Christi. Augusti.
units.tr: The Word of Christ is as great as the body of Christ. Augustine.

units.la: 1.q.1.Interrogo.) Interrogo vos fratres vel sorores, dicite mihi, quid plus videtur vobis, corpus Christi an verbū Christi? Si vultis verè re-spōdere, hoc dicere debetis, quòd nō sit minus Dei Verbū, quā Christi corpus, & ideo quāta sq[?] licitudine obseruamus, quádo nobis Christi corpus ministrat:vt nihil ex ipso de manib.nostris in terrā cadat, tanta sollicitudine obseruemus ne Verbum Domini, quod nobis erogatur, dū aliud aut cogitamus aut loquimur, de corde puro pereat. Quia non minus erit reus, qui verbū Dei negligenter audierit, quàm ille qui corpus Christi sua negligentia in terram cadere permiserit,
units.tr: 1. q. 1. Interrogo.) I ask you, brothers and sisters: tell me, which seems greater to you, the body of Christ or the word of Christ? If you wish to answer truly, you ought to say that the Word of God is no less than the body of Christ. Therefore, with what care we keep watch when the body of Christ is ministered to us, that nothing of it falls from our hands to the ground, with the same care we should take that the word of the Lord, which is dispensed to us, does not perish from a pure heart while we think or speak of other things. For he who has heard the word of God carelessly will be no less guilty than he who through his carelessness allowed the body of Christ to fall to the ground.

units.la: Sacramentum suo modo vocari corpus Christi, non rei veritate, sed signifi-cante mysterio.
units.tr: That the sacrament is called the body of Christ in its own way, not in the truth of the thing, but by signifying a mystery.

units.la: De Con. Dist. 2. Hoc est.) Sicut ergo cœle-stis panis, qui Christi caro est (id est cœleste Sacramentum quod verè REPRAESENTAT Christi carnē,) suo modo vocatur corpus Christi, (in Glossa iterū additur, vt sit sensus, vocatur Christi corpus, id est, SIGNIFICAT.) cum reuera sit Sacramentum corporis Christi illius videlicet, quod visibile, quod palpabile, mortale in cruce positum est, vocatúrque ipsa immolatio carnis, quæ sacerdotis manibus fit, Christi passio,mors,Crucifixio,non rei veritate,sed significante mysterio. Sic Sacramentum fidei,quod baptismus intelligitur,fides est.
units.tr: De Con. Dist. 2. Hoc est.) Therefore, just as the heavenly bread, which is the flesh of Christ (that is, the heavenly Sacrament which truly REPRESENTS the flesh of Christ), is in its own way called the body of Christ (the Gloss adds again, so that the sense is: it is called the body of Christ, that is, it SIGNIFIES), although it is really the sacrament of the body of Christ, namely of that body which, visible, tangible and mortal, was placed on the cross; and the very immolation of the flesh, which is performed by the priest's hands, is called Christ's passion, death and crucifixion, not in the truth of the thing but in the mystery it signifies. So too the sacrament of faith, which is understood to be baptism, is faith.

units.la: Pane significari corpus Christi, & vino sanguinem.
units.tr: That the body of Christ is signified by the bread, and the blood by the wine.

units.la: De Con. Dist. 2. Coperimus. Glossa habet: Portione, id est, specie panis, quae tantum sacrum corpus SIGNIFICAT. Item. A calice, id est, a specie vini, quae SIGNIFICAT sacrum sanguinem.
units.tr: De Con. Dist. 2. Coperimus. The Gloss has: By the portion, that is, by the species of bread, which alone SIGNIFIES the holy body. Likewise: by the chalice, that is, by the species of wine, which SIGNIFIES the holy blood.

units.la: Ibidem. C. Nulli.) Nulli est aliquatenus dubitandum, vnumquemque fidelium, corporis & sanguinis Dominici tunc esse participem, quando in baptismate membrum efficitur Christi, nec alienari ab illius panis calicisque consortio, etiamsi antequam panem illum comedat, calicemque bibat de hoc seculo migrauerit, in vnitate corporis Christi constitutus. Sacramenti quippe illius participatione ac beneficio non priuabitur, quando in se hoc quod illud sacramentum SIGNIFICAT inuenitur.
units.tr: Ibidem. C. Nulli.) No one should in any way doubt that each of the faithful is then a partaker of the body and blood of the Lord, when in baptism he is made a member of Christ, and is not cut off from the fellowship of that bread and cup, even if, before he eats that bread and drinks the cup, he has departed from this age, having been established in the unity of the body of Christ. For he will not be deprived of the participation and benefit of that sacrament, since in him is found what that sacrament SIGNIFIES.

units.la: Ascensionem Domini testari, quod Dominus corpus suum carnaliter non eroget, & quod gratia morsibus non consumatur.
units.tr: That the Ascension of the Lord testifies that the Lord does not dispense his body carnally, and that grace is not consumed by bites.

units.la: De Con. Dist. 2. Prima quidem.) Sciens autem Iesus ait, Hoc vos scandalizat, quia dixi, Do vobis carnem meam manducare, & sanguinem meum bibere? Si ergo videritis filium hominis ascendentem vbi prius erat. Quid est hoc? Hic soluit quod illos mouerat, hic aperuit vnde fuerant scandalizati, hinc plane, si intelligerent. Illi autem putabant erogaturum corpus suum, ille dixit, se ascensurum in Cœlum, vtique integrum. Cum videritis filium hominis ascendente ubi erat prius, certe vel tunc videbitis quia non eo modo quo putatis erogat corpus suum, vel tunc intelligetis, quia gratia eius non consumitur morsibus.
units.tr: De Con. Dist. 2. Prima quidem.) But Jesus, knowing, said: Does this scandalize you, that I said, I will give you my flesh to eat and my blood to drink? If therefore you see the Son of man ascending where he was before. What is this? Here he resolves what had disturbed them; here he opened up plainly, if they understood, where their scandal came from. But they thought he would give out his body, and he said that he would ascend into heaven, whole indeed. When you see the Son of man ascending where he was before, surely then you will see that he does not give out his body in the way you think; or then you will understand that his grace is not consumed by bites.

units.la: Dominũ sursum esse, & corpus eius in quo resurrexit in vno loco esse.
units.tr: That the Lord is above, and that his body in which he rose is in one place.

units.la: De Con. Dist.2. Prima quidem.) Item, donec fæculum finiatur, SVRSVM DOMINVS EST, sed tamen etiam hic nobiscum est veritas Domini. Corpus enim in quo resurrexit IN VNO LOCO ESSE OPORTET, veritas autem eius vbique diffusa est.
units.tr: De Con. Dist. 2. Prima quidem.) Again, until the world is finished, THE LORD IS ABOVE; yet even here the truth of the Lord is with us. For the body in which he rose MUST BE IN ONE PLACE, but his truth is diffused everywhere.

units.la: Quomodo Christus semel immolatus fit, & in Cœna quotidiè immoletur. Rubrica.
units.tr: How Christ was offered once, and in the Supper is immolated every day. Rubric.

units.la: De Con. Dist.2. Semel Christus.) Semel Christus mortuus est, iustus pro iniustis: & scimus & certũ habemus & spe immobili retinemus, quia Christus resurgens a mortuis, iam nõ moritur, mors illi ultra non dominabitur. Verba ista apostoli sunt. Tamen ne obliuiscamini quod semel factum est, in memoria nostra fit omni anno. Quotiens Pascha celebratur, nunquid totiens Christus occiditur? Non, sed anniuersaria recordatio repræsentat quod olim factū est, & sic nos facit moneri, táquam videamus præsentem Dominum in cruce.
units.tr: De Con. Dist. 2. Semel Christus.) Christ died once, the just for the unjust; and we know, and hold for certain, and retain with unshaken hope, that Christ, rising from the dead, now dies no more; death will no longer have dominion over him. These are the words of the Apostle. Yet, lest you forget what was done once, it is done in our memory every year. As often as the Passover is celebrated, is Christ killed so often? No; but the yearly remembrance represents what was done long ago, and so makes us remember, as though we saw the Lord present on the cross.

units.la: Ibidem.C.In Christo.) In Christo semel oblata est hostia ad salutem sempiternam potens. Quid ergo nos? Nonne per singulos dies offeri mus? sed ad recordationem mortis eius. Et vna est hostia, non multæ. Quomodo est vna, non multæ? quia semel oblatus est Christus, hoc autem sacrificium, EXEMPLVM est illius.
units.tr: Ibidem. C. In Christo.) In Christ a sacrifice was offered once, able to bring eternal salvation. What then of us? Do we not offer it every single day? Yes, but in remembrance of his death. And it is one sacrifice, not many. How is it one and not many? Because Christ was offered once; but this sacrifice is an EXAMPLE of that one.

units.la: Et mox ibidem.) Quod nos facimus, in COMMEMORATIONEM fit eius quod factum est. Hoc enim facite, ait, in meam commemorationem.
units.tr: Et mox ibidem.) What we do is done in COMMEMORATION of what was done. For he said: Do this in my commemoration.

units.la: Quomodo veteres eandem escam spiritualem nobiscum comederint.
units.tr: How the ancients ate the same spiritual food as we do.

units.la: De Con. Dist.2. Inquit Apostolus.) Inquit Apostolus, Omnes eandem escam spiritualem manducauerunt. Spiritualē vtiq; eandem, nam corporalem aliam, quia illi manna manducauerūt, nos aliud. Et omnes eundem potum spiritualē biberunt, aliud illi, aliud nos, sed specie visibili, quod tamen idem est virtute spirituali.
units.tr: De Con. Dist. 2. Inquit Apostolus.) The Apostle says: All ate the same spiritual food. Spiritual, certainly the same; for the bodily food was different, since they ate manna and we something else. And all drank the same spiritual drink: they had one drink, we another, but in visible form; yet it is the same in spiritual power.

units.la: Quòd in missa omnes communicare debeant,
units.tr: That all should communicate at the Mass,

units.la: De Con. Dist. 2. Perácta.) Perácta consecratione OMNES communicent, qui noluerint ecclesiasticis carere liminibus. Sic enim Apostoli statuerunt, & sancta Romana tenet ecclesia.
units.tr: De Con. Dist. 2. Perácta.) When the consecration is finished, let ALL communicate who are unwilling to be kept from the thresholds of the church. For so the Apostles decreed, and the holy Roman Church holds.

units.la: Quoties communicandum sit.
units.tr: How often one should communicate.

units.la: De Con. Dist.2. Quotidie. Quotidie eucharistiæ communionem accipere nec laudo, nec vitupero, omnibus tamen Dominicis diebus communicandum hortor.
units.tr: De Con. Dist. 2. Quotidie.) I neither praise nor blame receiving the communion of the Eucharist every day; yet I urge everyone to communicate on all the Lord's days.

units.la: Et mox.) Si dixerit quispiam, non quotidie accipiendam eucharistiam, alius affirmat, quotidie. Faciat unusquisque quod secundum fide suam pie credit faciendum.
units.tr: Et mox.) If someone says that the Eucharist should not be received daily, another affirms that it should be received daily. Let each one do what he piously believes, according to his faith, ought to be done.

units.la: Ibidem. C. Etsi. Etsi non frequentius, saltē[?] in anno ter homines communicent, nisi forte quis in maioribus quibuslibet criminibus impediatur, in pascha videlicet, & pentecoste, & natali Domini.
units.tr: Ibidem. C. Etsi.) Even if not more often, yet people should communicate at least three times a year, unless perhaps someone is prevented by some greater crimes: namely at Easter, at Pentecost, and at the birthday of the Lord.

units.la: Et mox C. Seculares.) Qui in natali Domini, pascha, pentecoste non communicauerint, catholici non credantur, nec inter catholicos habeantur.
units.tr: Et mox C. Seculares.) Those who have not communicated at the birthday of the Lord, at Easter, or at Pentecost are not to be believed Catholic, nor are they to be counted among the Catholics.

units.la: De utraque specie exhibenda.
units.tr: On administering both kinds.

units.la: De Con. Dist.2. Cum omne.) Cum omne crimen atque peccatum oblatis Deo sacrificijs deleatur, quid de cætero pro delictorum expiatione Domino dabitur, quando in ipsa sacrificiij oblatione erratur? Audiuimus enim quof-dá schismatica ambitione detentos, contra diui nos ordines & Apostolicas institutiones, lac pro vino in diuinis sacrificijs dedicare. Alias quoque intinctam eucharistiam populis pro complemento communionis porrigere.
units.tr: De Con. Dist. 2, Cum omne.) Since every crime and sin is wiped away by the sacrifices offered to God, what will be given to the Lord from then on for the expiation of offences, when error is made in the very offering of the sacrifice? For we have heard that certain men, held by schismatic ambition, contrary to the divine ordinances and apostolic institutions, consecrate milk instead of wine in the divine sacrifices, and also give the eucharist dipped (in wine) to the people as a supplement to communion.

units.la: Et mox ibidem.) Illud vero quod pro complemento communionis intincta tradunt eucharistiam populis, nec hoc prolatum ex euangelio testimonium receperunt, vbi Apostolis corpus suum commendauit & sanguinem, seorsum enim panis, & seorsum calicis commendatio memoratur. Nam intinctum panem alijs Christum prebuisse non legimus, excepto illo tantum discipulo, quem intincta buccela magistri proditorem ostenderet, non quæ sacramenti huius institutionem signaret.
units.tr: Et mox ibidem.) As for what they hand to the people, the dipped eucharist, as a supplement to communion, they have not received even this testimony from the Gospel, where Christ committed his body and blood to the Apostles; for the commission of the bread and of the cup is recorded separately. Indeed we do not read that Christ gave dipped bread to others, except that single morsel which he dipped and gave to his disciple to show who the traitor was, not to signify the institution of this sacrament.

units.la: Item. C. Comperimus.) Coperimus aute, quod quidam sumpta tantum modo corporis sacri portione, à calice sacrati cruoris abstineant, qui proculdubio (quoniam nescio qua superstitione docentur astringi) aut integra sacramenta percipiant, aut ab integris arceantur, quia
units.tr: Item. De Con. Dist. C. Comperimus.) We have also learned that certain people, having taken only a portion of the holy body, abstain from the cup of the holy blood; these, doubtless (since they are taught to be bound by I know not what superstition), either receive the sacraments whole or are excluded from those who receive them whole, because

units.la: DIVISIO VNIVS EIVSDEMQVE MYSTERII, SINE GRANDI SACRILEGIO NON POTEST PERVENIRE.
units.tr: Division of one and the same mystery cannot be effected without great sacrilege.

units.la: In priuatis domibus & oratorijs miss
units.tr: In private houses and oratories the mass is not to be celebrated.

units.la: D fam Non esse celebrandam. Ex Concil. Aurel.
units.tr: D. Not to be celebrated. From the Council of Orléans.

units.la: De Con. Dist.1.C.Vnicuique.)Vnicuique fi-delium in domo sua oratorium licet habere, & ibi orare, missas autem ibi celebrare non licet.
units.tr: De Con. Dist. 1, C. Unicuique.) It is permitted for each of the faithful to have an oratory in his own house, and to pray there, but it is not permitted to celebrate mass there.

units.la: Fidelem etiam ante perceptionem eucharistiæ morientem salvari posse.
units.tr: That a faithful person dying before receiving the eucharist can be saved.

units.la: De Con. Dist.2.C.Nulli.) Nulli est aliquantenus dubitandum, unumquemque fideliū, corporis & sanguinis Dominici tunc esse participem, quando in baptismate membrum effici-tur Christi, nec alienari ab illius panis calicisq; consortio, etiamsi antequam panem illum comedat calicemque bibat, de hoc seculo migraverit, in unitate corporis Christi constitutus. Sacramenti quippe illius participatione ac beneficio non privabitur, quando in se hoc quod illud sacramentum significat invenitur.
units.tr: De Con. Dist. 2, C. Nulli.) There is no doubt at all that each of the faithful becomes a partaker of the body and blood of the Lord at the time when he is made a member of Christ in baptism, and is not cut off from fellowship in that bread and cup, even if he departs from this world before he eats that bread and drinks that cup, being established in the unity of the body of Christ. For he will not be deprived of the participation and benefit of that sacrament, since what that sacrament signifies is found in him.

units.la: Excommunicandos, qui usque ad fi-nem missarum solennia non audierint, neque communionem perceperint.
units.tr: That those who have not heard the solemn rites of the mass to its end, nor received communion, are to be excommunicated.

units.la: De Con. Dist.1.C. Omnes fideles.) Omnes fideles qui conveniunt in solennitatibus sacris ad ecclesiam, & scripturas apostolorum & evan-gelium audient: Qui vero non perseverant in oratione usq; dum missa peragatur, nec sancta communione percipiunt, velut inquietudines ecclesiae commovētes convenit communione privari. Idem ibidem C. cum ad Celebrandas.
units.tr: De Con. Dist. 1, C. Omnes fideles.) All the faithful who come together to the church on the holy solemnities, and hear the writings of the apostles and the Gospel, but who do not remain in prayer until the mass is finished, nor receive holy communion, stirring up unrest in the church, it is fitting that they be deprived of communion. The same in the same place, C. Cum ad celebrandas.

units.la: Non nisi duobus præsentibus mis-sam celebrandam.
units.tr: That a mass is not to be celebrated unless two are present.

units.la: De Con. Dist. 1. Hoc quoque.) Hoc quoq; sta-tutum est, vt nullus presbyterorum missarum solennia celebrare præsumat, nisi duobus præ-sentibus sibique respondentibus, & ipse tertius habeatur, quia cum pluraliter ab eo dicitur, Dominus vobiscum. &c.
units.tr: De Con. Dist. 1, Hoc quoque.) It has also been decreed that no priest presume to celebrate the solemn rites of the mass unless two are present who respond to him, and that he himself be counted as the third, because when he says in the plural, "The Lord be with you," etc.

units.la: De his qui pro pecunijs una die plus quam unam faciunt missam.
units.tr: Concerning those who for money say more than one mass in one day.

units.la: De Con. Dist. 1. Sufficit.) Qui vero pro pe-cunijs aut adulationibus sæcularium una die præ-sumunt plures facere missas, nō æstimo euade-re damnationem:
units.tr: De Con. Dist. 1, Sufficit.) But those who, for money or for the flattery of laymen, presume to say several masses on one day, I do not think will escape condemnation.

units.la: Quamdiu clericis post Missam ieiu-nandum.
units.tr: How long clergy must fast after the mass.

units.la: De Con. Dist. 2. Tribus gradibus.) Si igitur mane Dominica portio editur, vsque ad sextā ieiunēt ministri, qui eam consumpserunt. Et si tertia vel quarta hora acceperint, ieiunent vsq; ad vesperas.
units.tr: De Con. Dist. 2, Tribus gradibus.) Therefore, if the portion is eaten on Sunday morning, the ministers who have consumed it are to fast until the sixth hour. And if they have received it at the third or fourth hour, they are to fast until evening.

units.la: DE EXCOMMUNICATIONE, CAPUT XIII.
units.tr: ON EXCOMMUNICATION, CHAPTER XIII.

units.la: 24.q.1. Audiuimus.) Gratian. inquit, Ligan-di nàmq; vel soluendi potestas veris non falsis sacerdotibus à Domino tradita est. Apostolis enim dicturus, quorum remiseritis peccata &c. præmisit, accipite Spiritum sanctum, vt evidenter cunctis ostenderet, eum qui Spiritum San-ctum non habet peccata nó posse tenere vel re-mittere.
units.tr: 24.q.1. Audiuimus.) Gratian says: the power of binding or loosing was handed down by the Lord to true priests, not to false ones. For when he was about to speak to the apostles, "Whose sins you remit," etc., he first said, "Receive the Holy Spirit," so as to show plainly to everyone that one who does not have the Holy Spirit cannot retain or remit sins.

units.la: Neminem excommunicandum, nisi de certa & manifesta peccati causa.
units.tr: No one is to be excommunicated except for a certain and manifest cause of sin.

units.la: 11.q.3. Nemo Episcoporum.) Nemo Episcoporum quamlibet sine certa & manifesta peccati causa, communione privet ecclesiastica. Ex Cŏcilio Meldensi.
units.tr: 11.q.3. Nemo Episcoporum.) No bishop shall deprive anyone of ecclesiastical communion without a certain and manifest cause of sin. From the Council of Meaux.

units.la: Quòd pro iniuria propria Episcopo aliquem excommunicare non liceat.
units.tr: That a bishop may not excommunicate anyone on account of an injury done to himself.

units.la: 23.q. Inter querelas.) Nil te cogitare de cœlestibus ostendis, sed terrenam te habere conversationem significas, dum pro vindicta propriæ iniuriæ (quod sacris regulis prohibetur) maledictionem anathematis inexisti.
units.tr: 23.q. Inter querelas.) You show that you think nothing of heavenly things, and that your conversation is earthly, since you have brought in the curse of anathema for the sake of revenge for your own injury, which the sacred rules forbid.

units.la: Pro leuibus causis neminem excommunicandum esse. Ex Cocilio Alvemeni.
units.tr: That no one is to be excommunicated for slight causes. From the Council of Alvernum.

units.la: II.q.
units.tr: II.q.

units.la: 11.q.3. Nullus sacerdotum.) Nullus facerdo-tum, quemquam rectæ fidei homine pro paruis & leuibus causis à communione suspendat, præter eas culpas,pro quibus antiqui patres arcere ab ecclesia iusserunt committentes.
units.tr: 11.q.3. Nullus sacerdotum.) No priest shall suspend from communion any man of sound faith for small and trivial causes, except for those faults for which the ancient fathers ordered offenders to be kept out of the Church.

units.la: Ex communicationem non nisi in impijs ratam esse.
units.tr: That excommunication is valid only against the impious.

units.la: 1.q.1. Vt euidenter.) Sicut is quem sacerdos tolerat in ecclesia tamen est extra ecclesiam, & extra corpus eius,cuius caput est Christus, fi ei ostiarius non aperuerit: Ita non ideo extra ecclesiam est,& non est de corpore, fi quis pastoris præiudicio conpellitur foris esse. Auguft.in Sermone de Remissione peccatorum.
units.tr: 1.q.1. Vt euidenter.) Just as one whom the priest tolerates in the Church is nevertheless outside the Church and outside the body of him whose head is Christ, if the doorkeeper does not open to him, so a person is not for that reason outside the Church and not of the body, if he is forced to stand outside through the prejudice of a minister. Augustine, in his sermon on the remission of sins.

units.la: Excommunicationem erga insontes non valere.
units.tr: That excommunication does not hold against the innocent.

units.la: 11.q.3. Quomodo.) Quomodo sacerdos mun-dum leprosum non facit, sic Episcopus vel presbyter non alligat eos qui insontes sunt,nec soluit noxios, sed pro officio suo,cum peccatorum varietates audierit,scit qui ligandus sit,qui sol uedus[?]. Hier. supra Malach. l.3.
units.tr: 11.q.3. Quomodo.) As a priest does not make a leper clean, so a bishop or presbyter does not bind those who are innocent, nor loose the guilty; but in discharging his office, when he has heard the varieties of sins, he knows who is to be bound and who is to be loosed. Jerome, on Malachi, book 3.

units.la: Ibidé. Auguft.de verbis Domini : Cepisti fratrem tuum habere tanquam publicanum, ligas illum in terra,sed vt iuste alliges vide,nam iniusta vincula disrumpit iustitia.
units.tr: Ibid. Augustine, on the words of the Lord: "If you have taken your brother as a publican, bind him on earth; but see that you bind justly, for justice breaks unjust chains."

units.la: Idem ad clerum Hipponensem.
units.tr: Again, to the clergy of Hippo.

units.la: homini,quod ex illa tabula vult eum delere humana ignorantia, si de libro viuentium non delet iniqua conscientia?
units.tr: ...to the man, whom human ignorance wishes to erase from that tablet, if an unjust conscience does not erase him from the book of the living?

units.la: De ijs qui innocentes excommunicantur. Hier. Origenes super Leuiticum.
units.tr: Of those who are excommunicated though innocent. Jerome; Origen on Leviticus.

units.la: 24.q.3.Siquis.) Si quis non recto iudicio eorum qui praesunt ecclesiae depellatur & foras mittatur, si ipse antea non exijt. h.si non ita egit vt mereretur exire, nihil laeditur in eo, quod non recto iudicio ab hominibus videtur expulsus. Et ita fit, vt interdum ille qui foras mittitur intus fit, & ille foris, qui intus videtur retineri.
units.tr: 24.q.3. Siquis.) If anyone is cast out and sent away from the Church by a judgment not right, of those who preside over the Church, when he himself has not gone out before, and has not acted so as to deserve to go out, nothing is harmed in him, though he seems to have been expelled by men by a judgment not right. And so it happens that sometimes he who is sent out is inside, and he who is outside seems to be kept inside.

units.la: Et mox C. Cum aliquis.) Cum aliquis exit à veritate, à timore Dei, à fide, à charitate, exit de castris ecclesiae, etiamsi per Episcopi vocem minime abijciatur, sicut è contrario aliquis non recto iudicio foras mittitur: sed si ante non exierit, id est, si non egerit, vt mereretur exire, nihil laeditur. Interdū enim qui foras mittitur, intus est, & qui foris est, intus videtur retineri.
units.tr: Et mox C. Cum aliquis.) When anyone departs from the truth, from the fear of God, from faith, from love, he departs from the camp of the Church, even if he is not thrown out by the voice of the bishop; just as, on the contrary, someone is sent out by a judgment not right. But if he has not gone out before, that is, if he has not acted so as to deserve to go out, nothing is harmed. For sometimes he who is sent out is inside, and he who is outside seems to be kept inside.

units.la: De praecipiti excommunicatione.
units.tr: On hasty excommunication.

units.la: 24.q.3.Non in perpetuum.) Multi sacerdotū culpam zelo Dei se persequi profitentur, sed dum indiscrete hoc agitur, sacrilegij facinus incurrunt, & dum praecipites quasi ad emendandum ruunt, ipsi quoque multo magis in dete-rius [?] cadunt.
units.tr: 24.q.3. Non in perpetuum.) Many priests profess that they pursue the fault of others with zeal for God; but while they do this without discernment, they incur the crime of sacrilege, and while they rush headlong, as if to amend, they themselves fall all the more into something worse.

units.la: Quod qui aliquem illicitè excommu-nicat, semetipsum non illum condemnet.
units.tr: That he who unlawfully excommunicates someone condemns himself, not the other.

units.la: Sic sonat Rubrica 24.q.3. Comperimus.
units.tr: Thus the rubric reads: 24.q.3. Comperimus.

units.la: Illum se ligandi & soluendi priuare po-testate, qui ea abutatur. Greg. homil. 27.
units.tr: That he who abuses the power of binding and loosing deprives himself of it. Gregory, Homily 27.

units.la: 11.q.3. Ipse ligandi.) Ipse ligandi atq; soluen-di se potestate priuat, qui hanc pro suis volup-tatibus, & non subditorum moribus exercet.
units.tr: 11.q.3. Ipse ligandi.) He himself deprives himself of the power of binding and loosing who exercises it for his own pleasures and not for the morals of his subjects.

units.la: Idem in registro) Priuilegium omnino me-retur amittere, qui permissa sibi abutitur pote-state.
units.tr: The same, in the Register.) He who abuses the power granted to him deserves altogether to lose the privilege.

units.la: Et aliquanto post. August.) Si quisquam fi-deliũ fuerit anathematizatus iniustè, potius ei oberit qui facit, quàm qui hanc patitur iniuriã.
units.tr: And a little later. Augustine.) If any of the faithful has been anathematized unjustly, the harm falls rather on him who does it than on him who suffers the injury.

units.la: Quòd qui contra fidem aliquid docet, neminem deijcere valeant nec damnare.
units.tr: That those who teach anything against the faith have no power to cast out or condemn anyone.

units.la: 24.q.1. Miramur. Gratianus. His authorita-tibus perspicue monstratur, quòd ex quo ali-quis contra fidem ceperit aliquid docere, nec deijcere quenquam valet, nec damnare.
units.tr: 24.q.1. Miramur. Gratian. From these authorities it is clearly shown that, from the time someone begins to teach anything against the faith, he has no power to cast out or condemn anyone.

units.la: Excommunicandos eos, qui dum sacrã fit concio, egrediuntur.
units.tr: That those who go out during a sermon are to be excommunicated.

units.la: De Con. Dist. 1. Sacerdote. Sacerdote verbũ in ecclesia faciente, qui egressus de auditorio fuerit, excommunicetur.
units.tr: De Con. Dist. 1. Sacerdote. If a priest who is preaching in the Church goes out of the hall, let him be excommunicated.

units.la: SENTENTIAE DE Excommunicandum, qui praeter mif-so ecclesiæ conuentu, ad spectacula vadit.
units.tr: Sentences concerning the one who goes to the spectacles, neglecting the assembly of the Church, to be excommunicated.

units.la: De Con. Dist. 1. Qui die.) Qui die solenni præ-termisso ecclesiæ conuentu, ad spectacula va-dit, excommunicetur.
units.tr: De Con. Dist. 1. Qui die.) Whoever, on a feast day, neglects the assembly of the Church and goes to the spectacles, let him be excommunicated.

units.la: DE RITIBVS ECCLESIA-sticis seu adiaphoris. CAPVT. XIIII.
units.tr: ON ECCLESIASTICAL RITES, OR THINGS INDIFFERENT. CHAPTER 14.

units.la: De libertate ecclesiarum circa ritus adiaphoros.
units.tr: On the liberty of churches concerning indifferent rites.

units.la: Dist. 11. In his rebus. In his rebus, de quibus nihil certe statuit diuina scriptura, mos populi Dei, & instituta maiorū pro lege tenenda sunt, & sicut præuaricatores diuinarum legum, ita contemptores ecclesiasticarum consuetudinū çoercendi sunt.
units.tr: Dist. 11. In his rebus. In those matters about which divine Scripture has laid down nothing certain, the custom of the people of God and the institutions of our forefathers are to be kept as law, and just as transgressors of divine laws are to be restrained, so too despisers of ecclesiastical customs are to be restrained.

units.la: Dist. 12. Illud.) Illud breuiter te admonen-dum puto, traditiones ecclesiasticas, præsertim QVAE FIDEI NON OFFICIANT, i-ta obseruandas, vt à maioribus traditæ sunt, nec aliquorum consuetudinem, aliorum con-trario more subuerti.
units.tr: Dist. 12. Illud. I think it should be briefly reminded to you that ecclesiastical traditions, especially those which do not harm the faith, are to be observed in the way they were handed down by our forebears, and that one group's custom is not to be overturned by another group's contrary practice.

units.la: Item. C. Nouit. Nouit fraternitas tua Rom. ecclesiæ consuetudines, in qua se meminit esse nutritam, sed mihi placet, vt siue in Romana, siue in Gallicorum, siue in qualibet ecclesia inuenisti, quòd plus omnipotenti Deo posit placere, solicitè eligas, & in Anglorum ecclesia, quæ adhuc in fidę noua est, & in constitutione præcipua quæ de multis ecclesijs colligere po-teris, infundas. Non enim pro locis res, sed pro rebus loca amanda sunt. Ex singulis ergo qui-buscunque ecclesijs, quæ pia, quæ religiosa, quę recta sunt, elige, & hæc quasi in fasciculum collecta, apud Anglorum mentes in consuetudinem depone.
units.tr: Item. C. Nouit. Your fraternity knows the customs of the Roman Church, in which you recall having been brought up. But it pleases me that, whether you have found something in the Roman, or the Gallican, or any other church, that can please almighty God more, you should carefully choose it, and infuse it into the church of the English, which is still new in the faith, and into the institutions most important that you can gather from many churches. For things are not to be loved for the sake of places, but places for the sake of things. Therefore, from each of the churches, whatever is devout, religious and right, choose these things, and, as if gathered into a bundle, lodge them in the minds of the English as custom.

units.la: Item. C. Illa autem.) Quòd alij ieiunant sabbatum, alij non, alij verò quotidie communicant corpori & sanguini Domini, alij certis diebus accipiunt, & si quid aliud huiusmodi animaduerti potest, totum hoc genus rerum liberas habet obseruationes. Quod enim neq; contra fidem Catholicam, neque contra bonos mores esse conuincitur, indifferenter est habendū, & pro eorū inter quos viuitur societate seruandum est. Augustinus idem auctoritate Ambrosij asserit, Mater mea Mediolanum me secuta inuenit ecclesiam sabbato non ieiunantem, cepit fluctuare quid ageret, tunc ego consului de hac re beatissimæ memoriæ Ambrosium Episcopum. At ille ait, cum Romam venio, sabbatum ieiuno. Cum Mediolani sum, non ieiuno. Sic & tu, ad quamcunq; forte ecclesiá veneris, eius morem serua, si cuiquam non vis esse scandalum, nec quenquam tibi. Hoc cum matri renunciassem, libenter amplexa est.
units.tr: Item. C. Illa autem. That some fast on the Sabbath and others do not, and that some receive the body and blood of the Lord every day while others receive on certain days, and whatever else of this kind may be observed, all such matters are left to free observance. For what is shown to be contrary neither to the Catholic faith nor to good morals is to be regarded as indifferent, and is to be kept in accordance with the fellowship of those among whom one lives. Augustine, likewise citing the authority of Ambrose, asserts: "My mother followed me to Milan and found the church not fasting on the Sabbath, and she began to waver over what to do. Then I consulted on this matter Ambrose, the bishop of most blessed memory. He said: 'When I come to Rome, I fast on the Sabbath; when I am in Milan, I do not fast. So you too, whatever church you happen to come to, keep its custom, if you do not wish to give offence to anyone, nor have anyone give offence to you.' When I reported this to my mother, she gladly embraced it."

units.la: De Con. Dist.4. De trina.) In vna fide nil officit sanctæ ecclesiæ consuetudo diuersa.
units.tr: De Con. Dist. 4. De trina. In the one faith, a diverse custom of the holy Church does no harm.

units.la: DE CANTV ECCLESIASTICO.
units.tr: On Church Singing.

units.la: CAPVT XV.
units.tr: Chapter 15.

units.la: Dist.23. C. Psalmista.) Cum cantores à presbyteris ordinantur, dicitur illis, Vide vt quod ore cantas, corde credas, & quod corde credis, operibus compleas.
units.tr: Dist. 23, c. Psalmista. When cantors are ordained by the presbyters, this is said to them: See that what you sing with your mouth, you believe in your heart, and what you believe in your heart, you complete in your works.

units.la: Dist.92. Cantantes.) Cantantes & psallentes in cordibus vestris Domino. Audiant hi, quibus in ecclesia est psallendi officium, Deo non voce, sed corde cantandum, nec in tragœdiarum modum guttur & fauces medicamine liniendæ sunt, vt in ecclesia theatrales moduli audiantur & cantica. Hier. in epist. ad Ephes.
units.tr: Dist. 92, Cantantes. "Sing and make melody in your hearts to the Lord." Let those hear this to whom the office of singing in the Church is entrusted: God is to be sung to not with the voice but with the heart; the throat and jaws are not to be smeared with ointment in the manner of tragic actors, so that theatrical tunes and songs are heard in the Church. Jerome, on the Epistle to the Ephesians.

units.la: Et mox C. In sancta.) Fit plerunque vt in sacro ministerio dum blanda vox quæritur, congrua vita negligatur, & Cantor minister Deum moribus stimulet, cum populum vocibus delectat.
units.tr: And soon after, C. In sancta. It often happens that, while a pleasing voice is sought in the sacred ministry, a fitting life is neglected, and the cantor, a minister, spurs the people on to God by his morals while he delights them with his voice.

units.la: Quomodo Psalmi canendi.
units.tr: How the Psalms are to be sung.

units.la: De Con. Dist.5. Non mediocriter.) Num-quid quid verborum multitudine flecti Deus ut homo potest? Non enim verbis tantùm,sed corde orandus est Deus. Quapropter melior est quin que Psalmorum decantatio cum cordis puritate ac serenitate, ac spirituali hilaritate, quàm totius Psalterij modulatio cum anxietate cordis atque tristitia.
units.tr: De Con. Dist. 5, Non mediocriter. Can God be bent by a multitude of words as a man can? For God is to be prayed to not only with words but with the heart. Therefore the chanting of five Psalms with purity and calmness of heart and with spiritual cheerfulness is better than the singing of the whole Psalter with anxiety and sadness of heart.

units.la: DE BONIS ECCLESIA-sticis. CAPVT XVI.
units.tr: DE BONIS ECCLESIASTICIS. CAPUT XVI.

units.la: De vsu auri ecclesiastici.
units.tr: On the use of church gold.

units.la: ) Aurum ecclesia habet nō ut seruet, sed ut eroget, & subueniat in necessitatibus. Quid est opus custodire,quod nihil adiu uat? An ignoramus,quantum auri atq; argenti de templo Domini Assyrij sustulerunt? Nonne melius conflat sacerdos pro alimonia pauperum,si aliqua subsidia desunt, quàm si sacrilegus contaminat & asportat hostis? Nonne dicturus est Dominus,Cur passus es tot inopes fame mori? Certè habebas aurum, unde ministrasses alimoniam. Cur tot captiui in captiuitatem ducti, nec redempti ab hoste occisi sunt? Melius fuerat ut vasa viuentium seruares quàm metallorum? His non potes responsum referre. Quid enim dices? Timui ne templo Dei ornatus deesset. Respondet, AVRVM SACRAMENTA NON QVAERVNT, neq; auro placent quæ auro nō emuntur. Ornatus sacrorum, redemptio captiuorum est, & vera illa sunt vasa pretiosa, quæ redimunt animas à morte, ille verus thesaurus est Domini, qui operatur, quod sanguis eius operatus est.
units.tr: The Church has gold not to keep it but to give it out and help in need. Why keep what does no good? Do we not know how much gold and silver the Assyrians carried off from the temple of the Lord? Would it not be better for a priest to melt down vessels for the feeding of the poor, if other resources are lacking, than for a sacrilegious enemy to defile and carry them off? Will not the Lord say, "Why did you allow so many poor to die of hunger? You certainly had gold from which you could have supplied food. Why were so many captives led into captivity and killed by the enemy without being ransomed? It would have been better for you to preserve the vessels of the living than those of metal." You cannot answer this. For what will you say? "I feared the temple of God would lack adornment." He answers: sacraments do not seek gold, and they are not pleased by things that cannot be bought with gold. The adornment of the sacred things is the ransom of captives. Those are the true precious vessels, which redeem souls from death; that is the true treasure of the Lord, which does what his blood has done.

units.la: De bonis ecclesiasticis in quatuor partes diuidendis.
units.tr: On dividing church goods into four parts.

units.la: 12.q.2. Concesso.) Redditus & oblationes fidelium in quatuor partes diuidat, quarum vnam Episcopus sibijpsi [?] retineat, alteram clericis pro officiorum suorum sedulitate distribuat, Fabricis tertiam, quartam pauperibus & peregrinis habeat fideliter erogandam, quarum rationem diuino est redditurus examini.
units.tr: 12 q.2. Concesso. The revenues and offerings of the faithful are to be divided into four parts: the bishop is to keep one for himself, distribute another to the clergy in proportion to their diligence in their offices, keep the third for the fabric, and faithfully dispense the fourth to the poor and to strangers, of whose accounts he will have to render an account to the divine judgment.

units.la: Et mox C. Quatuor.) Quatuor autem tam de redditu, quam de oblatione fidelium prout cuiuslibet ecclesiæ facultas admittit, sicut dudum rationabiliter est decretum, conuenit fieri portiones, quarum vna sit pontificis, altera clericorum, tertia pauperum, quarta est fabricis applicanda.
units.tr: And soon after, C. Quatuor. Moreover, the revenues and the offerings of the faithful, as far as the means of each church allow, as was reasonably decreed long ago, ought to be made into portions: one for the bishop, another for the clergy, a third for the poor, and the fourth to be applied to the fabric.

units.la: Idem mox C. Mos est.
units.tr: Likewise soon after, C. Mos est.

units.la: De his qui bona ecclesiastica in milites, aut seruitores, vel consanguineos conferunt.
units.tr: On those who confer church goods on soldiers, servants, or kinsmen.

units.la: Peruenit ad nos fama fini-stra, quod quidam Episcoporum, non sacerdotibus proprie diocesis decimas atque Christia-norum oblationes conferunt, sed potius laicalibus personis, militum videlicet siue seruito-rum, vel (quod grauius est) etiam consanguineis. Unde si quis a modo Episcopus inuentus fuerit huius praecepti diuini transgressor, inter maximos haereticos & antichristos non minus habeatur. Et sicut Nicaena Synodus de Simonia cis censuit, & qui recipiunt ab eo laici, & qui dat Episcopus, siue pretio siue beneficio, aeterni incendij ignibus deputentur.
units.tr: A sinister report has reached us that certain bishops confer the tithes and the offerings of Christians not on the priests of their own diocese but on lay persons, namely soldiers or servants, or (what is more grievous) even on kinsmen. Therefore, if any bishop is henceforth found to be a transgressor of this divine precept, let him be regarded as no less than the greatest heretics and antichrists. And just as the Nicene Synod decided concerning simoniacs, both the laymen who receive from him and the bishop who gives, whether for a price or for a favour, are to be consigned to the fires of eternal burning.

units.la: De ornatu templorum. Hieronymus ad Nepotianum.
units.tr: On the adornment of churches. Jerome to Nepotian.

units.la: Multi aedificant parietes, & columnas ecclesiae subtrahunt, marmora nitent, auro laquearia splendent, gemmis altare distinguitur, & ministrorum Christi nulla est electio. Neq; vero mihi aliquis opponat diues in Iudaea templum, mensam, lucernas, thuribula, patellas, cyphos, mortariola, & caetera ex auro fabricata. Tunc enim haec probabatur a Domino, quando sacerdotes hostias immolabant, & sanguis pecudum erat remissio peccatorum. Quanquam haec omnia praecesserint in figura. Scriptum est autem propter nos, in quos fines saeculorum deuenerunt. Nunc vero cum paupertatem domus suæ pauper Dominus dedi-cauit, portemus crucem, & delitias lutum pu-temus.
units.tr: Many build walls and take away the columns from the church; marbles gleam, ceilings shine with gold, the altar is set off with gems, and there is no choice of Christ's ministers. Nor let anyone object to me that in Judaea there was a rich temple, with its table, lamps, censers, dishes, cups, little mortars, and other things made of gold. For those things were approved by the Lord at a time when priests offered sacrifices and the blood of beasts was the forgiveness of sins. Yet all these things went before in figure. But it is written for our sake, upon whom the ends of the ages have come. Now, since the poor Lord dedicated the poverty of his house, let us carry the cross and count luxuries as mud.

units.la: De vasis ecclesiasticis.
units.tr: On ecclesiastical vessels.

units.la: De Con. Dist.1. Vasa.) Bonifacius martyr & Episcopus interrogatus si liceret in vasculis ligneis Sacramenta conficere, respondit, quon-dam sacerdotes non aureis sed ligneis calicibus utebantur. Zepherinus sedecimus Romanus Episcopus patenis vitreis missas celebrari constituit. Deinde Urbanus Papa omnia ministeria sacra fecit argentea, &c.
units.tr: De Con. Dist.1. Vasa. Boniface, martyr and bishop, when asked whether it was lawful to consecrate the sacraments in wooden vessels, replied that in former times priests used chalices not of gold but of wood. Zephyrinus, the sixteenth Roman bishop, ordained that masses be celebrated with glass patens. Then Pope Urban made all the sacred vessels of silver, and so on.

units.la: Et mox C. Ut calix.) Si quis autem tam pauper est, saltem vel stanneum habeat calicem.
units.tr: And soon after, C. Ut calix. But if anyone is so poor, let him at least have a chalice of tin.

units.la: DE MAGISTRATV. CAPVT XVII.
units.tr: DE MAGISTRATV. CAPVT XVII.

units.la: Magistratibus tributa ab ecclesiasticis non neganda. Ambrosius ad Auxent.
units.tr: Taxes owed to the magistrates are not to be denied by churchmen. Ambrose, to Auxentius.

units.la: 11.q.1. Si tributum.) Si tributum petit Imperator, non ei negamus, agri ecclesiæ soluant tributum. Si agros desiderat Imperator, potestate habet vendicandorum, tollat eos, si libitum est. Imperatori non dono, sed non nego.
units.tr: 11 q. 1. If tribute.) If the Emperor demands tribute, we do not deny it to him: the fields of the Church pay tribute. If the Emperor desires the fields, he has the power of claiming them; let him take them, if it pleases him. I do not give to the Emperor, but I do not deny him.

units.la: Et mox idem. Magnum quidem est & speciale documentum, quo Christiani viri subli-mioribus potestatibus docetur debere esse subiecti, ne quis constitutionem terreni regis putet esse soluendam. Si enim censum filius Dei soluit, quis tu tantus es, qui putas esse non soluendum? Ité Apostolus: Omnis anima sublimioribus potestatibus subdita fit. Item Petrus Apostolus generaliter omnibus fidelibus scribit, Estote subditi dominis vestris siue regi quasi præ cellenti, siue ducibus tanquam ab eo missis, ad vindictam malefactorum, laudem verò bonorum.
units.tr: And soon after, the same author: This is indeed a great and special lesson, by which Christian men are taught that they ought to be subject to the higher powers, lest anyone think that the levy of an earthly king is not to be paid. For if the Son of God paid the tax, who are you, so great a person, that you think it should not be paid? Likewise the Apostle: Every soul is made subject to the higher powers. Likewise the Apostle Peter writes generally to all the faithful: Be subject to your masters, whether to the king as preeminent, or to governors as sent by him, for the punishment of evildoers but the praise of the good.

units.la: DE IVREIVRANDO ET votis. CAPVT XVIII. Non iurandum esse per creaturas.
units.tr: On Oaths and Vows. Chapter XVIII. That one must not swear by creatures.

units.la: 22.q.1.Et iurabunt.) Quòd per mortuos iuret omnis idololatra. Hier.super Ierem.lib.1.
units.tr: 22 q.1, Et iurabunt. That every idolater swears by the dead. Jerome, on Jeremiah, book 1.

units.la: Item C.Considera.) Considera quòd saluatos non per Deum iurare prohibuit, sed per cœlum & terram, etiam per Hierosolymam, & per caput tuum. Hier. super Matth.lib.1.
units.tr: Likewise, C. Considera. Consider that the Saviour forbade swearing not by God but by heaven and earth, also by Jerusalem, and by your head. Jerome, on Matthew, book 1.

units.la: Et mox ex Concilio Carthaginensi IIII. C. Clericum per creaturas iurantem, acerrimè esse obiurgandum, si perstiterit in vitio, excommunicandum decernimus.
units.tr: And shortly after, from the Council of Carthage IV, canon: We decree that a clergyman who swears by creatures is to be sharply rebuked, and if he persists in the fault, excommunicated.

units.la: Et mox iterum C. Si quis.) Et si quis per creaturas iurauerit, acerrimè castigetur & iuxta id quod Synodus dijudicauerit, pœniteat.
units.tr: And shortly after again, canon Si quis. And if anyone has sworn by creatures, let him be sharply punished, and let him do penance according to what the Synod decides.

units.la: Si quis autem talem hominem non manifestá-uerit,non est dubium,quin diuina condemnatione coerceatur. Sed si Episcopus ista emendare neglexerit,acerrimè corripiatur.
units.tr: But if anyone has not reported such a man, there is no doubt that he is restrained by divine condemnation. But if a bishop has neglected to correct these things, let him be sharply reproved.

units.la: Et mox C.Monet te. Augustinus ad Publico jam,quod bis peccet, qui per falsos Deos juret, & fidem quoq; non servet.
units.tr: And shortly after, canon Monet te. Augustine to Publicola: that he sins twice who swears by false gods and also fails to keep faith.

units.la: Ibidem. Alia quæstio est,vtrum non peccet, qui per falsos Deos sibi jurari facit, quia ille qui ei jurat, jurat per falsos Deos quos colit. Cui quæstioni possunt illa testimonia suffragari,quę ipse commemorasti de Laban & Abimelech, si tamen Abimelech per Deos suos jurauit, sicut Laban per Deum Nahor. Sicut etiam cum in libro Machabæorum Romani legantur pacem firmasse cum Judæis, intelligendi sunt jurasse per falsos Deos, sicut & Judæi juraverunt per Deum verum. Sic etiam & de juramento quod fit per creaturas,intelligendū est,quod IPSVM QVIDEM JVRARE PER CREATVRAS MALVM EST, QVIA A DEO PROHIBITVM,sed servare quod juratur, bonum est, ut evitetur peccatum mendacij & dolositatis.
units.tr: In the same place. Another question is whether he does not sin who causes an oath to be sworn to him by false gods, since he who swears to him swears by the false gods whom he worships. The testimonies you yourself cited about Laban and Abimelech may support this question, if indeed Abimelech swore by his gods, just as Laban swore by the God of Nahor. Likewise, when the Maccabees' book tells that the Romans confirmed a peace with the Jews, they must be understood to have sworn by false gods, just as the Jews swore by the true God. So also concerning the oath that is made by creatures, it must be understood that TO SWEAR BY CREATURES IS IN ITSELF EVIL, BECAUSE IT IS FORBIDDEN BY GOD, but to keep what has been sworn is good, so that the sin of lying and deceit may be avoided.

units.la: Et mox ibidem. Deus autem per creaturas jurare prohibuit, ne vel more gentiliū aliquod numen Deitatis creaturis inesse crederetur,vel ne creaturas contemptibiles judicando,per eas promissa pro nihilo duceremus. Maius esse per Deum, quàm per Euangelium iurare.
units.tr: And shortly after, in the same place. But God forbade swearing by creatures, lest either, after the manner of the Gentiles, some divine power be believed to dwell in creatures, or lest, by judging creatures contemptible, we should count promises made through them as nothing. It is greater to swear by God than by the Gospel.

units.la: 22.q.1. Si aliqua. Si aliqua causa fuerit, modi cū videtur facere, qui iurat per Deū, qui autem per Euangelium, maius aliquid fecisse videtur; quibus dicendum est, Stulti, propter Deum scripturæ sanctæ sunt, nō Deus propter scripturas.
units.tr: 22 q.1, Si aliqua. If there is some reason why he who swears by God seems to act in one way, and he who swears by the Gospel seems to have done something greater, to these it must be said: Fools! The holy Scriptures exist on account of God, not God on account of the Scriptures.

units.la: Illicita iuramenta & vota non esse servanda.
units.tr: That unlawful oaths and vows are not to be kept.

units.la: 22.q.4. Multis hoc agitur Capitibus, & inducuntur diuersa Herodis & Dauidis exempla. Ibidem etiam hæc testimonia citantur.
units.tr: 22 q.4. This is treated in many chapters, and various examples of Herod and David are brought forward. In the same place these testimonies are also cited.

units.la: Isidorus in Synonymis lib. 2. In malis pro-missis resciinde[?] fidem, in turpi voto muta de-cretum, quod incautè vouisti, ne facias, impia est promissio, quæ scelere adimpletur.
units.tr: Isidore, in the Synonyma, book 2: In bad promises, rescind your pledge; in a shameful vow, change your decision. What you have rashly vowed, do not do; an impious promise is one that is fulfilled by crime.

units.la: Ambrosius de Officijs: Melius est non vouere, quàm vouere id, quod sibi is cui promittitur nolit exolui.
units.tr: Ambrose, On Duties: It is better not to vow than to vow what the one to whom it is promised does not wish to be paid.

units.la: August. Magnæ sapientiæ est reuocare ho-minem, quod malè locutus est.
units.tr: Augustine: It is the mark of great wisdom to recall a man from what he has said badly.

units.la: Concil. Elibertinum. Diffinitio incauta lau-dabiliter soluenda est, nec est prævaricatio, sed temeritatis emendatio.
units.tr: Council of Elvira: A rash definition is to be laudably dissolved; this is not prevarication but the correction of rashness.

units.la: August. Mulier si fide coniugali violata fi-dem feruet adultero, vtique mala est, porrò si eam flagitij pœnitéat, & ad castitatem redien[?] coniugalem, pacta ac placita adulterina rescin-dat, miror si eam fidei violatricem vel ipse ad-ulter putabit.
units.tr: Augustine: If a wife, having violated conjugal faith, burns with love for an adulterer, she is certainly wicked; but if she repents of the crime and returns to marital chastity, and annuls the adulterous pacts and agreements, I would be surprised if even the adulterer himself thought her a violator of faith.

units.la: DE HAERETICIS. CAPVT XIX.
units.tr: ON HERETICS. CHAPTER XIX.

units.la: 24.q.3. Hæresis.) Quicunq; igitur aliter scripturam intelligit, quàm sensus Spiritus sancti flagitat, à quo scripta est, licet ab ecclesia non recesserit, tamen hæreticus appellari potest.
units.tr: 24 q. 3, Heresy. Whoever therefore understands Scripture otherwise than the sense of the Holy Spirit, by whom it was written requires, may be called a heretic, even if he has not departed from the Church.

units.la: Angelos colere hæresim esse.
units.tr: That the worship of angels is heresy.

units.la: 24.q.3. In Catalogo hæreticorum recensen-tur etiam Angelici, qui ideo sic dicti sunt, quia angelos colebant.
units.tr: 24 q. 3. Among the catalogue of heretics are also listed the Angelici, who were so called because they worshipped angels.

units.la: DE PRIMATV IN ECCLE-sia, & de Papa. CAPVT XX.
units.tr: ON THE PRIMACY IN THE CHURCH, AND ON THE POPE. CHAPTER XX.

units.la: Omnes Apostolos eodem honore & eadem potestate præditos fuisse. Cyprianus Papa.
units.tr: That all the Apostles were endowed with the same honour and the same power. Cyprian, Pope.

units.la: 22.q.1. Loquitur.) Hoc vtiq; erant cæteri A-postoli,quod Petrus fuit,pari consortio præditi & honoris & potestatis.
units.tr: 22.q.1. He says: Indeed the other Apostles had the same fellowship of honour and power that Peter had.

units.la: Paulum Petro non fuisse imparem.
units.tr: That Paul was not inferior to Peter.

units.la: Hier.de Paulo super epistolam ad Gal.
units.tr: Jerome, on Paul's Epistle to the Galatians.

units.la: 2 q.7. Paulus.) Paulus Petrum reprehendit, quòd non auderet, nisi se non imparem sciret. Hic addit Gratianus de suo, Hoc non de officio ecclesiasticæ dignitatis, sed de puritate vitæ, & sanctitate conuersationis intelligitur. Solus e-nim Petrus inter Apostolos primatum gerebat. Hoc scilicet Hieronymus ignorauit.
units.tr: 2 q.7, Paul. Paul rebuked Peter, and he would not have dared to do so unless he knew himself not to be inferior. Here Gratian adds of his own: "This is to be understood not of the office of ecclesiastical dignity but of the purity of life and holiness of conduct. For Peter alone among the Apostles held the primacy." Jerome, of course, did not know this.

units.la: Et mox. Ambrosius. Beati Petrus & Paulus eminent inter vniuersos Apostolos, & speciali quadam prærogatiua præcellunt, verum inter ipsos quis cui præponatur incertum est. Puto enim illos æquales esse meritis, qui æquales sunt passione, & similí eos fidei deuotione vixisse, quos simul videmus ad martyrij gloriam peruenisse. Non enim sine causa factum putamus, quòd vna die passi sunt, vno loco, sub vno per-secutore. Vna die, vt ad Christum pariter per-uenirent. In vno loco, ne alteri Roma deesset. Sub vno persecutore, vt æqualis crudelitas v-trofq; costringeret. Dies ergo pro merito, locus pro gloria, persecutor decretus est pro virtute.
units.tr: And soon after, Ambrose: "The blessed Peter and Paul stand out among all the Apostles and excel by a certain special prerogative. Yet which of the two is placed over the other is uncertain. For I think those are equal in merit who are equal in suffering, and who lived with a similar devotion of faith, and whom we see reached the glory of martyrdom together. Nor do we think it happened without reason that they suffered on one day, in one place, under one persecutor. On one day, so that they might come to Christ together. In one place, so that Rome might not lack one of them. Under one persecutor, so that equal cruelty might bind them both. Thus the day was decreed for their merit, the place for their glory, the persecutor for their virtue."

units.la: Primitiuam ecclesiam nullos ordines habuisse præter diaconatum & presbyteratum. Urbanus Papa.
units.tr: That the primitive Church had no orders besides the diaconate and the presbyterate. Urban, Pope.

units.la: Dist. 6. C. Nullus.) Nullus in Episcopatum eligatur, nisi in sacris ordinibus religiosè viuens fuerit inuentus. Sacros autem ordines dicimus diaconatum & presbyteratum, Hos fiquidē so-los primitiua legitur habuisse ecclesia.
units.tr: Dist. 6, C. Nullus. No one is to be elected to the episcopate unless he is found living devoutly in the sacred orders. We call the sacred orders the diaconate and the presbyterate, for these alone are read to have been held by the primitive Church.

units.la: Episcopos & presbyteros olim idem & eiusdem dignitatis fuisse.
units.tr: That bishops and presbyters were formerly the same and of the same dignity.

units.la: Dist.21.Cleros.) Apud veteres idem Episcopi & presbyteri fuerunt.
units.tr: Dist. 21, Clerici. Among the ancients, bishops and presbyters were the same.

units.la: Dist.91.C.Legimus.) Ex Hieronymo ad E-uagrium vel Eugenium Episcopū multis pro-batur, quòd Episcopi & presbyteri eiusdē olim fuerint dignitatis. Postea sequitur: Quòd autē postea vnus electus est, qui cæteris præponere-tur, in schismatis remedium factum est, ne vnus quisq; ad se trahēs ecclesiam Christi rumperet.
units.tr: Dist. 91, C. Legimus. From Jerome to Evagrius, or Eugenius, the bishop, it is proved by many arguments that bishops and presbyters were formerly of the same dignity. He then goes on: "But that afterwards one was chosen to be placed over the rest was done as a remedy for schism, lest each one, drawing the Church of Christ to himself, should tear it apart."

units.la: Dist.95. C.Olim) Hier. super epistolam ad Titum. Olim idem erat presbyter qui & Episcopus, & antequā diaboli instinctu studia vel schismata in religione fieret, & diceretur in populis, Ego sum Pauli, ego sum Apollo, ego autē Ce-phę, communi presbyterorum consilio ecclesię gubernabantur. Postquā autem vnusquisq; eos quos baptizauerat suos esse putabat nō Christi, in toto orbe decretum est, vt vnus de presbyteris superponeretur omnibus, & schismatum semina tollerentur.
units.tr: Dist. 95, C. Olim. Jerome, on the Epistle to Titus: "Formerly the presbyter and the bishop were the same. Before factions and schisms arose in religion at the prompting of the devil, and people said, 'I am of Paul, I am of Apollos, but I am of Cephas,' the Church was governed by the common counsel of the presbyters. But after each one began to think that those whom he had baptized were his own and not Christ's, it was decreed throughout the whole world that one of the presbyters should be set over all the others, and the seeds of schism should be removed."

units.la: Et paulò post: Sicut ergo presbyteri sciunt se ex ecclesiæ consuetudine ei qui sibi præpositus fuerit esse subiectos, ita episcopi nouerint se magis consuetudine quā dispensationis Dominicę veritate presbyteris esse maiores, & in communi debere ecclesia regere.
units.tr: And a little later: "Just as presbyters know that, by the custom of the Church, they are subject to the one who has been set over them, so bishops should understand that they are greater than presbyters more by custom than by the truth of the Lord's arrangement, and that they ought to rule the Church in common."

units.la: Parem omnium ecclesiarum & Episcoporum esse dignitatem. Hiero.
units.tr: That the dignity of all churches and bishops is equal. Jerome.

units.la: Dist.93. C. Legimus.) Nec altera Romanæ vrbis ecclesia, altera totius orbis æstimanda est, & Galliæ & Britanniæ. Nam & Aphrica & Persis, & Oriens, & India, & omnes barbaræ nationes, vnum Christum adorant, vnam obseruant regulam veritatis. Si autè auctoritas quæreretur, orbis maior est vrbe. Vbicunq; fuerit Episcopus, siue Romæ, siue Eugubij, siue Constantinopoli, siue Regij, siue Alexandriæ, siue Thebis, siue Guarmatiæ, eiusdem meriti est, eiusdem & sacerdotij. Potentia diuitiarum, & paupertatis humilitas, vel sublimiorem vel inferiorem Episcopum non facit.
units.tr: Dist. 93, C. Legimus. The church of the city of Rome is not to be esteemed one thing, and the church of the whole world, of Gaul and Britain, another. For Africa, Persia, the East, India and all the barbarian nations worship one Christ and observe one rule of truth. If authority is sought, the world is greater than the city. Wherever a bishop is, whether at Rome, at Eugubium, at Constantinople, at Rhegium, at Alexandria, at Thebes, or at Guarmatia, he is of the same worth and the same priesthood. The power of riches and the humility of poverty do not make a bishop higher or lower.

units.la: Vnicuique ecclesiæ suus honor seruetur.
units.tr: Let each church keep its own honour.

units.la: Ex concilio Niceno.
units.tr: From the Council of Nicaea.

units.la: Dist.63. C. Mos antiquus.) Mos antiquus per duret in Ægypto vel Lybia & Pentapoli, vt Alexandrinus Episcopus horum omnium habeat potestatem, quandoquidem & Romano Episcopo pariliis est mos. Similiter aut apud Antiochiam & cæteras prouincias, honor suus vnicuique seruetur ecclesiæ.
units.tr: Dist. 63, C. Mos antiquus. Let the ancient custom endure in Egypt, Libya and Pentapolis, that the bishop of Alexandria have authority over all these, since the custom is similar for the bishop of Rome too. Likewise at Antioch and in the other provinces, let each church keep its own honour.

units.la: De primatu in ecclesia. Ex Concilio Aphricano.
units.tr: On the primacy in the Church. From the African Council.

units.la: Dist.99. C. Primæ.) Primæ sedis Episcopus, non appelletur princeps sacerdotum, vel summus sacerdos, aut aliquid huiusmodi, sed tantū primæ sedis Episcopus.
units.tr: Dist. 99, C. Primae. The bishop of the first see is not to be called prince of priests, or chief priest, or anything of the kind, but only bishop of the first see.

units.la: Vniuersalis aūt, nec etiā Romanus Pontifex appelletur. Vnde Pelagius omnibus Episcopis.
units.tr: Nor is he to be called universal, nor even the Roman Pontiff. Hence Pelagius to all bishops:

units.la: Nullus Patriarcharum vniuersalitatis vocabulo vnquam vtatur, quia si vnus patriarcha vniuersalis dicitur, patriarcharum nomen cæteris derogatur. Sed absit hoc à fidelibus, hoc sibi velle quempiá arripere, vnde honorem fratrū suorum imminuere ex quantulacunq; parte vi deatur. Quapropter charitas vestra neminē vn quam etiam suis in epistolis vniuersalem nomi net, ne sibi debitum subtrahat, cum alteri honorem infert indebitum.
units.tr: No patriarch shall ever use the title of universality, because if one patriarch is called universal, the name of patriarch is taken away from the rest. But far be it from the faithful to seize upon this, wishing to diminish the honour of their brothers in any small degree. Therefore your charity should never call anyone universal, even in your letters, lest it withhold what is due to himself when it gives undue honour to another.

units.la: Item Gregorius Eulogio patriarchæ Alexan drino. Ecce in præfatione epistolæ quā ad me ipsum, qui prohibui direxistis, superbæ appella tionis verbū, Vniuersalem mePapam dicentes, imprimere curastis. Quod (peto) mihi dulcisi ma sanctitas vestra vltra non faciat, quia vobis subtrahitur, quod alteri plusquam ratio exigit, præbetur. Ego non verbis quæro prosperari, sed moribus, nec honorē esse deputo, in quo fratres meos honorem suum perdere cognosco. Meus namq; est honor vniuersalis ecclesiæ, meus honor est fratrū meorum solidus vigor. Tunc ego honorahonoratus sum,cū singulis quibusq; honor debitus nō negatur. Si enim vniuersalem Papam vestra sanctitas dicit, negat se hoc esse quod me fatetur vniuersum. Sed absit hoc,recedát verba quæ veritatem inflant, & charitatem vulnerát.
units.tr: Likewise Gregory to Eulogius, patriarch of Alexandria: "Behold, in the preface of the letter which you sent to me, who forbade it, you have taken care to insert the proud expression, calling me universal pope. I beg that your holiness no longer do this, because what is given to another more than reason requires is taken away from you. I do not seek to prosper in words but in conduct, nor do I count it honour when I know my brothers lose their honour. For my honour is the honour of the universal Church; my honour is the firm strength of my brothers. Then am I truly honoured, when due honour is not denied to each one. For if your holiness calls me universal Pope, it denies itself to be what it confesses me to be, universal. But far be this; let the words which puff up the truth and wound charity depart."

units.la: Primatum quærentem in terra, confusionem inuenturum in cœlo, nec inter seruos Christi numerandum. Chrysost.
units.tr: He who seeks primacy on earth will find confusion in heaven, and is not to be numbered among the servants of Christ. Chrysostom.

units.la: Dist.4.C. Multi.) Quicunq; desiderauerit primatum in terra,inueniet cōfusionem in cœ-lo, nec inter seruos Christi cōputabitur, qui de primatu tractauerit. Nec vnusquisq; eorum su-stinet, quomodo alijs maior appareat,sed quo-modo omnibus inferior videatur. Quoniam nō qui maior fuerit in honore inter homines, ille est iustior,sed qui fuerit iustior,ille maior.
units.tr: Dist. 4, C. Multi. Whoever desires primacy on earth will find confusion in heaven, and whoever has discussed primacy will not be counted among the servants of Christ. Nor should any of them endeavour to appear greater than the others, but to seem inferior to all. For he who is greater in honour among men is not the more righteous; he who is more righteous is the greater.

units.la: Episcopi sacerdotes se sciant esse non dominos. Ex Hier. ad Nepotianum.
units.tr: Bishops should know that they are priests, not lords. From Jerome to Nepotianus.

units.la: Dist.59.C. Esto subiectus.) Esto subiectus pon-tifici tuo,& quasi parentem animæ ama, sed EPISCOPI SACERDOTES SE SCIANT ESSE NON DOMINOS.
units.tr: Dist. 59, C. Esto subiectus. Be subject to your pontiff, and love him as the parent of your soul, but BISHOPS SHOULD KNOW THEMSELVES TO BE PRIESTS, NOT LORDS.

units.la: Episcopi ordinantur, non vt præsint, sed vt prosint. Leo.
units.tr: Bishops are ordained not only to rule but to serve. Leo.

units.la: 1.q.1. Si qui Episcopi.) Non solùm vt præsint, sed etiam vt prosint sacerdotium datur.
units.tr: 1.q.1, Si qui episcopi. The priesthood is given not only that men may preside, but also that they may serve.

units.la: Sacerdotes præeminere debere sanctitate.
units.tr: Priests should excel in holiness.

units.la: Ibidem mox.C. Hiquofcunq.)[?] Qui ad hoc eliguntur ut cæteris præsint, sicut ordinantur dignitate, sic præeminere debent sanctitate.'A-lioquin cur cæteris præferuntur, qui nulla me-ritorum gratia à cæteris assumuntur?
units.tr: Ibid., soon after, C. Quicunque. Those who are chosen to preside over others should excel in holiness just as they are ordained in dignity. Otherwise, why are they preferred to others, when they are taken up above the rest by no grace of merit?

units.la: Quomodo Apostolorum vicarij debeamus esse.
units.tr: How the vicars of the Apostles ought to be.

units.la: Dist.35.C.Ecclesiæ principes.) Si in Apostolorum loco sumus, non solum sermonem eorum imitemur, sed etiam conversationem & absti-nentiam.
units.tr: Dist. 35, C. Ecclesiae principes. If we stand in the place of the Apostles, we should imitate not only their teaching but also their manner of life and their self-restraint.

units.la: Papam cum suis ab Imperatore corri-gi debere, Leo IIII, Ludovico Augusto.
units.tr: That the Pope and his followers ought to be corrected by the Emperor: Leo IV to Louis Augustus.

units.la: 2.q.7.Nos si.) Nos si incompetenter aliquid egimus, & in subditis iustæ legis tramitem non conservavimus, vestro ac missorum[?] vestrorum cunctavolumus emendare iudicio. Quoniam si nos qui aliena[?] debemus corrigere peccata peiora committimus, certè non veritatis discipuli, sed (quod dolentes dicimus) erimus præ cæteris erroris magistri.
units.tr: 2. q. 7, Nos si. If we have acted improperly in any matter, and have not kept to the path of just law in dealing with our subjects, we are willing to be corrected by your judgment and that of your envoys. For if we, who ought to correct the sins of others, commit worse ones, we shall certainly not be disciples of the truth but, (as we say with sorrow) we shall be masters of error beyond all others.

units.la: Papam non habere omnia iura in pe-ctore.
units.tr: That the Pope does not have all rights in his breast.

units.la: Dist.23. C.Præterea.) In Glossa marginali, ubi Papa Nicolaus dicit, Nisi nos fallat obliuio, Glossator addit, Non ergo Papa habet omnia iura in pectore suo.
units.tr: Dist. 23, C. Praeterea. In the marginal gloss, where Pope Nicholas says, "Unless forgetfulness deceives us," the glossator adds: "Therefore the Pope does not have all rights in his breast."

units.la: DE ELECTIONIBVS ET Ordinationibus.
units.tr: ON ELECTIONS AND ORDINATIONS.

units.la: CAPVT XXI.
units.tr: CHAPTER XXI.

units.la: Non consecrari debere, nisi Canonicè electum. Et si hoc non fiat, & consecrantem & consecratum absque recuperationis spe deponendos. Calixtus Papa.
units.tr: That no one should be consecrated unless he has been canonically elected. And if this is not done, both the consecrator and the one consecrated are to be deposed without hope of restoration. Pope Calixtus.

units.la: Dist.62. C. Nullus.) Nullus in Episcopum nisi Canonicè electum consecret. Quod si præsumptum fuerit, consecrans & consecratus absque recuperationis spe deponantur.
units.tr: Dist. 62, C. Nullus.) No one shall consecrate a bishop unless he has been canonically elected. But if this is presumed to have been done, both the consecrator and the consecrated are to be deposed without hope of restoration.

units.la: Ius ordinandi amittere eos, qui indignos consecrant. Leo Papa.
units.tr: Those who consecrate unworthy men lose the right of ordaining. Pope Leo.

units.la: 25.q.2.Si qui Episcopi.) Si qui Episcopi talem consecrauerint sacerdotem, qualem esse nō licet, etiamsi aliquo modo damnum proprij honoris euaserint, ordinationis ius ulterius non habebunt, nec unquam eidem sacramento intererunt, quod neglecto diuino iudicio, immeritò præstiterunt.
units.tr: 25 q. 2, Si qui Episcopi.) If any bishops have consecrated as priest a man who ought not to be one, then even though they have in some way escaped the loss of their own dignity, they shall no longer have the right of ordination, nor shall they ever again take part in that sacrament, since they granted it, having disregarded the divine judgment.

units.la: De promotione indignorum
units.tr: On the promotion of the unworthy

units.la: Dist.61.) Postquam multa de irrepræhensibilitate ministrorum, & quales eligi debeant, dictum est, sequitur inter alia.
units.tr: Dist. 61.) After much has been said about the blameless character of ministers and about the kind of men who ought to be chosen, the following follows among other things.

units.la: Vnde Leo Episcopis, C. Miramur.)
