Miramur tantum apud vos per occupationem temporis impacati, aut ambientium praesumptioné, aut tumultum voluisse popularé, vt indignis quibuslibet, & longè extra sacerdotale meritum constitutis, pastorale fastigium, & gubernatio ecclesiae crederetur. Non enim est hoc consulere populo sed nocere, nec praestare regimen, sed augere discrimen. Integritas enim praesidentium, salus est subditorum, & vbi est incolumitas obedientiae, ibi sana est forma doctrinae.
units.tr: Leo to the bishops, C. Miramur.) We are astonished that among you, through the neglect of time, or the presumption of ambitious men, or the desire of a popular tumult, it has been allowed that the pastoral office and the governance of the Church should be entrusted to unworthy men, placed far beyond any priestly merit. For this is not to care for the people but to harm them, not to provide government but to increase danger. For the integrity of those who preside is the safety of those under them, and where the soundness of obedience is, there also is the sound form of doctrine.

units.la: Qui non debeant ad ordines sacros ad mitti.
units.tr: Who ought not to be sent to the holy orders.

units.la: Dist.33. C. Maritum.) Inter alia. Neque illos qui vsuras accepisse cōuincuntur, aut in scena lusisse noscuntur, nec eum qui publica poenitentia mortalia crimina defleuit, neque illum qui in furiam aliquando versus insaniuit, vel afflictione diabolica vexatus est, neq; eum qui per emptionem ad imitationem Simonis Magi pecuniam obtulerit.
units.tr: Dist. 33, C. Maritum.) Among other things: neither those convicted of having taken usury, nor those known to have played games on the stage, nor one who has wept over mortal sins through public penance, nor one who at some time has gone mad into a frenzy or has been afflicted and vexed by a diabolical affliction, nor one who has offered money by purchase in imitation of Simon Magus.

units.la: Milites clericos fieri non posse. Inno-centius.
units.tr: Soldiers cannot be made clerics. Innocent.

units.la: Dist.50. C. Si quis.) Si quis, post remissionem peccatorum cingulum militiae saecularis habuerit, ad clericatum omnino admitti non debet.
units.tr: Dist. 50, C. Si quis.) If anyone, after the forgiveness of sins, has borne the belt of secular military service, he must in no way be admitted to the clergy.

units.la: De ambitione, qua ex laicis subito fi-
units.tr: On the ambition by which laymen are suddenly made

units.la: unt sacerdotes et Episco. Gregor. Brunnichildi reginæ Francorum.
units.tr: priests and bishops. Gregory, to Brunhild, queen of the Franks.

units.la: Dist. 61. C. Sacerdotale.) Sacerdotale officiū vestris in partibus, in tanta, sicut didicimus, est ambitione perductum, vt sacerdotes subito, quod nimis graue est, ex laicis ordinentur.
units.tr: Dist. 61, C. Sacerdotale.) In your regions, as we have learned, the office of priest has been brought to such a pitch of ambition that men are suddenly ordained priests out of the laity, which is very grievous.

units.la: Seculo implicatos, in clerum non recipiendos esse.
units.tr: Those entangled in worldly affairs are not to be received into the clergy.

units.la: Dist. 53. C. Lege.) Gregor. li. 8. Registri, de Lege Mauritij Augusti, inter alia. Hi qui seculi actionib. implicati sunt, in clero ecclesiæ, præpostere suscipiendi non sunt, quia dum in ecclesiastico habitu non dissimiliter quàm prius vixerant, viuunt, nequaquam student seculum fugere sed mutare.
units.tr: Dist. 53, C. Lege.) Gregory, Register book 8, concerning the law of the Emperor Maurice, among other things: Those who are entangled in the affairs of the world must not be received into the clergy of the Church out of due order, because, while living in ecclesiastical dress no differently than before, they do not strive at all to flee the world but to change its outward appearance.

units.la: Illiteratos non debere ordinari.
units.tr: That the unlettered ought not to be ordained.

units.la: Vide Dist. 55. multis locis.
units.tr: See Dist. 55, in many places.

units.la: Non debere ad sacerdotium promoueri, ecclesiasticis disciplinis prius non imbutos. Zosimus. Papa.
units.tr: That those not previously trained in ecclesiastical disciplines ought not to be promoted to the priesthood. Pope Zosimus.

units.la: Dist. 59. C. Qui ecclesiastici.) Qui ecclesiastici-eis disciplinis per ordinem nō est imbutus, nec temporum approbatione, diuinis stipendijs eruditus, nequaquam ad summum sacerdotium ecclesiæ aspirare vel præsumere debet, &c. non solum in eo ambitio inefficax habeatur, verum ordinatores eius careatur eo ordine, quem contra praecepta crediderant praesumendum.
units.tr: Dist. 59, C. Qui ecclesiastici.) Whoever has not been trained in ecclesiastical disciplines in due order, nor instructed in divine services through the proof of time, must by no means aspire to or presume upon the highest priesthood of the Church, etc. Not only is ambition in this matter held to be ineffective, but its ordainers are also to be deprived of that office which they had believed, contrary to the precepts, could be presumed upon.

units.la: Item ibidé. C. Hoc ad nos peruenisse, quod non dissimili dignum est detestatione comple-cti, quod quidam honoris desiderio inflamma-ti, defunctis Episcopis tonsurantur, & fiunt repente ex laicis sacerdotes, atque inuerecunde & repente religiosi propositi ducatum arripi-unt, qui esse nec adhuc milites didicerunt. Quid putamus quod isti subiectis praestaturi sunt, qui antequam disciplinatus limen attingant, tene-re locum regiminis non formidant?
units.tr: Likewise in the same place, C. Hoc ad nos peruenisse: It has come to us that, with a desire for honour inflamed, certain men, when bishops have died, receive the tonsure and suddenly become priests out of the laity, and shamelessly and abruptly seize the leadership of the religious life, though they have not yet learned even to be soldiers. What do we suppose such men will provide to those under them, who do not hesitate to hold a place of government before they have touched the threshold of discipline?

units.la: Et. C. Ordinatos. Celestinus Episcopis Galliarum. Debet enim ante esse discipulus, quisquis doctor esse desiderat, ut possit docere quod didicit. Omnis enim vitae institutio ad id quod tendit, se ratione confirmat. Qui minimé literis operam dederit, praeceptor esse non potest lite-rarum. Qui non per singula stipendia creuerit, ad meritum stipendij ordinem non potest per-uenire. Solum sacerdotium inter ista rogo vilius est? Cur facilius tribuitur, cum difficilius impleatur?
units.tr: And C. Ordinatos. Celestine to the bishops of Gaul. For whoever wishes to be a teacher must first be a disciple, so that he can teach what he has learned. For every training of life confirms by reason the goal toward which it tends. Whoever has devoted himself least to letters cannot be a teacher of letters. Whoever has not advanced through each stage cannot attain to the rank of an office that is earned by such service. Is the priesthood alone, I ask, of less worth than these? Why is it bestowed more easily, when it is harder to fulfil?

units.la: Eruditionem Episcopis necessariam esse. Ex Concilio Toletano.
units.tr: That the bishops must be learned. From the Council of Toledo.

units.la: Dist. 38. C. Ignorantia.) Ignorantia mater sanctorum[?] cunctorum errorum, maximè in sacerdotibus Dei evitanda est, qui docendi officium in po-pulo Dei susceperunt. Sacerdotes legere sanctas admonentur scripturas, Paulo Apostolo dicente ad Timotheum, Attende lectioni, & exhortationi doctrinæ, & semper permane in his. Sciant ergo sacerdotes sanctas scripturas & canones, & OMNE OPVS EORVM IN PRAEDICATIONE ET DOCTRINA CONSISTAT, atque ædificent cunctos, tā fidei scientia, quàm operum disciplina.
units.tr: Dist. 38, C. Ignorantia.) Ignorance, the mother of all errors, is above all to be avoided in the priests of God, who have undertaken the office of teaching among the people of God. Priests are admonished to read the holy Scriptures, the Apostle Paul saying to Timothy: Give attention to reading, to exhortation and to doctrine, and continue in these things. Let priests therefore know the holy Scriptures and the canons, and let all their work consist in preaching and teaching, and let them edify all, both by the knowledge of faith and by the discipline of works.

units.la: Ibidem. C. Si in laicis. Leo Episcopis Constā[?]-tinopolis. Si in laicis videtur intolerabilis infci-tia, quanto magis in his qui præsunt, nec excu-satione est digna nec venia.
units.tr: Ibidem, C. Si in laicis. Leo to the bishops of Constantinople. If ignorance seems intolerable in laymen, how much more so in those who preside? Such ignorance deserves neither excuse nor pardon.

units.la: Ibidem. C. Omnes psallentes. Ex VII. Syno-do. Unde diffinimus, omnem qui ad Episcopatus est provehendus gradum, modis omnibus Psalterium nosse, ut ex hoc etiam omnis clerus qui sub eo fuerit ita moneatur & imbuatur. Inquiratur autem diligenter à metropolitano si in promptu habeat legem, scrutabiliter & non transitorie, tam sacros canones & sanctum evangelium[?], quam divini Apostoli librum, & omne divinam scripturam, atque secundum mandata conservare & docere populum sibi com-missum. Substantia enim summi sacerdotij no-stri sunt eloquia divinitus tradita, id est, vera divinarum scripturarum disciplina, queadmodū magnus perhibet Dyonisius. Quod si discepta-verit, & ita libenter facere & docere minimè sponderit, nullatenus consecretur. Ait enim prophetæ Deus. Tu scientiā repulisti, & ego re-pellam te, ne sacerdotio fungaris mihi.
units.tr: Ibidem, C. Omnes psallentes. From the Seventh Synod. Therefore we decree that every man who is to be advanced to the rank of bishop must in every way know the Psalter, so that by this means the whole clergy under him may be instructed and trained in the same way. Let the metropolitan carefully inquire whether he has ready at hand the law, studied diligently and not superficially, both the sacred canons and the holy Gospel, as well as the book of the divine Apostle and all Divine Scripture, and whether he can keep and teach the people committed to him according to the commandments. For the substance of our high priesthood is the words divinely handed down, that is, the true discipline of the divine Scriptures, as the great Dionysius affirms. But if he disputes this, and does not willingly promise to act and teach accordingly, he must in no way be consecrated. For God says through the prophet: Because you have rejected knowledge, I will reject you, that you should not serve as priest to me.

units.la: Sacerdotes debere eruditos esse.
units.tr: Priests ought to be learned.

units.la: Vide Decreta Gelasij & Zosimi Pontificū Dist.36. C. Illiteratos, &, Qui ecclesiasticis. Quibus mox subiungit Gratianus.)
units.tr: See the decrees of Gelasius and Zosimus, popes, Dist. 36, C. Illiterati and Qui ecclesiasticis. Immediately after these, Gratian adds.

units.la: Ecce quod sacrarum literarum oportet Episcopum habere peritiam. Unde in veteri testa-mento inter cætera ornamenta pontifex rationale ferebat in pectore, in quo scribebatur, Manifestatio & veritas, quia in pectore pontificis, manifesta debet esse cognitio veritatis, &c.
units.tr: Behold, a bishop must have a knowledge of the sacred letters. Hence in the Old Testament, among the other ornaments, the high priest wore the rational on his breast, on which was written "Manifestation and truth," because in the breast of the priest the knowledge of truth ought to be manifest, etc.

units.la: Colligit deinceps multa scripturarum testi-monia & exempla. Tandem concludit. Ex quibus omnibus liquido colligitur, quod non suf-ficit prælatis bona conuersatio & morum ho-nestas, nisi addatur scientia doctrinæ.
units.tr: He then gathers many testimonies and examples from Scripture. Finally he concludes: from all these it is clearly gathered that good conduct and uprightness of morals are not enough for prelates unless knowledge of doctrine is added.

units.la: Et mox ibidem. C. si quis vult. Ex Hieronymo. Hæc duo sunt pontificis opera ut a Deo di-scat legendo scripturas divinas, & sæpius medi-tando, aut populū doceat. Sed illa doceat, quæ a Deo ipse didicerat, non ex proprio corde, vel humano sensu, sed quæ Spiritus sanctus docet.
units.tr: And soon after, in the same place, C. si quis vult, from Jerome: There are two tasks of a bishop: to learn from God by reading the divine Scriptures and meditating on them often, and to teach the people. But let him teach those things which he himself has learned from God, not what comes from his own heart or human sense, but what the Holy Spirit teaches.

units.la: De examine eorum,qui ad sacrũ ministerium accedere volunt.
units.tr: On the examination of those who wish to approach the sacred ministry.

units.la: Dist.24. C. Quando.) Episcopus à latere suo eligere debet sacerdotes, & alios prudentes viros,gnaros diuinæ legis, exercitatos in ecclesia sticis sanctionibus, qui ordinandorum vitam, genus,patriam,ætatem,institutionem,locū vbi educati sunt,si sint bene literati,si instructi in lege Dei,ante omnia diligenter inuestigent, si fidem Catholicam firmiter teneant, & verbis simplicibus afferere queant.
units.tr: Dist. 24, C. Quando.) A bishop ought to choose from his own side priests and other prudent men, skilled in divine law and practised in ecclesiastical decrees, who are to inquire carefully, above all, into the life, birth, country, age, upbringing and the place where those to be ordained were educated: whether they are well lettered, whether they are instructed in the law of God, whether they firmly hold the Catholic faith and can state it in simple words.

units.la: Et mox · Igitur per tres continuos dies examinentur,& sic Sabbato,qui probati sunt,Episcopo repræsententur.
units.tr: And soon after: Therefore let them be examined over three consecutive days, and thus on the Sabbath those who have been approved are presented to the bishop.

units.la: De examine Episcoporum.
units.tr: On the examination of bishops.

units.la: Dist. 23[?]. C. Qui Episcopus.) Qui Episcopus ordinandus est, antea examinetur,si natura sit prudens, si docibilis,si moribus temperatus, si vita castus,si sobrius, si peruigil,si semper suis negotijs cauens,si humilis, si affabilis,si misericors,si literatus, si in lege Domini instructus, si in scripturarum sensibus cautus vel acutus,si in dogmatibus ecclesiasticis exercitatus, & ante omnia si fidei documenta verbis simplicibus afferat.
units.tr: Dist. 23[?], C. Qui Episcopus.) A man who is to be ordained bishop is to be examined beforehand: whether he is by nature prudent, whether teachable, whether moderate in morals, whether chaste in life, whether sober, whether watchful, whether always cautious in his affairs, whether humble, whether affable, whether merciful, whether lettered, whether instructed in the law of the Lord, whether wary or sharp in the senses of Scripture, whether practised in ecclesiastical doctrines, and above all whether he sets out the teachings of the faith in simple words.

units.la: Nullus inuitis detur Episcopus. Dist.61. C. Nullus.) Nullus invitis detur E-piscopus.
units.tr: No bishop is to be given against the wishes of others. Dist. 61, C. Nullus.) No bishop is to be given against the wishes of others.

units.la: Quando de aliena ecclesia Episcopus eligendus.
units.tr: When a bishop is to be elected from another church.

units.la: Ibidem. Tunc autem alter de altera eligatur ecclesia, si de civitatis ipsius clero, cuius est E-piscopus ordinandus, nullus (quod evenire nō credimus) dignus poterit reperiri. Vide ibidē plura.
units.tr: Ibid. Then indeed someone is to be chosen from another church, if no one worthy (which we do not believe will happen) can be found among the clergy of the city itself whose bishop is to be ordained. See there for more.

units.la: Extraneos et ignotos in electionibus, notis & bene meritis de ecclesia non debere præponi. Celestinus Papa.
units.tr: That strangers and unknown persons should not be preferred in elections over those who are known and well deserving in the Church. Pope Celestine.

units.la: Dist.61. Nec emeritis.) Nec emeritis in suis ecclesijs peregrini & extranei, & qui ante ignoti sunt, ad exclusionem eorum qui bene civiū sanctorum[?] meretur testimonium præponantur.
units.tr: Dist. 61, Nec emeritis.) Foreigners and strangers in their own churches, and those who were previously unknown, are not to be preferred to the exclusion of those who merit the good testimony of the citizens of the saints.

units.la: Qua ætate ordinandi ministri.
units.tr: At what age ministers are to be ordained.

units.la: Dist.77. Subdiaconus.) Ex VI. Synodo. Sub-diaconus non minor X X. annorū ordinetur. Si quis vero in aliquo sacro ordine sacerdotali, præter constituta tempora ordinatus fuerit, deponatur.
units.tr: Dist. 77, Subdiaconus.) From the Sixth Council: A subdeacon is not to be ordained under twenty years of age. If anyone is ordained to any sacred, priestly order outside the appointed times, he is to be deposed.

units.la: Item. C. Placuit, ex Concil. Carthaginen. Placuit ut ante X X V. annos ætatis nec dia-coni ordinentur, nec virgines consecrentur.
units.tr: Likewise, C. Placuit, from the Council of Carthage: It has been decided that neither deacons are to be ordained nor virgins consecrated before the age of twenty-five years.

units.la: Item ex Concilio Agathen. Episco. benedistionem diaconatus minoribus XXV.annorū penitus non committat.
units.tr: Likewise, from the Council of Agde: a bishop is not to confer the blessing of the diaconate at all on those under twenty-five years.

units.la: Et mox: Presbyterum vel Episcopum ante XXX.annos,id est, antequam ad perfecti viri ætatem perueniant, nullus metropolitanorum ordinare præsumat,ne per ætatē, quod aliquoties euenit, aliquo errore culpentur.
units.tr: And soon after: No metropolitan should presume to ordain a presbyter or bishop before thirty years of age, that is, before they reach the age of a mature man, lest they be blamed for some error arising from youth, which sometimes happens.

units.la: Item ex Concilio Toletano,à XXV. anno suæ ætatis Leuitæ consecrentur, & à XXX. presbyteri ordinentur. Bonifacius.
units.tr: Likewise, from the Council of Toledo: Levites are to be consecrated from the twenty-fifth year of their age, and presbyters ordained from the thirtieth. Boniface.

units.la: Dist.78.Si quis.) Si quis XXX. ætatis suæ annum non impleuerit, nullo modo presbyter ordinetur,etiamsi valde sit dignus.
units.tr: Dist. 78, Si quis.) If anyone has not completed his thirtieth year of age, he is by no means to be ordained presbyter, even if he is very worthy.

units.la: Ibidem. C. Nemo.) Nemo presbyter cōsecretur, qui minor XXX. annis sit. Nemo diaconus vel subdiaconus fiat, qui minor XXV.annis sit. Nemo lectorib. communeretur, qui minor XVIII.annis fuerit. Nemo intra diaconissas consecretur sacrosanctæ ecclesiæ, quæ minor sit XL.annos vel ad secundum matrimonium peruenerit.
units.tr: Ibid., C. Nemo.) No one is to be consecrated presbyter who is under thirty years. No one is to be made deacon or subdeacon who is under twenty-five. No one is to be admitted as reader who is under eighteen. No one is to be consecrated among the deaconesses of the holy Church who is under forty years, or who has entered a second marriage.

units.la: Item ex Concilio Neocesariensi. Presbyter ante XXX.annorū ætatem nō ordinetur quāuis sit probabilis vitæ, sed obseruetur, vsque ad præfinitum tempus. Dominus enim XXX. anno baptizatus est & tunc prædicauit.
units.tr: Likewise from the Council of Neocaesarea: A presbyter is not to be ordained before the age of thirty, although he be of approved life, but he must be kept until the appointed time. For the Lord was baptized in his thirtieth year, and then he began to preach.

units.la: Laicos posse aliquando ordinari.
units.tr: That laymen can sometimes be ordained.

units.la: Dist.33.C.Laici.) Laici qui habentes vxores
units.tr: Dist. 33, C. Laici.) Laymen who have wives,

units.la: F baptizati sunt, ac sic fe instituerunt ut in nullo eorū opinio vacillaret, aut clericis iuncti sunt, aut monasterijs ex quo baptizati sunt adhæserunt, si non concubinam, si non pellicem noverint, si in bonis operibus vigilaverint, non prohibentur huiusmodi ad clericatus sortem assumi. Innocentius Papa.
units.tr: who have been baptized, and who have so conducted themselves that in none of them is their reputation wavering, either have been joined to clerics or have attached themselves to monasteries since their baptism, if they have known no concubine and no mistress, and if they have kept watch in good works, are not forbidden to be taken up into the rank of the clergy. Pope Innocent.

units.la: De Laicis qui Episcopi facti sunt.
units.tr: On laymen who were made bishops.

units.la: Dist.61. C.Statuimus. Gratianus ait.) E contra Beatus Nicolaus ex laico electus est in Episcopum. Beatus Seuerus ex lanificio assumptus est in archiepiscopum. Beatus Ambrosius, cum nondum esset baptizatus, in Archiepiscopum est electus.
units.tr: Dist. 61, C. Statuimus. Gratian says.) On the contrary, Blessed Nicholas was elected bishop from the laity. Blessed Severus was taken from wool-working to be archbishop. Blessed Ambrose, though not yet baptized, was elected archbishop.

units.la: Romani Pontificis nō rite electi, eiusque sequacium condemnatio.
units.tr: The Roman Pontiff not rightly elected, and the condemnation of his followers.

units.la: Dist.23. C.In nomine Domini.) Quòd si quis contra hoc decretum nostrum, synodali sententia promulgatum, quasi per seditionem vel præsumptionem, aut quolibet ingenio, electus, aut etiam ordinatus, seu inthronizatus fuerit, authoritate divina & sanctorum Apostolorum Petri & Pauli, perpetuo anathemate cum suis authoribus & fautoribus & sequacibus, à liminibus sanctæ Dei ecclesiæ separatus abijciatur, sicut antichristus, & invasor & destructor to-tius tius Christianitatis, nec aliqua super hoc ei audientia refervetur, sed ab omni ecclesiastico gradu in quocunque fuerat prius, sine retractatione deponatur. Cui quisquis adhæserit, vel qualemcunqne tanquam Pontifici reverentias exhibverit, aut in aliquo eum defendere præsumpserit, pari sententia sit mancipatus. Quòd si quis huius nostræ sanctæ Decreta-lis sententiæ temerator extiterit, & Romanam ecclesiam sua præsumptione confundere & perturbare contra hoc statutum tentaverit, perpetuo anathemate atque excommunicatio-ne damnetur, & cum impijs, qui non resurgent in iudicio, reputetur. Omnipotentis iram contra se sentiat, & sanctorum Apostolorum Petri & Pauli, quorum ecclesiam præsumit confundere, in hac vita & in futura furorem sentiat. Fiat habitatio eius deserta, & in tabernaculis suis non sit qui inhabitet. Fiant filij eius orphani & uxor eius vidua. Commotus commoveatur, ipse & filij eius mendicet, & eijciantur de habi-tationib.suis. Scrutetur etiā fœnerator omnem substantiā eius, & diripiant alieni labores eius. Orbis terrārū pugnet cōtra eū, & cuncta elementa sint ei contraria, & omnium sanctorum quorum scientium[?] merita, illum confundant, & in hac vita super eum apertam vindictam eorū ostendant. Observatores autē huius nostri Decreti, omne potétis gratia protegat,& authoritas beatorum Apostolorum Petri & Pauli omniū peccatorum vinculis absoluat.
units.tr: Dist.23. C.In nomine Domini.) If anyone, contrary to this our decree, promulgated by synodal sentence, is elected, or even ordained or enthroned, by sedition or presumption, or by any contrivance whatever, then by the divine authority and that of the holy Apostles Peter and Paul, let him be cast out, separated from the thresholds of the holy Church of God, under perpetual anathema together with his authors, abettors and followers, like Antichrist and the invader and destroyer of the whole of Christendom. Let no hearing be reserved for him on this matter, but let him be deposed from every ecclesiastical rank he previously held, without any possibility of revision. Whoever adheres to him, or shows him any reverence as a pontiff whatsoever, or presumes to defend him in any way, shall be subject to the same sentence. But if anyone violates this our sacred decretal sentence, and attempts by his presumption to confound and disturb the Roman Church contrary to this statute, let him be condemned to perpetual anathema and excommunication, and be reckoned with the impious, who will not rise in judgment. Let him feel the wrath of the Almighty against himself, and the fury of the holy Apostles Peter and Paul, whose Church he presumes to confound, both in this life and in the next. Let his habitation be made desolate, and let there be none to dwell in his tents. Let his sons be made orphans and his wife a widow. Let him be unsettled and move about, and let him and his sons beg, and be cast out of their dwellings. Let the moneylender search out all his substance, and let strangers plunder his labours. Let the whole world fight against him, and let all the elements be against him, and let the merits of all the saints, whose deeds they know, confound him, and let them show their open vengeance upon him in this life. But as for the observers of this our decree, let the grace of the Almighty protect them, and let the authority of the blessed Apostles Peter and Paul absolve them from the chains of all their sins.

units.la: Imperatorem ius habere eligēdi Pontificem, & ordinandi Apostolicam sedem, & inuestiendi archiepiscopos & episcopos per singulas prouincias.
units.tr: That the emperor has the right to elect the Pontiff, and to ordain the Apostolic See, and to invest the archbishops and bishops throughout the several provinces.

units.la: Dist.63.C.Hadrianus.) Hadrianus autē PP.cū vniuersa synodo tradiderit Carolo ius & potestate eligendi Pontificē, & ordinandi apostolicā sedem. Dignitatē quoq; patriciatus ei concesserat. Insuper archiepiscopos & episcopos per singulas prouincias ab eo inuestitura accipere diffiniuit, vt nisi à rege laudetur & inuestiatur Episcopus, à r e mine[?] consecretur.[?] Et quicunq; contra hoc decretū ageret, anathematis vinculo eum innodauit, & nisi resipisceret, bona eius publicari præcepit.
units.tr: Dist.63. C.Hadrianus.) Now Pope Hadrian, together with the whole synod, handed to Charles the right and power of electing the Pontiff and of ordaining the Apostolic See. He had also granted him the dignity of patrician. Moreover, he decreed that the archbishops and bishops throughout the several provinces should receive investiture from him, so that a bishop should not be consecrated unless he has been approved and invested by the king, and by the metropolitan. And he bound with the chain of anathema whoever acted contrary to this decree, and ordered that his goods be confiscated unless he repented.

units.la: Et mox item Leo Papa in synodo congregata Romæ in Ecclesia sancti saluatoris, ad exemplū Beati Hadriani Apostolicæ sedis antistitis, qui Domino Carolo victoriosissimo regi Francorum ac Longobardorum patriciatus dignitate ac ordinatione Apostolicæ sedis, & inuestitura Episcoporū concesit. Ego Leo quoq; seruus seruorum Dei Episcopus cū toto clero ac Romano populo, constituimus & confirmamus, & corroboramus, & per nostrā Apostolicā authoritate cocedimus atq; largimur Domino Ottoni pri mo,regi Theutonicorū,eiusq; successoribus hu ius regni Italiæ in perpetuū, facultate eligendi successorem,atq; summę sedis apostolicæ Pon tificem ordinandi, Ac per hoc archiepiscopos, seu Episcopos,vt ipsi ab eo inuestitura accipiát, & consecratione unde debet, exceptis his quos Imperator Pontificibus & archiepiscopis con cesit. Et vt nemo deinceps cuiusc unq; dignita tis vel religionis eligendi vel patriciū,vel Pon tificé summæ sedis Apostolicæ, aut quemcūq; Episco.ordinandi habeat facultaté absq; cosen su ipsius Imperatoris. Quod tamē fiat absq; om ni pecúia,& vt ipse sit patricius, & rex.Quod si à clero & populo quis eligatur Episcopus,nisi à supradiĉto rege laudetur, & inuestiatur, nō có secretur.Si quis contra hanc apostolicá auĉto ritaté aliquid molietur , hûc excômunicationi subiacere decernim9,et nisi resipuerit,irreuoca bili exîtio puniri, vel vltimis supplicijs affici.
units.tr: And soon after, likewise Pope Leo, in a synod gathered at Rome in the Church of the holy Saviour, following the example of the blessed Hadrian, bishop of the Apostolic See, who to the most victorious lord Charles, king of the Franks and Lombards, granted the dignity of patrician, the ordering of the Apostolic See, and the investiture of bishops: I, Leo, also servant of the servants of God and bishop, together with all the clergy and the Roman people, establish, confirm and strengthen, and by our apostolic authority grant and bestow upon the lord Otto the First, king of the Teutons, and his successors in this kingdom of Italy, for ever, the power of electing the successor and ordaining the Pontiff of the supreme Apostolic See; and by this means the archbishops, or bishops, that they may receive investiture from him, and consecration from where it is due, except those whom the emperor has granted to the pontiffs and archbishops. And that no one of whatever dignity or religious order may henceforth have the power of electing or ordaining a patrician, or the Pontiff of the supreme Apostolic See, or any bishop, without the consent of the emperor himself. This shall be done without any payment, and so that he himself may be patrician and king. But if anyone is elected bishop by the clergy and people, unless he is approved and invested by the aforesaid king, let him not be consecrated. If anyone attempts anything against this apostolic authority, we decree that he is subject to excommunication, and unless he repents, that he be punished with irrevocable destruction, or be visited with the final penalties.

units.la: In eadē distinĉtione plura inuenies in hanc sententiá vtpote. Quód sacra principis authori tas ordinandis sit necessaria C.Principali. Item Papa rogat Augustū , vt Reatinam ecclesiá cui dam eleĉto dignetur concedere. C. Reatina.
units.tr: In the same distinction you will find many things to this effect: that the sacred authority of the prince is necessary for ordinations, C. Principali. Likewise, the Pope asks Augustus to deign to grant the Church of Rieti to a certain man who was elected. C. Reatina.

units.la: Item, quód Imperatoris epistola in eleĉtio nis confirmatione desideretur. C. Leĉtis.
units.tr: Likewise, that the emperor's letter is required for the confirmation of an election. C. Lectis.

units.la: Itē. Quód eleĉtus in Romanum Pontificem non[?] ordinari debeat, nisi eius decretum Imperatori primo prefentetur. C. Agatho.
units.tr: Likewise, that the one elected Roman Pontiff ought not to be ordained unless his decree is first presented to the emperor. C. Agatho.

units.la: Hæc omnia quantumuis diserté ponantur, postea tamen diuersum statuitur. C. Quia. Item C.cū' Hadrianus. Item C. Ego Ludouicus. Itē C. Tibi Domino. Et C. Omnis electio.
units.tr: Although all these things are set down so explicitly, yet afterwards a different rule is laid down. C. Quia. Likewise C. Cum Hadrianus. Likewise C. Ego Ludovicus. Likewise C. Tibi Domino. And C. Omnis electio.

units.la: De ordinibus ecclesiasticis cum ex Iudaismo tùm ex gentilismo desumptis.
units.tr: On the ecclesiastical orders, taken both from Judaism and from paganism.

units.la: Dist.21. C. Decretis.) dicitur quod summorū Pontificum, pręfulum & reliquorum sacerdotum institutio in vęteri testamento inchoata fit. Et sequitur.
units.tr: Dist. 21, C. Decretis: it is said that the institution of the chief pontiffs, prelates and other priests began in the Old Testament. And it continues.

units.la: Summi etenim pōtifices et minores sacerdotes à Deo sunt instituti per Mosem, qui ex præcepto Domini Aaron in summū pontifice, filios vero eius unxit in minores sacerdotes. Postea vero Dauid, cum ministeria domus Domini ampliaret, ianitores & cantores instituit. Porrò Solomon quendam modum exorcizandi inuenit, quo dæmones adiurati ex obsessis corporibus pellebantur. Huic officio mancipati exorciste vocati sunt. De quibus Dominus in euangelio: Si ego in Beelzebub eijcio dæmonia, filij vestri, scilicet exorcistæ, in quo eijciūt? Hæc omnia in nouo testamento ecclesia imitata, habet ianitores suos, quos hostiarios appellamus. Pro cantoribus, lectores & cantores instituit. ftituit. Exorcistas autē nomine antiquo & ossi- cio permanente recepit. Pro filijs verò Aaron, omnes infra fummū pontificē facerdotiū admi niftrantes sunt consecrati. Inter eos quædā di- fcretio seruata est, vt alij appellētur simpliciter sacerdotes, alij archipresbyteri, alij Chorepifco pi, alij episcopi, alij Archiepiscopi seu Metro- politæ, alij primates, alij patriarchæ, alij summi Pōtifices. Horū discretio A GENTILIBVS MAXIME INTRODVCTA EST, qui suos slamines, alios simpliciter slamines, alios archislamines, alios protoslamines appellabāt.
units.tr: For the chief priests and the lesser priests were instituted by God through Moses, who by the Lord's command anointed Aaron as chief priest and his sons as lesser priests. Later, when David enlarged the services of the house of the Lord, he appointed gatekeepers and singers. Solomon also discovered a certain method of exorcism, by which demons were driven out of possessed bodies when they had been adjured. Those devoted to this office were called exorcists. Of them the Lord says in the Gospel: "If I cast out devils by Beelzebub, by whom do your sons cast them out?" In the New Testament the Church has imitated all these things: it has its gatekeepers, whom we call doorkeepers. In place of the singers it has appointed readers and singers. It has received exorcists, keeping the ancient name and the continuing office. In place of the sons of Aaron, all who serve in the priesthood below the chief priest have been consecrated. Among these a distinction has been kept, so that some are called simply priests, some archpriests, some chorepiscopi, some bishops, some archbishops or metropolitans, some primates, some patriarchs, and some chief pontiffs. This distinction was introduced chiefly by the Gentiles, who called some of their flamens simply flamens, some archflamens, and some protoflamens.

units.la: DE SIMONIA, CAPVT XXII, De Simoniacis.
units.tr: On Simony, Chapter 22, Concerning the Simoniacs.

units.la: 1.q.6. Quid vero. ) Perinde Simoniacus habetur, qui pro electione præmia largitur, ac si pro consecratione munera dedisset.
units.tr: 1. q. 6. Quid vero.) A man who gives rewards for his election is held to be a Simoniac just as much as one who gave gifts for his consecration.

units.la: Et mox. Gregor. Siagrio Episcopo Augusto dunensi. Sicut is qui inuitatus renuit, quæsitus refugit, sacris altaribus est admouendus, sic qui vltrò ambit, vel importunè se ingerit, est proculdubio repellendus. Nam qui sic nititur ad altiora consicendere, quid aliud agit, nisi vt crescendo decrescat & ascendendo exterius, interius in profundum descendat? Itaque frater charissime in sacerdotibus ordinandis sinceritas vigeat, fit simplex & fine venalita te cósensus, pura præferatur eleétio,vt ad fummũ sacerdotij (vel pontificij)non suffragio vé- ditorũ prouectus,sed Dei credatur efle iudicio.
units.tr: And shortly after, Gregory to Siagrius, bishop of Autun: As one who, when invited, refuses, and when sought, flees, is to be brought to the holy altars, so one who seeks it of his own accord, or thrusts himself in without being asked, is beyond doubt to be rejected. For what else does one who strives in this way to climb to higher things accomplish, except that by growing he diminishes, and by ascending outwardly he descends inwardly into the depths? Therefore, dearest brother, let sincerity flourish in the ordination of priests. Let the election be simple and free of venal agreement, and let it be pure, so that a man is advanced to the summit of the priesthood (or the pontificate) not by the vote of sellers, but is believed to be raised by the judgment of God.

units.la: 1. q. 1. Reperimur. Ambrosius. Reperiuntur quaplurimi negotiatione muneris mercari vel- le gratia Spiritus sancti, dū illi preciū donant, vt pontificalis ordinis sublimitate accipiant,o- bliti verborum Petri,qui dixit,ad Simonē,Pe- cunia tua tecū fit in perditione, quia existima- sti donū Dei posse pecunia posideri. Proinde quia & vsitatum est tantū malum, & maiorum extat frequenter mucrone succisum,nos quoq; huic vulneri cancerofo, ignitu quod superest adhuc inijcimus ferrum,decernetes omnino,vt quicuq; deinceps pro accipienda diuina dignitate doni, quod libet premium detectus fuerit obtulisse,ex eode tepore se nouerit anathematis opprobrio condemnatu atq; a participatione corporis & sanguinis Christi alienu,ex quo illū costat execrabile Christo perpetrasse flagitiū. Quòd si aliquis eius accusator extiterit, ille qui hūc ordine, munerum fuerit donatione lucratus,& suscepto honoris gradu priuetur,& in monasterio sub perenni poena retrudatur. Illi vero qui hac causa, munerũ acceptores extiterint,si clerici fuerint,honoris sui amissione mul- ctentur,si vero laici,perpetuo anathemate condemnentur.
units.tr: 1. q. 1. Reperimur.) Ambrose: Many are found who, by a business of bribery, wish to buy the grace of the Holy Spirit. They give a price so that they may receive the high dignity of the pontifical order, forgetting the words of Peter, who said to Simon: "Your money perish with you, because you thought the gift of God could be possessed with money." Therefore, since so great an evil is both customary and frequently cut down by the sword of our elders, we too apply the iron that remains to this cancerous wound by fire, decreeing absolutely that whoever henceforth shall be found to have offered any price whatever in order to receive the divine dignity of the gift shall know that from that very time he stands condemned with the disgrace of anathema and is cut off from participation in the body and blood of Christ, since it is clear that he has committed a detestable crime against Christ. But if anyone shall appear as his accuser, the man who has gained this order by the giving of gifts shall be deprived of the degree of honour he has received and confined in a monastery under perpetual penalty. Those, however, who in this matter have been the receivers of gifts, if they are clergy, shall be punished by the loss of their rank; if they are laymen, they shall be condemned to perpetual anathema.

units.la: Item ex VIII. Synodo. Qui per pecuniam quenquam consecrauerit, vel ab alio consecratus est, alienus à sacerdotio fiat.
units.tr: Likewise from the Eighth Synod: Whoever has consecrated anyone for money, or has been consecrated by another for money, shall become a stranger to the priesthood.

units.la: Item Gregor. Nazianzenus. Qui studet donum Dei pretio mercari, in sacro ordine nulla ratione de cætero permanere aut reuocare posse dubium non est, talis à communione omnibus modis abscindatur. Nam Spiritus sancti donum pretio comparari, quid aliud est quâ capitale crimen & Simoniaca haeresis? Quod quam detestabiliter in utroq; Testamento vindicatum sit, multorum exemplis facile apparet. Giezi enim gratiâ sanitatis Naaman Syro vendidit, eandemq; gratiam sanitatis Helisæo vindicante leprosus factus amisit. Iudas omnium redemptorem vendidit, mox laqueo suspensus, eandem redemptoris gratiam non obtinuit. Et merito, quia nemo potest retinere quod vendidit. Simon etiam Magus cum eandem Spiritus sancti gratiam emere vellet, damnationis sententiam à Petro audiuit: Pecunia tua tecum sit in perditionem, quia donum Dei existimasti pecunia possideri. Dominus etiam, vt ementes & vendentes huius gratiæ expertes ostenderet, cunctos alios peccatores per gratiam in templo dimisit, singulariter vendentes & ementes increpans & flagellans, de templo eiecit, in quo venditores & emptores suos gratia Spiritus san &i constat destitutos esse et vacuos. Quos enim Christus eiecit è templo, nunquâ spiritus Christi sibi faciet templum.
units.tr: Likewise Gregory Nazianzen: There is no doubt that one who seeks to buy the gift of God with a price can in no way remain or be restored to the sacred order thereafter; such a person must be cut off from communion in every way. For to acquire the gift of the Holy Spirit with a price is nothing other than the capital crime and the heresy of Simon Magus. How detestably this has been punished in both Testaments is easily shown by many examples. Gehazi sold to Naaman the Syrian the grace of healing, and, when Elisha avenged this grace of healing, he became a leper and lost it. Judas sold the Redeemer of all, and was soon hanged with a noose, and did not obtain the grace of the Redeemer. And rightly so, because no one can keep what he has sold. Simon Magus too, when he wished to buy the same grace of the Holy Spirit, heard the sentence of damnation from Peter: "Your money perish with you, because you thought the gift of God could be possessed with money." The Lord also, in order to show that buyers and sellers of this grace are without it, dismissed all the other sinners from the temple by grace, and, rebuking and scourging the buyers and sellers individually, cast them out of the temple. It is evident that those buyers and sellers were left destitute and empty of the grace of the Holy Spirit. For Christ never makes a temple for his Spirit out of those whom he has cast out of the temple.

units.la: Item, Ambr. ait. Cū ordinaretur Episcopus, quod dedit aurum fuit, quod perdidit, anima fuit. Cum alium ordinaret, quod accepit, aurū fuit, quod dedit, lepra fuit.
units.tr: Likewise Ambrose says: When a bishop was being ordained, what he gave was gold, what he lost was a soul. When he ordained another, what he received was gold, what he gave was leprosy.

units.la: 1.q.7. Si quis omnem.) Omnis Episcopus vel presbyter aut diaconus, convictus quòd pro muneribus ordinationem dederit vel acceperit, à sacerdotio cadat.
units.tr: 1. q. 7. Si quis omnem.) Every bishop, presbyter or deacon who is convicted of having given or received ordination for gifts shall fall from the priesthood.

units.la: Et mox ibidē. Cum omni fidutia clamo, qui per Simoniam ordinatus est, siue Episcopus, siue presbyter, siue diaconus, alienus est à sacer-dotio, neq; enim venalis est gratia spiritus san-cti. Caiaphæ traditio, & adinuentio Simonis, à sancto sacerdotio est aliena. Vide ibidem plura.
units.tr: And shortly after in the same place: With full confidence I declare that whoever has been ordained through simony, whether bishop, presbyter or deacon, is a stranger to the priesthood. For the grace of the Holy Spirit is not for sale. The betrayal of Caiaphas and the invention of Simon are foreign to holy priesthood. See more in the same place.

units.la: Item ibidem amplius. Quicunq; per pecuniā dispensationem vel curam sortiti sunt monaste-riorū, vel ecclesiarum, vel religiosarū domorū gerontocomiorū, xenodochiorū, orphanotro-phiorum, cū depositione expellantur à dispen-satione illa & cura.
units.tr: Likewise, further in the same place: Whoever have obtained by money the stewardship or the care of monasteries, churches, or religious houses, of homes for the aged, hospices, or orphanages, shall be expelled from that stewardship and care with deposition.

units.la: Et mox ex Concil. Melden. Cauendū est & summopere studendū, ac per virtutem Christi sanguinis interdicendū Episcopis & regibus, et omnibus sublimioribus potestatibus, atq; cun-ctis fautoribus & electoribus quorūcunq; con-sensoribus[?] fenforibus seu ordinatoribus in gradu ecclesia-stico, ut nemo per Simoniacâ hæresim obtineat locū, quacunq; functione, calliditate, promissione seu cōmoditate aut datione, per se aut sub-missam personam.
units.tr: And shortly after, from the Council of Meaux: Care must be taken, and every effort made, and by the power of the blood of Christ it must be forbidden to bishops, kings, and all higher powers, and to all supporters and electors, or consenters, or ordainers in ecclesiastical rank, that anyone obtain a place in the Simoniacal heresy by any function, cunning, promise, advantage, or gift, whether by himself or through a substituted person.

units.la: Simoniacâ hæresim cæteris damnabiliorē esse.
units.tr: That the heresy of simony is more damnable than all others.

units.la: 1.q.7.Patet.)Paschalis p p.Patet Simoniacos veluti primos & præcipuos hæreticos ab omnibus fidelibus respuendos, & si cōmoniti non resipuerint, ab exteris etiam potestatibus opprimendos. Omnia etiam crimina ad cōparatione Simoniacæ hæresis quasi pro nihilo reputatur.
units.tr: 1.q.7.Patet.) Pope Paschal: It is clear that simoniacs, as the first and chief heretics, are to be shunned by all the faithful, and if, when warned, they do not repent, they are to be suppressed even by secular powers. Indeed, all crimes are regarded as nothing in comparison with the heresy of simony.

units.la: 1.q.1.Eos qui.) Eos qui p pecunias manus imposuerút vel imponút, Petrus divinus Apostolus, cuius cathedrā sortita est sanctitas vestra, tá quá Simonē Magū deponit. Tolerabilior est enim Macedonii, & eorū qui circa ipsum sunt S. sancti impugnatorū impia hæresis. Illi enim creatura & seruūDei patris & filii S. sanctū delirando fatetur, isti verò S. sanctū efficiút suū servū. Omnis enim dominus quod habet si vultvedit, sive servū, sive aliquid aliud eorū quæ posidet[?]. Similiter & qui emit, dñs eius volés esse quod emerit, per pretiū pecuniæ illud acquirit. Ita & hi, qui hac iniqua actione operatur, detrahút S. sancto, æqualiter peccantes his qui blasphema-verint dicētes Christū in Beelzebub eijcere dæmonia. Atq; ut verius dicamus Judæ cōparatur ꝓditori, qui Judæis occiforibꝰ Christū vēdidit.
units.tr: 1.q.1.Eos qui.) Those who have laid on hands for money, Peter the divine apostle, whose chair your holiness has obtained, deposed as Simon Magus. For the impious heresy of Macedonius and of those around him who attack the Holy Spirit is more tolerable. For he, raving, confesses the Holy Spirit to be a creature and servant of the Father and the Son; but these make the Holy Spirit their servant. For every master, if he wishes, sells whatever he possesses, whether a slave or anything else he owns. Likewise the buyer, wishing to be the owner of what he has bought, acquires it by paying money. So too those who perform this wicked act detract from the Holy Spirit, sinning equally with those who blasphemed, saying that Christ casts out demons by Beelzebub. And to speak more truly, they are compared to Judas the betrayer, who sold Christ to the Jewish murderers.

units.la: De his qui per munera invadunt ecclesias vacantes. Ex Concilio Rothomagensi.
units.tr: Concerning those who invade vacant churches by means of gifts. From the Council of Rouen.

units.la: Sancitum est.) Sancitum est, atque omnibus modis prohibitum, ut si quis presbyter inuentus fuerit alicui clerico vel laico munera dare vel dedisse, aut aliam pecuniam tribuere, ut alterius presbyteri ecclesiam vacantem pretio redimat, pro hac cupiditate, seu rapina, seu praesumptione, turpis lucri gratia, deijciatur à clero, & alienus existat à regula.
units.tr: Sancitum est.) It has been decreed, and forbidden in every way, that if any presbyter is found to have given, or to have offered, gifts or other money to any cleric or layman in order to buy back another presbyter's vacant church for a price, out of this greed, whether plunder or presumption, for the sake of shameful gain, he is to be cast out from the clergy and be a stranger to the rule.

units.la: Simoniacos non esse sacerdotes, ideoq; deponi debere.
units.tr: That simoniacs are not priests, and therefore ought to be deposed.

units.la: Quicunq;.) Quicunq; sacros ordines vendunt aut emunt, sacerdotes esse non possunt.
units.tr: Quicunq;.) Whoever sells or buys holy orders cannot be a priest.

units.la: Item. Gregor. Quicunque studet per pretij datonem sacrum ordinem accipere, sacerdos non est, sed inaniter tantummodo dici concupiscit.
units.tr: Likewise, Gregory: Whoever strives to receive holy orders by the giving of a price is not a priest, but desires only to be called one in vain.

units.la: Idem in Registro. Presbyter si per pecuniam ecclesias obtinuerit, non solum ecclesia priuetur, sed etiam sacerdotij honore spolietur, quia & altare & decimas & Spiritum sanctum emere vel vendere, Simoniacam haeresim esse nullus fidelium ignorat.
units.tr: Also in the Register: If a presbyter has obtained churches through money, he is not only to be deprived of the church but also stripped of the honour of the priesthood, because no one of the faithful is ignorant that to buy or sell the altar, tithes, and the Holy Spirit is the Simoniacal heresy.

units.la: Simoniacos habere et dare Spiritum mendacij. Leo Papa.
units.tr: That simoniacs have and give the spirit of lying. Pope Leo.

units.la: 1.q 1. Gratia.) Quid ergo dant? Profecto quod habent. Quid habent? Spiritum vtique mendacij. Quomodo hoc probamus? Quia si spiritus veritatis (testante ipsa veritate de qua procedit) gratis accipitur, proculdubio spiritus mendacij esse conuincitur, qui non gratis accipitur vel datur.
units.tr: 1.q 1. Gratia.) What then do they give? Surely what they have. And what do they have? Surely the spirit of lying. How do we prove this? Because if the spirit of truth (as the Truth himself, from whom it proceeds, testifies) is received freely, then beyond doubt the spirit that is not received or given freely is shown to be the spirit of lying.

units.la: Simoniacs panem pollutum offerre. Hier. super Malach.
units.tr: Simoniacs offer polluted bread. Jerome on Malachi.

units.la: Dist.49.C.Sacerdotes.) Sacerdotes nomen Domini despiciunt, & quantum ad se, panem pollutum offerunt, qui ad altare indigne accedunt, quique dato munere sacerdotium praesumunt, &c.
units.tr: Dist.49.C.Sacerdotes.) Priests despise the name of the Lord, and so far as they are concerned, they offer polluted bread: those who approach the altar unworthily, and who presume to the priesthood by giving a gift, etc.

units.la: De his qui vendunt beneficia ecclesiastica. Gregor.
units.tr: Concerning those who sell ecclesiastical benefices. Gregory.

units.la: 1.q. 2. Si quis dator.) Si quis dator vel accep-tor, Dei ecclesias, vel ecclesiastica beneficia, quae quidam praebendas vocant, sub pecuniae in-teruentu susceperit, siue dando emerit, siue accipiendo vendiderit, a Simonis non excluditur perditione. Sed si perseuerans fuerit, perpetua mulctetur damnatione, &c.
units.tr: 1.q. 2. Si quis dator.) If anyone, whether giver or receiver, has taken up God's churches or ecclesiastical benefices, which some call prebends, through the intervention of money, whether by giving he has bought or by receiving he has sold, he is not excluded from the perdition of Simon. But if he persists, let him be punished with perpetual condemnation, etc.

units.la: Et mox. Si quis Episcopus prębendas, archi-diaconatus, praeposituras, vel aliqua officia ec-clesiastica vendiderit, vel aliter quā statuta sanstorum patrum præcipiunt ordinauerit, ab officio suspendatur. Dignū est enim, vt sicut gratis Episcopatum accepit, ita membra eiusdem Episcopatus gratis distribuat.
units.tr: And soon after: If any bishop has sold prebends, archdeaconries, provostships, or any ecclesiastical offices, or has ordained them otherwise than the statutes of the holy fathers prescribe, let him be suspended from office. For it is fitting that, as he received the bishopric freely, so he should distribute the members of the same bishopric freely.

units.la: Contra pluralitatem beneficiorum. Ex Synodo VII.
units.tr: Against the plurality of benefices. From the Seventh Synod.

units.la: 21.q.1. Clericus.) Clericus ab instante tempore non connumeretur in duabus ecclesijs. Negotiationis enim hoc est, & turpis lucri proprium commodum, & ab ecclesiæ consuetudine penitus alienum. Audiuimus enim ex ipsa Domini ca voce, quòd nemo potest duobus dominis seruire.
units.tr: 21.q.1. Clericus.) Henceforth a cleric is not to be counted in two churches. For this belongs to trade, is the proper advantage of shameful gain, and is wholly alien to the custom of the Church. For we have heard from the Lord's own voice that no one can serve two masters.

units.la: Et mox ex Chalcedonen. Conc. Clericū in duarū ecclesijs ciuitatū conscribi non oportet.
units.tr: And soon after, from the Council of Chalcedon: A cleric ought not to be enrolled in two churches of cities.

units.la: Duas præbendas clericum non debere habere, nec in duabus intitulari ecclesijs.
units.tr: A cleric ought not to have two prebends, nor be entitled to two churches.

units.la: Dist.70. Sanctorum.) In qua ecclesia quilibet intitulatus est, in ea perpetuò perseueret. Omnino autem in duabus aliquę intitulari nō liceat, sed vnusquisq; in qua intitulatus est, in ea tantum canonicus habeatur. Licet enim Episcopus dispositione vnus diuersis præesse possit ecclesijs, canonicus tamē præbendarius nisi vnius ecclesiæ in qua conscriptus est, esse non debet.
units.tr: Dist.70. Sanctorum.) In whatever church anyone is entitled, let him persevere in it forever. Indeed it is in no way permitted to be entitled to two, but each is to be regarded as a canon only in the one in which he is entitled. For although a bishop, by arrangement, may preside over several churches, a canon prebendary ought not to belong to any church except the one in which he is enrolled.

units.la: Plures ecclesias vni presbytero non debere committi.
units.tr: Several churches ought not to be committed to one presbyter.

units.la: 10.q.3.Vnio.) Plures ecclesiæ vni nequaquā committantur presbytero, quia solus per totas ecclesias, nec officium valet persoluere, nec rebus earum necessariam curam impendere.
units.tr: 10.q.3. Vnio.) Several churches ought by no means to be committed to one presbyter, because one man alone cannot discharge the office throughout all the churches, nor give the necessary care to their affairs.

units.la: Qui sumptibus p̄ oprijs viuere potest, stipendium ab ecclesia non debere accipere. Hier. ad Damasum Papam.
units.tr: One who is able to live from his own resources ought not to receive a stipend from the Church. Jerome to Pope Damasus.

units.la: 1.q.1.Clericos autem.) Clericos autē illos conuenit ecclesiæ stipendijs sustentari, quibus parentum & propinquorū nulla suffragantur bona. Qui autem bonis parentum & opibus suis sustentari possunt, si quod est pauperum accipiunt, sacrilegium profecto committunt, & per abusionem taliū[?] iudiciū sibi manducant & bibunt.
units.tr: 1.q.1. Clericos autem.) It is fitting that those clerics be sustained by church stipends who have no parents or relatives to support them with their goods. But those who can be sustained by their parents' goods and their own resources, if they take what belongs to the poor, certainly commit sacrilege, and by such abuse they eat and drink judgment to themselves.

units.la: Ad alienas ecclesias non transfundum esse.
units.tr: That one should not transfer to other churches.

units.la: 7.q.Quia frater.) Ambitionis causa quicunq; ecclesię suę mediocritate despecta, ad maiorem ecclesiam transfire voluerit, debet reuocari ad propriam. Quòd si redire contempserit, careat aliena & propria.
units.tr: 7.q.Quia frater.) Whoever, out of ambition, despises the modest standing of his own church and wishes to move to a larger one, must be recalled to his own. But if he refuses to return, let him lose both the foreign church and his own.

units.la: Ibidem mox ex Conc. Niceno, quòd Episcopus vel quilibet clericus non debeat relicta sua ecclesia ad aliam transfire.
units.tr: Immediately after this, from the Council of Nicaea: a bishop or any other cleric must not leave his church and move to another.

units.la: Item in monasterium deputatur Episcopus qui in ecclesia sua residere contemnit. Item excommunicari jubentur clerici, qui relicta sua ecclesia, ad eam redire noluerint.
units.tr: Likewise, a bishop who refuses to stay in his own church is assigned to a monastery. Likewise, clerics who, having left their church, are unwilling to return to it are ordered to be excommunicated.

units.la: Item ex Concilio Antiocheno. C. Episcopu.) Episcopum de dioecesi ad dioecesim nō debere transire, neque si seipsum ingesserit, neque si ab populis fuerit violenter attractus, neq; si etiam hoc ei ab Episcopis suadetur. Manere autem eum debere in ecclesia Dei, quam ab initio for-titus est, & non ab ea alibi demigrare, secundum regulam super hoc olim à Patribus constitutam decernimus.
units.tr: Likewise, from the Council of Antioch. C. Episcopu.) We decree that a bishop must not pass from one diocese to another, whether he thrusts himself forward, or is violently carried off by the people, or even if the bishops urge him to do so. He must remain in the Church of God which he was first appointed to, and must not migrate from it elsewhere, according to the rule on this matter laid down long ago by the Fathers.

units.la: Sua sede careat, qui alienam appetit.
units.tr: Let him who seeks another's see lose his own.

units.la: 7.q.1.Si quis.) Si quis Episcopus suae civitatis mediocritate despecta administrationem celebrioris loci ambierit, & ad maiorem plebem se quacunque ratione transtulerit, à cathedra quidem pellatur aliena. Carebit etiam propria, ut nec illis præsideat, quos per avaritiam concupivit, nec illis quos per superbiam spreuit. suis igitur terminis contentus quisque sit, nec supra mensuras juris sui affectet augeri.
units.tr: 7.q.1.Si quis.) If any bishop, despising the modest standing of his own city, seeks the administration of a more famous place, and transfers himself by any means to a larger people, he shall indeed be thrown from the other's chair. He shall also lose his own, so that he presides neither over those whom he has coveted out of greed nor over those whom he has scorned out of pride. Let each therefore be content within his own boundaries, and not aim to enlarge himself beyond the measure of his right.

units.la: Et mox ex Concilio Meldensi. Si quis de ordine sacerdotali, contemptu minoris ecclesiæ ambitiosè & improbè ad potiorem aspiraverit, canonica erga eum diffinitio conservetur, hoc est, ut utraq; careat.
units.tr: And immediately after, from the Council of Meaux: If anyone of the priestly order, out of contempt for a smaller church, ambitiously and wrongfully aspires to a more important one, the canonical judgment is to be upheld against him, namely that he lose both.

units.la: De conductitijs presbyteris.
units.tr: On hired priests.

units.la: 21.q.2. 21.q.2. Præcipimus.) Præcipimus etiam,ne conductitijs presbyteris ecclesia committatur, sed vnaquæq; ecclesia cui facultas suppetit,pro prium habeat sacerdotem.
units.tr: 21.q.2. 21.q.2. We also command that the congregation not be entrusted to hired priests, but that each church, where it has the means, should have its own priest.)

units.la: De Quæstionarijs & Curtisanis. Ex Concilio Meldensi.
units.tr: On Questionaries and Courtiers. From the Council of Meaux.

units.la: 6.q.3. De illis autem.) De illis autem,qui infra parochiam beneficium aut hæreditatem habent,& alterius Episcopi parochiani sunt,& de loco ad locum iter faciunt,& rapinam & deprædationes peragunt,placuit vt excōmunicentur, nec ante ex parochia exeant;quâ quæ patrarūt[?] digné emendent. Quorum excōmunicatio seniori eorum & proprio Episcopo significanda est, ne eos recipiat antequam illuc redeant vbi rapinam fecerunt, & ibi omnia pleniter emendent.
units.tr: 6.q.3. De illis autem.) As for those who hold a benefice or inheritance within a parish, who are parishioners of another bishop, and who travel from place to place committing robbery and plunder, it has been resolved that they are to be excommunicated and not to leave their parish before they have duly made amends for what they have done. Their excommunication must be made known to their superior and their own bishop, so that he does not receive them until they return to the place where they committed the robbery and there fully make amends for everything.

units.la: Pro pallio nihil accipiendum.
units.tr: Nothing is to be accepted for the pallium.

units.la: Dist.99.C.Nouit.) Nouit sanctitas tua,quia prius pallium,nisi dato commodo,nō dabatur. Quod quia incongruum erat,facto Concilio ad te[?] corpus Petri Apostolorum principis, tam de hoc, quàm de eorum ordinationibus aliquid accipere, sub districta interdictione vetuimus. Oportet ergo, vt neq; per commodum, neque per gratiam, aut quorundam supplicationibus aliquos ad sacros ordines consentiatis vel permittatis adduci. Gregor.
units.tr: Dist.99.C.Nouit.) Your holiness knows that formerly the pallium was not given unless a payment was made. Since this was improper, we have, at a council held at the body of Peter, prince of the Apostles, forbidden under strict prohibition that anything be taken either for this or for their ordinations. Therefore you must neither consent to nor permit anyone to be brought to holy orders by a payment, by favour, or by the petitions of certain persons. Gregory.

units.la: SENTENTIAE DE DE OFFICIO ET STVDIIS Sacerdotum & Episcoporum. CAPVT XXIII.
units.tr: SENTENTIAE DE OFFICIO ET STUDIIS SACERDOTUM & EPISCOPORUM. CAPUT XXIII.

units.la: Omne opus sacerdotum in prædica-tione consistere debere.
units.tr: The whole work of priests should consist in preaching.

units.la: Dist.38. Ignorantia.) Sacerdotes legere sanctas admonentur scripturas, Paulo Apostolo dicente ad Timotheum: Attende lectioni, & exhortationi doctrinæ, & semper permane in his. Sciant ergo sacerdotes sanctas scripturas & canones, & omne opus eorum in prædicatione & doctrina consistat, atq; ædificent cunctos tam fidei scientia, quàm operum disciplina.
units.tr: Dist. 38, Ignorantia.) Priests are urged to read the holy Scriptures, the Apostle Paul saying to Timothy: "Give attention to reading, to exhortation and to doctrine, and continue in these things." Let priests therefore know the holy Scriptures and the canons, and let their whole work consist in preaching and teaching, and let them edify all, both by the knowledge of the faith and by the discipline of good works.

units.la: Episcopos docere debere.
units.tr: Bishops ought to teach.

units.la: Dist.43. C. Sit rector.) Episcopi sine tintinnabulis incedunt, qui non prædicant Verbum Dei. Scriptum autem est: Sacerdos ingrediens vel egrediens, moritur, si de eo sonitus non audiatur.
units.tr: Dist. 43, C. Sit rector.) Bishops who do not preach the Word of God go about without bells. It is written: "A priest who goes in or comes out dies, if no sound is heard from him."

units.la: Item. C. Dispensatio.) Nicolaus Papa ipse dicit: Dispensatio est nobis cœlestis feminis iniun cta. Væ si non sparserimus, væ si tacuerimus.
units.tr: Likewise, C. Dispensatio.) Pope Nicholas himself says: "A dispensation has been enjoined upon us by heavenly decree. Woe to us if we do not sow; woe to us if we keep silent."

units.la: Substantiam sacerdotij nostri esse sanctam scripturam.
units.tr: That the substance of our priesthood is holy Scripture.

units.la: Dist.38. C. Omnes psallentes.) Substantia summi sacerdotij nostri sunt eloquia diuinitus tradita, dita, id est vera diuinarũ scripturarũ disciplina.
units.tr: Dist. 38, C. Omnes psallentes.) The substance of our highest priesthood is the divinely delivered words, that is, the true discipline of the divine Scriptures.

units.la: Gentilium libros Episcopos non debere legere. Ex Concilio Carthaginensi.
units.tr: Bishops ought not to read the books of the Gentiles. From the Council of Carthage.

units.la: Dist.37.C.Episcopus.) Episcopus gentilium libros non legat, haereticorum autem perlegat pro necessitate aut tempore.
units.tr: Dist. 37, C. Episcopus.) A bishop should not read the books of the Gentiles, but may read through the books of heretics when necessity or the occasion requires.

units.la: Et mox C.Sacerdotes Dei.)Ex Hier.ad Da-masum Papam. Sacerdotes Dei omissis evangeliis & prophetis, videmus comœdias legere, amatoria bucolicorum versuum verba cantare, tenere Vergilii in manibus, & id quod in pueris adest causa necessitatis, crimen in se facere voluptatis.
units.tr: And soon after, C. Sacerdotes Dei.) From Jerome to Pope Damasus. We see priests of God, leaving aside the Gospels and the Prophets, reading comedies, singing the amorous words of the pastoral verses, holding Virgil in their hands; and what is permitted to boys out of necessity, they make into a crime of pleasure in themselves.

units.la: Item.C.Legimus.) Ex Rabano de pressuris ecclesiasticis. Legimus de B.Hieron.quòd cum libros legeret Ciceronis, ab Angelo est corre-ptus, eò quòd vir Christianus paganorum figmentis intenderet. Hinc etiam filius ille prodigus in Euangelio reprehenditur, qui de siliquis quas porci comedebant, ventrem suum replere cupiebat. Hinc etiâ Origenes cyniphes & ranas quibus Ægyptij sunt percusi, dialecticorũ garrulitatem & sophistica argumeta intelligit. Ex quibus omnibus colligitur, quòd non est ab ec-clesiasticis secularium literarum quaerenda peritia.
units.tr: Likewise, C. Legimus.) From Rabanus, on ecclesiastical hardships. We read of blessed Jerome that, while he was reading the books of Cicero, he was rebuked by an angel, because a Christian man was giving attention to the fictions of the pagans. Hence also that prodigal son in the Gospel is reprimanded, who desired to fill his belly with the husks which the swine were eating. Hence also Origen understands the gnats and frogs with which the Egyptians were struck as the chattering of the dialecticians and their sophistical arguments. From all these things it is gathered that the knowledge of secular letters is not to be sought from churchmen.

units.la: Episcopum non debere rei familiaris curam gerere, sed tantum lectioni, oratio
units.tr: A bishop ought not to take charge of household affairs, but should devote himself only to reading, prayer,

units.la: ni,& praedicationi vacare. Ex Concilio Carthaginensi.
units.tr: and preaching. From the Council of Carthage.

units.la: Dist.88. C.Episcopus nullam.) Episcopus nullam rei familiaris cura ad se reuocet,sed lectioni & orationi, & verbo praedicationis tantummodo vacet.
units.tr: Dist. 88, C. Episcopus nullam.) Let no care of household affairs call a bishop back, but let him devote himself only to reading, prayer and the ministry of preaching.

units.la: Episcopos debere annuis vicibus ecclesiam visitare. Ex Concil.Tarraconen.
units.tr: Bishops ought to visit the church every year. From the Council of Tarragona.

units.la: 10.q 1.C. Decreuimus,ut antiquę consuetudinis ordo seruetur,& annuis vicibus diœceses ab Episcopo visitentur.
units.tr: 10 q. 1, C. Decreuimus: let the order of ancient custom be kept, and let the dioceses be visited by the bishop in yearly turns.

units.la: Quid Episcopi plebem docere debeat.
units.tr: What a bishop ought to teach the people.

units.la: 10.q.1.C.Placuit.) Inter alia doceant illos ut errores fugiant idolorum,&c.
units.tr: 10 q. 1, C. Placuit.) Among other things, let them teach those people to flee the errors of idols, etc.

units.la: DE VITA ET CONVERSATIONE clericorum. CAPUT XXIIII.
units.tr: ON THE LIFE AND CONDUCT OF CLERGY. CHAPTER 24.

units.la: Professionem operibus ostendendam. Ambrosius.
units.tr: A profession must be shown by works. Ambrose.

units.la: 22.q.5.Cauete.) Mendacium est se Christianum dicere & opera Christi non facere. Mendacium est Episcopum, sacerdotem vel clericum se profiteri,& contraria huic ordini operari.
units.tr: 22.q.5.Cauete.) It is a lie to say that one is a Christian and yet not to do the works of Christ. It is a lie to profess oneself a bishop, priest or cleric, and yet to act contrary to that order.

units.la: Dignitatem non facere Episcopum, sed vitam. Hier.ad Heliodorum.
units.tr: Dignity does not make a bishop, but life. Jerome to Heliodorus.

units.la: Non omnes Episcopi sunt Episcopi. Attende Petrū, sed Iudam considera, Stephanum suscipe, Nicolaum respice. Non facit ecclesiastica dignitas Christianū. Cornelius centurio adhuc ethnicus dono sancti Spiritus mūdatur. Presbyteros Daniel puer iudicat. Non est facile stare in loco Petri & Pauli, scilicet tenere locū iam cum Christo regnantium. Infatuatum sal ad nihilum prodest, nisi vt proijciatur foras, & à porcis conculcetur.
units.tr: Not all bishops are bishops. Consider Peter, but look at Judas; take up Stephen, but regard Nicolas. Ecclesiastical dignity does not make a Christian. Cornelius the centurion, still a heathen, is cleansed by the gift of the Holy Spirit. Daniel, a boy, judges the elders. It is not easy to stand in the place of Peter and Paul, that is, to hold the place of those who already reign with Christ. Salt that has lost its savour is good for nothing, except to be cast out and trodden under foot by swine.

units.la: De habitu clericorum. Ex Concilio Carthaginensi IIII.
units.tr: On the dress of clergy. From the Fourth Council of Carthage.

units.la: Clericus profesionem suam & habitu & inceßu probet, & ideo nec vestibus nec calciamentis decorem quærat.
units.tr: A cleric should prove his profession both by his dress and by his bearing, and therefore should seek adornment neither in clothing nor in footwear.

units.la: Clericos non debere vsurari. Ex Concilio Arelatensi.
units.tr: That clergy must not practise usury. From the Council of Arles.

units.la: Ministri qui fœnerantur, placuit iuxta formam diuinitus datam eos à communione abstinere.
units.tr: Ministers who lend at interest: it has been decided that, according to the form given by God, they are to be kept from communion.

units.la: Item ex Concilio Tarraconen. Canonum statutis firmatum est, vt quicunque in clero esse voluerit, emendi vilius & vendendi carius studio non vtatur. Quod si exercere voluerit, sohibeatur à clero. Vide ibidem plura.
units.tr: Likewise from the Council of Tarragona: it has been confirmed by the statutes of the canons that whoever wishes to be in the clergy shall not use the desire to buy cheaply and sell dearly. But if he wishes to practise this, he is to be barred from the clergy. See there for more.

units.la: Negotiatorem clericum tanquam pestem fugiendum. Hier.
units.tr: A clerical merchant is to be shunned as a plague. Jerome.

units.la: Dist. 88, C. Negotiatorem.) Negotiatorem clericum, & ex inope diuite, & ex ignobili glo-riosum quasi quandam pestem fuge.
units.tr: Dist. 88, C. Negotiatorem.) Shun a clerk who is a merchant, whether he has become rich from poverty or boastful from obscurity, as a kind of plague.

units.la: Dist. 46. C. Non licet) Non licet fœnerari ministris altaris, vel in sacerdotali ordine constitutis, vel usuras vel lucra quæ sexcupla dicuntur, accipere.
units.tr: Dist. 46. C. Non licet) It is not lawful for ministers of the altar, or for those established in the priestly order, to lend at interest, or to take usury or those profits which are called sexcuple.

units.la: Dist. 47. C. Episcopus.) Ex Canonibus Apostolorum. Episcopus aut presbyter aut diaconus, usuras à debitoribus exigens, aut desinat, aut certè deponatur.
units.tr: Dist. 47. C. Episcopus.) From the Canons of the Apostles: A bishop, presbyter or deacon who exacts usury from his debtors must either desist or certainly be deposed.

units.la: Et mox. C. Quoniam multi.) Ex Concilio Niceno. Quoniam multi sub regula constituti avaritiam & turpia lucra sectantur, oblitiqué diuinæ scripturæ dicentis: Qui pecuniam suam non dederit ad usuram, &c. mutuum dantes centesimas usuras exigunt, iustè censuit magna & sancta Synodus, ut si quis inuentus fuerit post hanc deffinitionem usuras accipiens, aut aliquam adinuentionem faciens, vel quolibet modo negotia transfigens, aut hemiolia, id est, sexcupla exigens, vel aliquid tale prorsus excogitans, turpis lucri gratia, deijciatur à clero, & alienus existat à regula.
units.tr: And soon after, C. Quoniam multi.) From the Council of Nicaea: Since many who are placed under a rule pursue avarice and shameful gain, and forget the divine Scripture which says, "He who has not given his money at usury," and so on, while those who lend charge a hundredth part as interest, the great and holy Synod has justly decreed that if anyone is found, after this definition, taking usury, or devising some contrivance, or conducting business in any way, or exacting hemiolia, that is, sixfold, or thinking up anything of the kind at all for the sake of shameful gain, he shall be cast out of the clergy and be a stranger to the rule.

units.la: Item paulò post ex Concilio Elibertino, Si quis clericorum detectus fuerit usuras accipere, placuit degradari & abstinere.
units.tr: Likewise, a little later, from the Council of Elvira: If any of the clergy is detected taking usury, it is decided that he be degraded and abstain.

units.la: Item Leo Episcopus Anatholio Episcopo. Virum catholicum & praecipuè Domini sacerdotem, sicut nullo errore implicari, ita nulla opum cupiditate violari.
units.tr: Likewise Leo, bishop, to Anatolius, bishop: A Catholic man, and especially a priest of the Lord, should be entangled in no error, just as he should not be violated by any greed for riches.

units.la: Sacerdotes & qui scientiam Domini tractant non debere agitare iudicium sanguinis. Ex Concilio Tolet. IIII.
units.tr: Priests and those who handle the knowledge of the Lord ought not to take up judgement of blood. From the Fourth Council of Toledo.

units.la: 23.q.8. Saepe.) Saepe principes contra quoslibet maiestatis obnoxios, sacerdotibus negotia sua committunt. Quia vero sacerdotes à Christo ad ministerium salutis electi sunt, ibi consentiant fieri Regibus iudices, vbi iureiurando supplicijs indulgentia promittitur, non vbi discriminis sententia praeparatur. Si quis ergo sacerdotum contra hoc commune consultum discurfor, in alienis periculis extiterit, sit reus effusi sanguinis apud Christum, & apud ecclesiam perdat proprium gradum.
units.tr: 23.q.8. Saepe.) Often princes entrust their affairs to priests, against whomever is liable to a charge of treason. Yet since priests have been chosen by Christ for the ministry of salvation, they should consent to become judges for kings only where indulgence in punishment is promised by oath, and not where a sentence of peril is being prepared. If therefore any priest, running counter to this common decision, has acted as an agent in the perils of others, let him be guilty of shed blood before Christ, and lose his own rank in the Church.

units.la: Et mox ex Concilio Toletano IX. His à quibus sacra Domini tractanda sunt, iudicium sanguinis agitare non licet.
units.tr: And soon after, from the Ninth Council of Toledo: Those by whom the sacred things of the Lord are to be handled may not take up judgement of blood.

units.la: Clericos ociosos fori obambulatores degradandos esse.
units.tr: Idle clerics who stroll about the marketplaces are to be degraded.

units.la: Dist.91. C. Clericus.) Qui verò non pro emendo aliquid in nundinis vel foro deambulant, ab officio suo degradentur.
units.tr: Dist.91. C. Clericus.) But those who walk about in the marketplace or forum, not to buy anything, shall be degraded from their office.

units.la: Clericos non debere militiae exercere.
units.tr: Clerics ought not to practise soldiering.

units.la: Dist.59.C. Clericum.) Cum discreti sint milites saeculi à militibus ecclesiae, non convenit militibus ecclesiae militare saeculo, per quod ad effusionem sanguinis necesse est peruenire.
units.tr: Dist.59.C. Clericum.) Since the soldiers of the world are distinct from the soldiers of the Church, it is not fitting for the soldiers of the Church to serve the world, for that necessarily leads to the shedding of blood.

units.la: Clericum militaria arma ferentem gradum amittere. Ex Concilio Meldensi.
units.tr: A cleric who bears military arms loses his rank. From the Council of Meaux.

units.la: 23. q. 8. Quicunque.) Quicunque ex clero videntur esse, arma militaria non sumant, nec armati incedant, sed professionis suae vocabulum religiosis moribus & religioso habitu praebeant. Quod si contempserint, tanquam sacrorum canonum contemptores, & ecclesiae authoritatis prophanatores, proprij gradus amissione mulctentur, quia non possunt simul Deo & saeculo militare.
units.tr: 23. q. 8. Quicunque.) Whoever seem to belong to the clergy shall not take up military arms, nor go about armed, but shall show the name of their profession by religious conduct and religious dress. But if they despise this, as despisers of the sacred canons and profaners of the authority of the Church, let them be punished by the loss of their own rank, because they cannot serve God and the world at the same time.

units.la: Ibidem, quòd Episcopis vel quibuslibet clericis non liceat nec suanec Romani Pontificis authoritate arma sumere, probatur.
units.tr: Likewise, in the same place, it is shown that it is not lawful for bishops or any clerics to take up arms, neither by their own authority nor by that of the Roman Pontiff.

units.la: Ité ex Concil. Tolet. C.clerici.) Clerici qui in quacunque factione arma volentes sumpse-rint,reperti,amisso ordinis sui gradu,in monas-terio perenniter tradantur.
units.tr: Likewise from the Council of Toledo, C. Clerici.) Clerics who are found to have taken up arms in any faction, having lost the rank of their order, are to be handed over to a monastery for life.

units.la: Item Ambrosius ibidem C.conuenior. La-chrymæ meæ arma mea sunt. Talia enim sunt munimēta sacerdotis, aliter nec debeo nec pos-sum resistere.
units.tr: Likewise Ambrose there, C. Conuenior. My tears are my arms. For such are the defences of a priest; otherwise I neither ought nor am able to resist.

units.la: Pro clerico non orandum, qui aut in bello, aut in rixa, aut in gentilium ludis perit. Ex Concil. Triburien.
units.tr: Prayers should not be offered for a cleric who perishes in war, in a brawl, or at the games of the heathen. From the Council of Tribur.

units.la: 23.q. 8. C. Quicunque.) Quicunque clericus aut in bello, aut in rixa, aut gentiliū ludis mor-tuus fuerit, neque in oratione pro eo postule-tur, sed in manus incidat iudicis, sepultura ta-men non priuetur.
units.tr: 23 q. 8, C. Quicunque.) Whatever cleric dies in war, in a brawl, or at the games of the heathen, let no prayer be requested for him; yet he shall not be deprived of burial, though he falls into the hands of the judge.

units.la: Aleatores & ebrios Episcopos & presbyteros excommunicandos. Ex Ca-non. Apost.
units.tr: Bishops and presbyters who gamble or drink are to be excommunicated. From the Apostolic Canons.

units.la: Dist 35. C. Episcopus.) Episcopus, aut presby-ter aut diaconus, aleæ atque ebrietati deserui-ens, aut desinat, aut certè damnetur. Subdiaco-nus autem, aut lector, aut cantor, similia faciés aut desinat aut communione priuetur. Simi-liter & laicus.
units.tr: Dist. 35, C. Episcopus.) If a bishop, presbyter or deacon, having given himself over to dice and drunkenness, either stops or else is condemned. If a subdeacon, a reader or a cantor does the same, let him either stop or be deprived of communion. Likewise also a layman.

units.la: Ebrij Clerici quomodo puniendi. Ex Concilio Agathensi.
units.tr: How drunken clerics are to be punished. From the Council of Agde.

units.la: Dist.35.C. Ante omnia.) Ante omnia cleri-cis vetetur ebrietas, quæ omnium vitiorum fo-mes ac nutrix est. Itaque is qui ebrius fuisse cō-stiterit (vt ordo patitur) aut 3o.dierum spacio à communione submoueatur, aut corporali sub-datur supplicio.
units.tr: Dist. 35, C. Ante omnia.) Above all, drunkenness is to be forbidden to clerics, since it is the kindling and nurse of all vices. Therefore, whoever is shown to have been drunk shall either be kept from communion for thirty days, as the rank allows, or be subjected to bodily punishment.
