units.la: Quomodo Sacerdotes se in conuiuijs gerere debeant. Ex Concil. Nauetẽ.
units.tr: How priests ought to conduct themselves at feasts. From the Council of Navailles.

units.la: Dist.44.C. Nullus.) Nullus presbyterorū, quando ad anniuersarium diem, trigesimū aut septimum aut tertiū alicuius defuncti, aut qua-cunque vocatione ad collectam conuenerit, se inebriare vllatenus præsumat, nec precatus a-more sanctorum, vel ipsius animæ, bibere, aut alios ad bibendum cogere, vel se aliena preca-tione ingurgitare, nec plausus & ritus incondi-tos & fabulas inanes ibi referre aut cantare præ-sumat.
units.tr: Dist. 44, C. Nullus.) When any presbyter gathers for the anniversary day, the thirtieth or seventh day, or the third day after someone's death, or for any other occasion of assembly, let him by no means presume to get drunk; nor, after saying grace out of love for the saints or for the soul of the dead man himself, let him drink, or compel others to drink, or gorge himself on another's grace; nor let him presume to recount or sing there unseemly applause, rough rites and empty tales.

units.la: Item ex eodem ibidem. Quando autem con-ueniunt presbyteri ad aliquod conuiuium, ali-quis prior illorum versum ante mensam inci-piat, & cibum benedicat, & tunc secundum or-dinem sedeant, alter alteri honorem præbentes, & per vices cibū & potum benedicant, & ali-quis de illorum clericis aliquid de sancta scri-ptura ptura legat. Post refectionem similiter hymnū dicant,ad exemplum Domini, sicut in cœna scisse legitur: Et se contineant omnes presbyteri (maximè in talibus locis) vt non vituperetur ministerium eorum.
units.tr: Likewise from the same place. When presbyters come together for some banquet, let one of them, the first in rank, begin a verse before the table and bless the food, and then let them sit according to their order, showing honour to one another, and by turns bless the food and drink. Let one of their clerics read something from holy Scripture. After the meal let them likewise sing a hymn, after the example of the Lord, as we read was done at the Supper. And let all presbyters restrain themselves (especially in such places), so that the ministry of them is not brought into reproach.

units.la: Nuptialibus conuiuijs clericos inter-esse non debere. Ex Concil. Agathensi.
units.tr: Clerics ought not to attend wedding feasts. From the Council of Agde.

units.la: Dist.34. C. Presbyteri.) Presbyteri,diacones subdiacones,vel deinceps, quibus ducendi vxores licentia modo non est,etiam aliarum nup-tiarum euitent conuiuia,nec his coetibus misceantur, vbi amatoria cantantur,& turpia,& ob-scoeni motus corporum choreis & saltationi-bus efferuntur,ne auditus & obtuitus sacris ministerijs deputati, turpium spectaculorum atq; verborum contagione polluantur.
units.tr: Dist. 34, C. Presbyteri.) Presbyters, deacons, subdeacons, and those beyond them, who are not now permitted to take wives, shall also avoid the feasts of other weddings, nor mix with those gatherings where love songs are sung and shameful things, and where obscene movements of the body are carried along in dances and leaps; lest their hearing and sight, set apart for sacred ministries, be polluted by the contagion of shameful spectacles and words.

units.la: Clericos non debere tabernas intrare. Ex Concil. Laodicensi.
units.tr: Clerics ought not to enter taverns. From the Council of Laodicea.

units.la: Dist.44. C. Non oportet.) Non oportet clericos seruientes a presbyteris vsque ad dia-conos, & deinceps ordinis ecclesiastici omnes, vsque ad ministros, aut lectores, aut exor-cistas,aut ostiarios, aut psalmistas,aut etiá eos, qui in proposito continentiæ sunt,tabernas(nisi causa necessitatis) intrare.
units.tr: Dist. 44, C. Non oportet.) It is not fitting for clerics serving under presbyters, down to the deacons, and all beyond them in the ecclesiastical order, down to ministers, readers, exorcists, doorkeepers, psalmists, or even those who are under a vow of continence, to enter taverns (unless from necessity).

units.la: Item ex VI. Synodo. Nulli clerico licet tabernam aut ergasterium (id est stationem) habere. Si enim huiusmodi tabernam ingredi prohibetur, quanto magis alijs ministrare in ea? Si quis vero tale quid fecerit, aut cessẹt, aut depona-tur.
units.tr: Likewise from the Sixth Synod. No cleric is permitted to keep a tavern or a workshop (that is, a booth). For if he is forbidden to enter such a tavern, how much more to serve in it? If anyone does such a thing, let him either cease or be deposed.

units.la: Item ex Concil. Carthaginen. IIII. clerici edędi vel bibendi causa tabernas non ingredia-tur, nisi peregrinationis necessitate compulsi.
units.tr: Likewise from the Council of Carthage IV: clerics shall not enter taverns for the sake of eating or drinking, unless compelled by the necessity of a journey.

units.la: Et mox Gregorius Natalem Episcopū corripit, quod pastorali cura relicta, conuiuijs oc-cuparetur.
units.tr: And soon after, Gregory rebukes Bishop Natalis, because, having abandoned his pastoral care, he gave himself to banquets.

units.la: De clericis scurrilibus.
units.tr: On scurrilous clerics.

units.la: Dist.46.C. Clericum.) Clericum scurrilem & verbis turpibus ioculatorem, ab officio esse retrahendum censemus.
units.tr: Dist. 46, C. Clericum.) We judge that a cleric who is a buffoon and a jester with shameful words is to be withdrawn from his office.

units.la: De clericorum leuitate.
units.tr: On the levity of clerics.

units.la: 2. q. 7. C. Secuti.) Nonnunquam multi Catholicorum in tantum mercedem amant iniquitatis, vt etiam docti ab indoctis, clerici à laicis merito redarguantur. Qui verò & iure comparantur prophetæ, qui verbis asinæ contra naturam loquentis corripitur, nec tamen à proposito prauii itineris retardatur. Beda in 2.epi. Pet.2.Cap.
units.tr: 2 q. 7, C. Secuti.) Many of the Catholics, not infrequently, love the wage of iniquity to such an extent that learned men are rightly rebuked by the unlearned, and clerics by laymen. Yet they are rightly compared with the prophet, whom the ass speaking against nature rebuked, and yet he was not turned back from the purpose of his wicked way. Bede, on 2 Peter, chapter 2.

units.la: Quod sæpe Laici Episcopis & clericis me-liores sint: vide 8.q.1. Vereor, & deinceps.
units.tr: That laymen are often better than bishops and clerics: see 8 q. 1, Vereor, and following.

units.la: Negligentes Episcopi canes potius appellandi quam Episcopi.
units.tr: Negligent bishops are to be called dogs rather than bishops.

units.la: Qui nec regiminis in se rationem habuit, nec sua delicta detersit,nec filiorū crimen correxit, canis impudicus dicendus est magis quam Episcopus.
units.tr: One who has neither kept account of the rule over himself, nor wiped away his own offences, nor corrected the crime of his sons, is to be called a shameless dog rather than a bishop.

units.la: Indignos sacerdotes corui similes esse.
units.tr: Unworthy priests are like ravens.

units.la: Non omnis qui dixit pax vobis, quasi columba est audiendus. Corui de morte pascuntur: Hoc columba non habet, immo de fructibus terrae viuit, innoces est victus eius. Hic in glosla additur. Coruo æquiparatur malus prælatus vel malus prælsbyter, in nigredine vitiorum, & in raucedine vocis, & in voracitate,scilicet mortuorum oblationum, & in fœtore Spiritus, & in garrulitate,& in furto.
units.tr: Not everyone who says "Peace be to you" is to be heard as a dove. Ravens feed on death; the dove does not do this, but lives on the fruits of the earth, and its food is innocent. Here it is added in the gloss: the wicked prelate or wicked presbyter is equated with the raven, in the blackness of vices, in the hoarseness of voice, in voracity (namely for the offerings of the dead), in the stench of the spirit, in garrulousness, and in theft.

units.la: De clericis diutius ab ecclesia sua absentibus. Ex Concil. Agathen.
units.tr: On clergy who stay away from their own church for long periods. From the Council of Agde.

units.la: Si quis in clero constitutus; ab ecclesia sua diebus solennibus defuerit, id est, nativitate Domini,epiphania, pascha vel pentecoste,dū potius saecularibus lucris studet quàm servitio Dei parere, convenit ut triennio à communicatione,suspendatur. Similiter diaconus vel presbyter,si per tres hebdomadas ab ecclesia sua defuerit,huic damnationi succumbat.
units.tr: If anyone who has been appointed to the clergy is absent from his own church on the solemn days, that is, at the Nativity of the Lord, the Epiphany, Easter or Pentecost, while he is more concerned with secular gain than with serving God, he shall be suspended from communion for three years. Likewise, if a deacon or elder is absent from his church for three weeks, he shall be subject to the same condemnation.

units.la: Venationes Episcopis prohibitæ.
units.tr: Hunting forbidden to bishops.

units.la: Dist.34.C. Quorumdam.) Exemplum ponitur cuiusdam Lanfredi Episcopi venationibus intenti, & iubetur admoneri, atque si desistere nolit, excommunicari.
units.tr: Dist. 34, C. Quorumdam.) An example is given of a certain Bishop Lanfred, who was devoted to hunting, and it is ordered that he be admonished and, if he refuses to give it up, be excommunicated.

units.la: Et ibidem mox sequitur. C. Episcopū. Ex Concilio Aurelianen. IIII. Episcopum, presbyterum aut diaconum, canes ad venandum, aut accipitres, aut huiusmodi res habere non licet. Quòd si quis talium personarum, in hac voluptate sæpius detentus fuerit, si Episcopus est, tribus mensibus à communione su-spendatur, Diaconus verò ab omni officio [?] & comunione suspendatur.
units.tr: And immediately after, in the same place, C. Episcopum. From the Council of Orléans IV: It is not permitted for a bishop, elder or deacon to keep dogs for hunting, or hawks, or things of this kind. But if any such person is often caught in this pleasure, if he is a bishop, he shall be suspended from communion for three months; but a deacon shall be suspended from all office [?] and from communion.

units.la: Et mox. C. Omnibus,) Omnibus feriis Domini venationes & syluaticas vagationes cum canibus, & ut accipitres aut falcones habeant, interdicimus.
units.tr: And soon after, C. Omnibus. We forbid hunting and wandering in the woods with dogs on all the Lord's days, and keeping hawks or falcons.

units.la: Dist.86.C. Esau.) Hieronymus in Psal.82. Esau venator erat, quoniam peccator erat. Et penitus non invenimus in scripturis sanctis, sanctum aliquem venatorem, piscatores invenimus sanctos.
units.tr: Dist. 86, C. Esau.) Jerome, on Psalm 82: Esau was a hunter because he was a sinner. And we find nowhere in the holy Scriptures any holy hunter, but we do find holy fishermen.

units.la: Satius esse paucos bonos habere ministros, quàm multos inutiles.
units.tr: It is better to have few good ministers than many useless ones.

units.la: Dist.23. C.) Tales. Tales ad ministerium eligantur clerici, qui digne possunt Dominica Sacramenta tractare. Melius est enim Domini sacerdotium paucos habere ministros, qui possint digne opus Dei exercere, quàm multos in utiles, qui ouns graue ordinatori adducant.
units.tr: Dist. 23, C.) Tales. Let such men be chosen as clergy for the ministry as can worthily handle the Lord's sacraments. For it is better for the priesthood of the Lord to have few ministers who can worthily carry out the work of God than many useless ones, who bring a grave burden upon the one who ordains them.

units.la: Deponendos esse illicite viventes.
units.tr: That those who live unlawfully are to be deposed.

units.la: Dist. 81. C. Maximianus.) Qui sancti non sunt, sancta tractare non possunt, atque alieni efficiantur à ministerio, quod viuendo illicite polluerunt.
units.tr: Dist. 81, C. Maximianus.) Those who are not holy cannot handle holy things, and they are to be removed from the ministry, since by living unlawfully they have defiled it.

units.la: Qualis debeat esse Clericorum conversatio. Isidorus.
units.tr: What the conduct of clergy ought to be. Isidore.

units.la: Dist. 13. C. His igitur.) His igitur lege patrum cauetur, vt à vulgari vita seclusi, à mundi voluptatibus se abstineant, non spectaculis, non pompis intersint, conuiuia publica fugiant, priuata non tantum pudica sed sobria colant, u-suris nequaquam incumbant, neque turpium occupationibus lucrorum, nō fraudibus cuiuscunque studium appetant. Amorem pecuniae quasi materiam cunctorum criminum fugiát, & secularia negotia, officiáque abnuant. Honoris gradum per ambitionem non suscipiant. Pro beneficiis medicinae Dei munera non accipiant. Dolos & coniurationes caueant. Odiū, aemulationes, obtrectationes, atque inuidiam fugiant. Non vagi oculis, non effreni lingua, aut petulanti fluidoque gestu incedant, sed pudorem & verecundiam mentis, simplici habi-tu incessuque ostendant. Obscenitate etiá me-brorum & verborum sicut & operum penitus exercentur. Viduarum & virginum frequenta-tiones penitus fugiant. Contubernia extranea-rum fœminarum nullatenus appetant. Casti-moniam quoque non violati corporis perpe-tuo obseruare studeant, AUT CERTE UNIUS MATRIMONII VINCULO FOEDERENTUR. Senioribus quoque de-bitam prebeant obedientiam, neque ullius ia-stantiæ studio semetipsos attollant. Postremò, doctrinæ, lectionibus, psalmis, hymnis, canticis, exercitio iugiter incumbant. Tales enim debet esse, qui divinis cultibus sese emancipados stu-dent, scilicet ut dùm scientiæ operam dant, do-ctrinæ gratiam populis administrent.
units.tr: Dist. 13, C. His igitur.) By the law of the Fathers it is therefore provided that, set apart from ordinary life, they abstain from worldly pleasures; that they take no part in spectacles or processions; that they avoid public feasts and cultivate a private life that is not only chaste but sober; that they by no means devote themselves to usury, nor seek after any shameful gains from occupations or any kind of fraud. Let them flee the love of money as the root of all crimes, and let them refuse secular business and offices. Let them not receive a rank of honour through ambition. Let them not accept gifts in return for the benefits of God's medicine. Let them beware of deceit and conspiracies. Let them flee hatred, rivalry, slander and envy. Let them not walk with wandering eyes, an unbridled tongue, or a wanton and loose gesture, but show modesty and the shame of a sound mind by their plain dress and bearing. Let them be entirely free from obscenity of body, words and deeds. Let them completely avoid visits to widows and virgins. Let them never seek the company of strange women in their dwellings. Let them also strive always to keep chastity of an undefiled body, or else be bound by the bond of one marriage. Let them also show due obedience to their elders, and not exalt themselves out of a desire for any distinction. Finally, let them constantly devote themselves to teaching, reading, psalms, hymns, canticles and practice. For such ought those to be who strive to dedicate themselves to divine worship, so that, while they labour at learning, they may impart the grace of teaching to the people.

units.la: CONTRA LUXUM Sacerdotum.
units.tr: Against the luxury of priests.

units.la: CAPUT XXV. Clericos secularia non debere tractare.
units.tr: CHAPTER XXV. That clerics ought not to deal with secular affairs.

units.la: Dist.10. C. Quoniam idem.)
units.tr: Dist. 10, C. Quoniam idem.)

units.la: Item 21.q.3. Mollicijs.) Mollicijs & seculari-bus rebus laqueisque obligari non debent, qui diuinis rebus & spiritualibus occupati sunt, nec ad terrenos, & seculares actus uacare. Vide ibidem plura.
units.tr: Likewise 21, q. 3, Mollicijs.) Those who are occupied with divine and spiritual things ought not to be bound by soft living and worldly entanglements, nor to be free for earthly and secular business. See there for more.

units.la: Dist.88. C.Episcopus.) Ex Can.Apost. Episcopus aut sacerdos aut diaconus, nequaquam seculi curas assumat, sin aliter, deijciantur.
units.tr: Dist. 88, C. Episcopus.) From the Apostolic Canons: a bishop, a priest or a deacon must in no way take up the cares of the world; otherwise let him be deposed.

units.la: Item ex concilio Carthaginen.III. Episcopus nullam rei familiaris curam ad se revocet, sed lectioni & orationi, & verbo praedicationis tantummodo vacet.
units.tr: Likewise from the Third Council of Carthage: a bishop should not take upon himself any care of family property, but should devote himself only to reading, prayer and the ministry of preaching the Word.

units.la: Clericos nihil proprij possidere debere.
units.tr: Clerics ought to possess nothing of their own.

units.la: 12.q.1.Clericus.) Qui Dominum possidet & vna cum propheta dicat, pars mea Dominus, nihil extra Dominum habere potest. Quod si quippiam aliud habuerit praeter Dominum, pars eius non erit Dominus; verbi gratia: si aurum, si argentum, seu possessiones, si varia supellectile, cum istis partibus non dignatur Dominus fieri pars eius.
units.tr: 12, q. 1, Clericus.) He who possesses the Lord, and says with the prophet, "The Lord is my portion," can have nothing outside the Lord. But if he has anything besides the Lord, the Lord will not be his portion; for example, if gold, silver or estates, or various household goods, the Lord does not deign to become his portion along with those portions.

units.la: Et mox. Cui portio Deus est, nihil debet curare nisi Deum. Vide ibidem plura.
units.tr: And soon after: he to whom God is his portion ought to care for nothing but God. See there for more.

units.la: Clericis non licere sua repetere.
units.tr: Clerics may not reclaim what is their own.

units.la: 14.q.1. Quod autem sua repetere non possint, facile videtur probari. Ait enim Dominus, si vis perfectus esse, vade & vende omnia quae habes, & da pauperibus. Quia ergo isti iter perfectionis arripiunt, non licet eis sua habere; Multo ergo minus licet eis repetere, quia non debet repeti quod possideri non licet.
units.tr: 14, q. 1. That they cannot reclaim their own things is easily shown. For the Lord says, "If you want to be perfect, go and sell all that you have and give it to the poor." Since, therefore, these men take up the way of perfection, it is not lawful for them to have their own things; much less, then, is it lawful for them to reclaim them, since what it is not lawful to possess ought not to be reclaimed.

units.la: H
units.tr: H

units.la: Episcopi victus et supellex qualis esse debeat.
units.tr: What the bishop's food and furniture ought to be like.

units.la: Dist.41. C. Episcopus.) Episcopus vilem supellectilem & mensam ac victum pauperè habeat,& dignitatis suae auctoritatem,fidei & vitae meritis quaerat,hospitium quoque non longè ab ecclesia habeat.
units.tr: Dist. 41, C. Episcopus.) A bishop should have cheap furniture, a plain table and poor fare, and should seek the authority of his dignity from the merits of his faith and life. He should also have a lodging not far from the church.

units.la: De habitu clericorum. Ex Concil.Carthaginen.IIII.
units.tr: On the dress of clerics. From the Fourth Council of Carthage.

units.la: Dist.41.C.Clericus.) Clericus professionem suâ & habitu & incessu probet, & ideo nec vestibus nec calceamentis decorem quaerat.
units.tr: Dist. 41, C. Clericus.) A cleric should commend his profession by his dress, bearing and gait, and therefore should seek no finery in either clothes or shoes.

units.la: De luxu sacerdotum. Hier.
units.tr: On the luxury of priests. Jerome.

units.la: Dist.44. C.Cum autem.) Tibi ò sacerdos de altari viuere non luxuriari permittitur. Ibidé, quòd non ebrietati vacare debeant,aut gulæ.
units.tr: Dist. 44, C. Cum autem.) To you, O priest, it is permitted to live from the altar, but not to live in luxury. There too: that they ought not to give themselves to drunkenness or gluttony.

units.la: 12.q. 2. Gloria Episcopi.) Hier. ad Paulinum. Crates ille Thebanus, homo quondam ditissimus,cum ad philosophandum Athenas perge-ret,magnum auri pondus abiecit, neque putauit se posse & virtutes & diuitias simul posse-dere. Nos suffarcinati auro Christum pauperem sequimur, & sub praetextu eleemosynae pristinis opibus incubantes, quomodo possumus aliena fideliter distribuere, qui nostra timidè reseruamus?
units.tr: 12, q. 2, Gloria Episcopi.) Jerome to Paulinus: That Theban Crates, once a very rich man, when he was setting out for Athens to study philosophy, threw away a great weight of gold, for he did not think he could possess both virtue and riches at the same time. We, loaded down with gold, follow the poor Christ, and, under the pretext of almsgiving, clinging to our former wealth, how can we faithfully distribute what belongs to others when we timidly hoard what is our own?

units.la: De vestitu Clericorum.
units.tr: On the clothing of clerics.

units.la: 21.q.4.C. Omnis.) Omnis iactura & ornatu-ra corporalis à sacrato ordine aliena est. Eos er-go Episcopos vel clericos, qui se fulgidis & cla-ris vestibus ornant, emendari oportet. Quòd si in hoc permáserint, epitimio (id est suspensio-ni vnius septimanæ, vt glossator habet, Epiti-mium dicitur increpatio, vel est genus poenæ) contradantur, similiter & eos qui vnguentis vnguntur, &c. Ex V II. Synodo.
units.tr: 21, q. 4, C. Omnis.) Every ostentation and bodily adornment is foreign to the sacred order. Therefore those bishops or clerics who adorn themselves with shining and bright garments ought to be corrected. But if they persist in this, let them be put under epitimion (that is, suspension for one week, as the glossator has it; epitimion is called a rebuke, or is a kind of punishment); likewise those who anoint themselves with ointments, etc. From the Seventh Synod.

units.la: Et mox. Prisci enim temporibus, omnis sacratus vir cum mediocri aut vili veste conuer-sabatur. Omne quippe quod non propter necessitatę suâ sed propter venustatę accipitur, elationis habet calumniâ, quemadmodû magnus ait Basilius. Sed neque ex sericis texturis ve-stem quis variatam induebat, neque appone-bat variorum colorum ornamenta in summi-tate vestimentorum, Audierat enim, quia qui in mollibus vestiuntur in domibus regum sunt.
units.tr: And soon after: For in earlier times every consecrated man lived in a moderate or plain garment. For whatever is taken not out of necessity but for elegance carries the charge of pride, as the great Basil says. Nor did anyone put on a garment woven of silk, nor did they add ornaments of various colours to the upper parts of their garments; for they had heard that those who dress in soft things are in the houses of kings.

units.la: Delicatulos principes ecclesiæ eijciendos in tenebras exteriores.
units.tr: Pampered princes of the Church are to be cast out into the outer darkness.

units.la: Dist.35.C. Ecclesiæ principes.) Ecclesiæ prin-cipes, qui delicijs affluunt, & inter epulas atque lasciuias pudicitiam seruare se credunt, prophe-ticus sermo describit, quòd eijciendi sunt de spaciosis domibus, lautisq; conuiuijs, & multo labore epulis conquisitis. Et si uis scire quo eij- ciendi sunt propter malas cogitationes & opera sua, euangelium lege. In tenebras scilicet exteriores, vbi erit fletus & stridor dentium. An nō confusio & ignominia est, Iesum crucifixū, pauperem & esurientē, fartis prædicare corporibus, & ieiuniorū doctrinam rubētes buccas, tumentiāq; ora proferre? Si in Apostolorum loco sumus, non solum sermonem eorum imitemur, sed etiā conuersationem & abstinentiam.
units.tr: Dist. 35, C. Ecclesiae principes.) The prophetic word describes the princes of the Church who abound in delights and believe they keep chastity amid feasts and wantonness: they are to be cast out of spacious houses and sumptuous banquets, and of foods sought out with great labour. And if you want to know where they are to be cast, because of their evil thoughts and works, read the Gospel: into the outer darkness, namely, where there will be weeping and gnashing of teeth. Is it not a matter of confusion and shame to preach a crucified, poor and hungry Jesus with bodies stuffed full, and to bring forth the doctrine of fasting with reddened cheeks and swollen mouths? If we stand in the place of the Apostles, we should imitate not only their preaching but also their way of life and abstinence.

units.la: Qui nam ecclesiam faciant speluncam latronum. Origenes.
units.tr: Who make the church a den of robbers. Origen.

units.la: 16. q. 7. Et hæc diximus.) Nūc autem arbitror templum Dei ex lapidibus viuis constructum esse ecclesiam Christi. Sunt autem multi in ea, non sicut condecet spiritualiter viuentes, sed secundum carnem militantes, qui & domum orationis de viuis lapidibus constructam, faciunt esse spelunca latronum actibus suis, non ecclesia Dei digni, sed spelunca latronum. Qui enim considerat, in multis ecclesijs talium Christianorum peccata inueniet, arbitrantes quēstum esse pietatem, & cum deberent de euangelio viuere, secundum quod decet viuere seruos Dei, hoc non faciunt, sed diuitias & multas possessiones acquirunt: nonne dices spelunca latronum factam esse sub illis ecclesiam? &c.
units.tr: 16, q. 7, Et haec diximus.) Now, however, I think the temple of God built of living stones is the Church of Christ. There are many in it who do not live as befits spiritually living people, but fight according to the flesh, and who, by their deeds, make the house of prayer built of living stones into a den of robbers, unworthy to be the Church of God but a den of robbers. For whoever considers will find the sins of such Christians in many churches, thinking godliness is a means of gain; and when they ought to live from the gospel, as the servants of God ought to live, they do not do this, but acquire riches and many possessions. Will you not say that under such men the church has been made a den of robbers? etc.

units.la: CAP.
units.tr: CAP.

units.la: DE FORNICATIONE Sacerdotum. CAPVT. XXVI.
units.tr: ON THE FORNICATION OF PRIESTS. CHAPTER XXVI.

units.la: Pudicos esse debere sacerdotes.
units.tr: Priests ought to be chaste.

units.la: Dist.43.C.Pudicus. Pudicus quoque debet esse sacerdos, vt & moribus & verbis pudorem indefinéter exhibeat. Vnde in Cáticis Cáticorum, Genæ sponsæ, id est, prædicatores turturi comparantur.
units.tr: Dist. 43, C. Pudicus. A priest too ought to be chaste, so that he shows modesty without limit both in his conduct and in his words. Hence in the Song of Songs the cheeks of the bride, that is, the preachers, are compared to a turtledove.

units.la: Fornicarios in sacerdotium non recipiendos.
units.tr: Fornicators are not to be admitted to the priesthood.

units.la: 1.q.7. Si quis omnem. Et si in fornicatione lapsus est aliquis post baptismum, in sacerdotium non recipitur, canones enim hoc prohibent. Si quis verò cum hoc peccato ad sacerdotium prouectus est, cognitus degradetur.
units.tr: 1. q. 7, Si quis omnem. If anyone has fallen into fornication after baptism, he is not admitted to the priesthood, for the canons forbid this. But if anyone has been advanced to the priesthood while guilty of this sin, and it becomes known, he is to be deposed.

units.la: De pœna sacerdotum fornicantium. Ex Can. Apostolorum.
units.tr: On the punishment of priests who fornicate. From the Canons of the Apostles.

units.la: Dist.81, C.Si quis Episcopus. Si quis Episcopus aut presbyter, aut diaconus, post diaconij acceptum gradum fuerit fornicatus aut moechatus, deponatur, & ab ecclesia proiectus inter laicos agat pœnitentiam.
units.tr: Dist. 81, C. Si quis Episcopus. If any bishop, presbyter or deacon, after receiving the rank of deacon, has committed fornication or adultery, let him be deposed, and, cast out of the Church, let him do penance among the laity.

units.la: Officium fornicariorum non audiendū.
units.tr: The office of fornicators is not to be heard.

units.la: Gregor.
units.tr: Gregory.

units.la: Dist.81.C. Si qui. Omnibus per regnū Italicum & Theutonicorum, Si qui sunt presbyteri, diaconi vel subdiaconi, qui in crimine forni-cationis iaceant, interdicimus eis ex parte Dei omnipotentis, & sancti Petri authoritate, eccle-siae introitum, vsq; dū poeniteant & emendent. Si qui vero in peccato suo perseuerare malue-rint, NVLLVS VESTRVM EORVM PRAE-SVMAT AVDIRE OFFICIVM, quia benedi-ctio eorum vertetur in maledictionem, & oratio in peccatū, testante Domino per prophe-tā, Maledicá inquit benedictionib. vestris. Qui vero huic saluberrimo praecepto obedire noluerint, idololatriae peccatum incurrent, Samuele testante, & beato Gregorio instruente.
units.tr: Dist. 81, C. Si qui. To all of you throughout the Italian and German kingdoms: if there are any presbyters, deacons or subdeacons who lie in the crime of fornication, we forbid them, in the name of Almighty God and by the authority of St Peter, to enter the Church until they repent and amend. But if they have preferred to persist in their sin, LET NONE OF YOU PRESUME TO HEAR THEIR OFFICE, because their blessing will be turned into a curse and their prayer into sin, as the Lord testifies through the prophet: "I will curse your blessings." But those who refuse to obey this most salutary precept will incur the sin of idolatry, as Samuel testifies and blessed Gregory teaches.

units.la: Clericos solos cum mulieribus versari aut miscere sermones non debere.
units.tr: That clerics alone should not associate with women or exchange words with them.

units.la: Dist.8i[?].C.Clericus. Clericus solus ad foeminae tabernaculum non accedat, neq; properet si ne maioris natu sacerdotis iussione. Nec solus presbyter cum sola foemina fabulas misceat. Nec archidiaconus sub prętextu humilitatis aut ossi-cij frequenter intret domicilia matronarū, aut forte per clericos aut domesticos matronae mandet aliquid secretė. Si agnitū fuerit, & ille depo-natur, & illa à liminibus ecclesiae arceatur.
units.tr: Dist. 81, C. Clericus. A cleric alone shall not approach a woman's dwelling, nor hasten there, without the order of an elder priest. Nor shall a presbyter alone mix talk with a woman alone. Nor shall an archdeacon, under pretext of humility or of duty, often enter the homes of matrons, or perhaps send anything secretly to a matron through clerics or servants. If it is discovered, let him be deposed, and let her be barred from the threshold of the Church.

units.la: Non esse audiendam missam presbyteri concubinam habentis.
units.tr: That the mass of a presbyter who keeps a concubine is not to be heard.

units.la: Dist. 32. C. Nullus.) Nullus missam audiat presbyteri, quem scit concubinam indubitanter habere, aut subintroductam mulierem. Hæc Nicol. Papa, omnibus Episcopis scribit.
units.tr: Dist. 32, C. Nullus. Let no one hear the mass of a presbyter whom he knows without doubt to keep a concubine or a woman brought in under cover. So writes Pope Nicholas to all bishops.

units.la: Et mox. C. Præter. Alexander II. Præter hoc autem præcipiendo mandamus, vt nullus missam audiat presbyteri quem scit concubinam habere indubitanter, vel subintroductam mulierem. Vnde etiam sancta Synodus hoc capitulum sub excommunicatione statuit dicens, Quicunq; sacerdotû, diaconorû, subdiaconorû post constitutû beatæ memoriæ prædecessoris nostri sancti Leonis Papæ & Nicolai, de caftita te clericorû, concubinâ palàm duxerit, vel duftam non reliquerit, ex parte omnipotentis Dei, & authoritate principum Apostolorum Petri & Pauli præcipimus, & omnino cõtradicimus, vt missas non cantet, nec etiam euangelium legat, neque epistolam ad missam, neque in presbyterio cum his ad diuina officia, qui prefatæ constitutioni obedientes fuerint, maneat, neque partem ab ecclesia suscipiat.
units.tr: And soon after, C. Praeter. Alexander II. Moreover, we command by this precept that no one hear the mass of a presbyter whom he knows without doubt to keep a concubine, or a woman brought in under cover. Hence also the holy Synod has decreed this chapter under excommunication, saying: whoever of the priests, deacons or subdeacons, after the decree of our predecessors of blessed memory, Pope Leo and Pope Nicholas, concerning the chastity of clergy, has openly taken a concubine, or has not put away the woman he has married, we command in the name of Almighty God and by the authority of the chief Apostles Peter and Paul, and utterly forbid, that he not sing mass, nor read the Gospel or the Epistle at mass, nor remain in the presbytery with those who obey the aforesaid decree for the divine offices, nor receive a share from the Church.

units.la: Clericos mulieres secum non debere habere, nisi forte matres, aut sorores, aut alias, quæ non possint esse suspectæ. Ex Niceno Concilio.
units.tr: Clerics should not keep women with them, except perhaps mothers, sisters, or others who cannot be suspected. From the Council of Nicaea.

units.la: Dist. 32. C. Interdixit.) Interdixit per omnia sancta synodus, non Episcopo, non presbytero, non diacono, non subdiacono, non alicui omnino qui in clero est, licere subintroductam habere mulierem, nisi forte aut matrem aut sororem, aut amitam, aut etiam eas idoneas personas, quae fugiant suspiciones.
units.tr: Dist. 32, C. Interdixit. The holy synod has forbidden absolutely that a bishop, a presbyter, a deacon, a subdeacon, or anyone at all in the clergy, be permitted to have a woman brought in under cover, except perhaps a mother, a sister, an aunt, or other suitable persons who avoid suspicion.

units.la: Et mox. Item Hieronymus. Hospitiolū tuū, aut raro aut nunquam mulierum pedes terant. Quia non potest toto corde cum Deo habitare, qui foeminarū accessibus copulatur, foeminae conscientiā secū pariter habitantis exurit. Nū-quā de mulierū formis disputes. Foeminae nomen tuum nesciant. Foeminā quā bene videris cō versante, mete dilige, nō corporali frequētia. Si bonum est mulierem non tangere, malum ergo est tangere.
units.tr: And soon after. Likewise Jerome. Let women's feet rarely or never tread your little lodging. For he cannot dwell with God with his whole heart who is joined to the company of women; the conscience of the woman living together with him burns him. Never dispute about the beauty of women. Let women not know your name. Love a woman who you see is living well with you in your mind, not by bodily frequency. If it is good not to touch a woman, then it is bad to touch her.

units.la: Dist.81. C.Oportet.) Gregorius. Neq; enim hoc silere debeo, quod cū graui animi tristitia & amaritudine dico. Sacerdotes cum foeminis habitare conspicio, quod nefariū est dicere vel audire, & contra sanctorū Canonū sancita. Vbi enim talis fuerit commorantium cohabitatio, antiqui hostis stimuli non desunt.
units.tr: Dist. 81, C. Oportet. Gregory. For I must not keep silent about this, which I say with heavy sadness and bitterness: I see priests living with women, which is wicked to say or hear, and contrary to the decrees of the holy canons. For where such cohabitation of people living together exists, the goads of the ancient enemy are never lacking.

units.la: Ite.C. Volumus. Symmachus, Volumus ut sacerdotes prohiberi debeāt, ne cū mulieribus cōuersentur, excepta dūtaxat matre vel sorore vel VXORE, quae caste regenda est.
units.tr: Item, C. Volumus. Symmachus: We wish that priests be forbidden to associate with women, except only a mother, a sister, or a wife, who must be kept chastely.

units.la: Et mox C.Legitur.) Legitur quod B. Augusti, nec cum sorore cohabitare consenserit, dicens, Quæ cum sorore mea sunt, sorores meæ non sunt.
units.tr: And soon after, C. Legitur. It is read that blessed Augustine did not consent even to live with his sister, saying: "Those who are with my sister are not my sisters."

units.la: Item C. In omnibus.) Certè solum ad solam accedere, nulla religionis ratio permittit.
units.tr: Likewise, C. In omnibus. Certainly no principle of religion permits one to approach a woman alone.

units.la: Item ex Concil. Carthaginen. C. Cum omnibus.) Cum omnibus omnino clericis extraneæ fœminæ non cohabitent, &c.
units.tr: Likewise from the Council of Carthage, C. Cum omnibus. No foreign woman shall live with any cleric at all, etc.

units.la: Item ex Concil. Toletano. C. Quidam.) Clerici legitimum non habentes coniugium, extra nearum mulierum vel ancillarum suarum (quæ interdicta sunt) consortia appetunt. Ideo quæcunque clericis taliter coniunctæ sunt, ab Episcopo auferantur & venundentur, illis pro tempore relegatis ad pœnitentiam, quos sua libidine infecerunt.
units.tr: Likewise from the Council of Toledo, C. Quidam. Clerics who do not have a lawful marriage seek the company of women outside their own kin or of their maidservants, which are forbidden. Therefore, whatever women are joined to clerics in this way are to be removed by the bishop and sold, while the men who have defiled them by their lust are exiled for a time to penance.

units.la: Item. C. Fœminas.) Siricius Papa. Fœminas non alias in domo clericorum esse patimur, nisi eas tantum, quas propter solas necessitudinis causas habitare cum eis Synodus Nicena permisit.
units.tr: Likewise, C. Feminas. Pope Siricius: We do not allow women to be in the house of clerics otherwise than those only whom the Synod of Nicaea permitted to live with them for the sole reasons of close kinship.

units.la: De pœna sacerdotum, ex quibus infantes procreantur. Innocentius.
units.tr: On the penalty of priests from whom children are born. Innocent.

units.la: Dist.81. C. Propositi.) Propositi quid de his observari debeat, quos in diaconij ministerio, aut in officio presbyterij positos, incōtinen tes esse aut fuisse, generati filij prodiderunt. De his etiam manifesta est divinarum legum disciplina, & beatæ recordationis Siricij Episcopi monita euidentia comonstrarunt, vt incōtinentes in officijs positi talibus, omni honore ecclesiastico priuaretur, nec admittatur ad tale ministerium, quod sola cōtinentia oportet impleri.
units.tr: Dist. 81. C. Propositi.) Concerning what ought to be observed regarding those who, placed in the ministry of the diaconate or in the office of the presbyterate, have been reported by their begotten sons to be, or to have been, incontinent. The discipline of the divine laws is plain on this point, and the admonitions of Siricius, Bishop of blessed memory, have clearly shown that incontinent men placed in office should be deprived of all ecclesiastical honour and not admitted to such a ministry, which can be fulfilled only by continence.

units.la: Quæ pœnitentia imponenda sacerdoti fornicario. Ex Gangren. Concilio.
units.tr: What penance is to be imposed on a fornicating priest. From the Council of Gangra.

units.la: Dist. 82[?]. C. Presbyter.) Presbyter si fornicationem fecerit, quanquam secundum canones Apostolorum debeat deponi, tamen iuxta auctoritatem B. Syluestri, si in vitio non perdurauerit, si sua sponte confessus adiecit vt resurgat, decem annis in hunc modum poeniteat. Tribus quidem mensibus à cæteris remotus, pane & aqua à vesperę in vesperam vtatur, tantum autem diebus Dominicis & præcipuis festis modico vino, & piscisculis atq; leguminibus recreetur, fine carne, & fagimine ouis & caseo vtatur, sacco indutus humi adhęreat, die ac nocte misericordiam Dei omnipotentis imploret.
units.tr: Dist. 82[?]. C. Presbyter.) If a presbyter has committed fornication, although according to the canons of the Apostles he ought to be deposed, nevertheless, according to the authority of St Silvester, if he has not persisted in the vice, and has confessed of his own accord and added that he will rise again, let him do penance in this manner for ten years. For three months he is kept apart from the others; from evening to evening he uses bread and water, and only on the Lord's days and the chief feasts is he refreshed with a little wine, and small fish and pulses. He abstains from meat, and uses neither lard nor eggs nor cheese. Clothed in sackcloth, he lies prostrate on the ground, and day and night implores the mercy of Almighty God.

units.la: Finitis tribus mensibus continuis exeat, tamen in publicum non procedat, ne grex fidelis in eo scandalū patiatur, nec enim debet sacerdos publicè pœnitere sicut laicus. Postea aliquātisper viribus resumptis, vnum annum & dimidium in pane & aqua expleat, &c. Vide plura ibidem.
units.tr: When the three continuous months are finished, he may go out, yet he should not come forward into public, lest the faithful flock suffer scandal from him, for a priest ought not to do public penance as a layman does. Afterwards, when his strength has somewhat returned, he should complete one and a half years on bread and water, etc. See more in the same place.

units.la: De Episcopis ferentibus fornicatio-nem suorum clericorum. Gregor. VII.
units.tr: On bishops who tolerate the fornication of their clerics. Gregory VII.

units.la: Dist.83. C.Si quis Episcopus.) Si quis Episcopus in fornicationem presbyterorum, diaconorum vel crimen incestus in sua parochia pretio vel precibus interveniente consenserit, vel comis-sum authoritate officij fui non impugnauerit, ab officio suspendatur.
units.tr: Dist. 83. C. Si quis Episcopus.) If any bishop, for a price or at the request of an intervening party, has consented to the fornication of presbyters or deacons, or to the crime of incest in his parish, or has not opposed what was committed while he held the authority of his office, let him be suspended from office.

units.la: Et mox Augus t. Episcopus qui talium crimina non corrigit, magis dicendus est canis im pudicus quàm Episcopus.
units.tr: And soon after, Augustine: A bishop who does not correct the crimes of such men is to be called an impudent dog rather than a bishop.

units.la: De spurijs clericorũ. Ex Conc. Tolet. IX.
units.tr: On the spurious children of clerics. From the Council of Toledo IX.

units.la: 15.q.8. Cum multae.) Cum multae super innocentia ordinis clericorum hactenus emanaverint sententiae patrum, & nullatenus ipsorum firmari correctio morum quiverit, usq; adeò sententiam iudicantium protraxère comis-sa culparum, ut non tantum inferretur ultio in actores scele-rum, verumetiam in progeniem damnatorum. Ideoq; quilibet abEpiscopo usq; ad subdiaconẽ deinceps vel ex ancillę vel ex ingenuę detestando cõnubio in honore constituti, filios procreaverint, illi quidem ex quibus geniti probabun-tur, canonica censura damnetur. Proles autem aliena pollutione nata, non solùm hæreditatem nunquam accipiet, sed etiam in servitutem eius ecclesiae, de cuius sacerdotis vel ministri igno-minia nati sunt, iure perenni manebunt.
units.tr: 15. q. 8. Cum multae.) Since many sentences of the Fathers have hitherto been issued concerning the innocence of the clerical order, and the correction of their morals could in no way be secured, the judges have so far extended the sentence concerning the crimes committed that the vengeance falls not only on the perpetrators of the crimes but also on the offspring of the condemned. Therefore, whoever, from a bishop down to a subdeacon, placed in honour, has begotten children in a detestable marriage, whether with a slave woman or a free woman, let those from whom they are proved to be born be condemned by canonical censure. Moreover, the offspring born of another's defilement shall not only never receive an inheritance, but shall also remain in perpetual servitude to that church in whose priest's or minister's disgrace they were born.

units.la: De pœna sacerdotum, cum filiabus spiritualibus (hoc est, his, quæ vel baptizarunt, vel quæ illis confessæ sunt) rem habentium.
units.tr: On the penalty of priests who have relations with their spiritual daughters (that is, with those whom they have baptized or who have confessed to them).

units.la: 30. q. 1. Si quis. Si quis sacerdos cum filia spirituali fornicatus fuerit, sciat se graue adulterium commisisse. Iccirco fœmina, si laica est, omnia derelinquat, & res suas pauperibus tradat, & conuersa in monasterio Deo vsq; ad mortem seruiat. Sacerdos autem qui malum exemplū dedit hominibus, ab omni officio deponatur, & peregrinado duodecim annis pœniteat, postea verò ad monasterium vadat, ibiq; cunctis diebus vitæ suæ Deo seruiat.
units.tr: 30. q. 1. Si quis. If any priest has committed fornication with a spiritual daughter, let him know that he has committed grave adultery. Therefore the woman, if she is a laywoman, should leave everything, give her goods to the poor, and, converted, serve God in a monastery until death. But the priest who has given a bad example to men shall be deposed from every office, and do penance as a pilgrim for twelve years; afterwards let him go to a monastery and there serve God all the days of his life.

units.la: Item. Non debet Episcopus aut presbyter commisceri cum mulieribus, quæ ei sua fuerint confessæ peccata. Si forte (quod absit) hoc contigerit, sic pœniteat, quomodo de filia spirituali, Episcopus quindecim annos, presbyter duodecim, & deponatur, tamen si in conscientiam populi deuenerit,
units.tr: Likewise. A bishop or presbyter ought not to have intercourse with women who have confessed their sins to him. If perhaps (which God forbid) this should happen, let him do penance as for a spiritual daughter: a bishop fifteen years, a presbyter twelve, and let him be deposed, if it has nevertheless come to the knowledge of the people.

units.la: Lapsos clericos non iterum in ordine assumendos.
units.tr: Fallen clerics not to be taken back into orders.

units.la: Dist. 50. Multis hoc agitur, quod lapsi non debeant iterum in ordinem assumi. Item quod post perpetratum homicidium, sacerdotale officium administrari non possit. Ibidem. C. Peruenit.) Gregor. Qui post acce ptum sacrum ordinem lapsus in peccatum car- nis fuerit, sacro ordine careat, & ad altaris mi- nisterium non acceda t.
units.tr: Dist. 50. Many matters are treated here: that the lapsed ought not to be taken back into orders; likewise that after a homicide has been committed, the priestly office cannot be administered. In the same place, chapter Peruenit.: Gregory. Whoever, having lapsed into sin of the flesh after receiving sacred orders, shall be without sacred order and shall not approach the ministry of the altar.

units.la: Item. C. Si post.) Martinus Papa. Si post or- dinationem suam quispiam in lapsum cecide- rit, & si præuaricationis peccato fuerit depre- hensus obnoxius, omnimodo prohibendus est cum manibus lutulentis atq; pollutis mysteria nostræ salutis tractare.
units.tr: Likewise, chapter Si post.: Pope Martin. If anyone, after his ordination, has fallen into a lapse and has been found guilty of the sin of transgression, he is in every way to be forbidden to handle the mysteries of our salvation with muddy and defiled hands.

units.la: Mox tamen diuersum probatur. Nam C. Po- deret.) Calixtus Papa inter alia inquit: Errant itaq; qui putant, sacerdotes post lapsum si cõdi- gnam egerint pœnitentiam, Domino nõ posse ministrare, & suis honoribus frui, si bonam de- inceps vitam duxerint, & suum sacerdotiū di- gnè custodierint. Et ipsi qui hoc putant, non so lum errant, sed etiam traditas ecclesiæ claues de spicere videntur, de quibus dicitur: Quodcunq; soluueritis super terram, erit solutum & in cœlo.
units.tr: Yet soon a different view is set forth. For in chapter Poderet., Pope Callixtus says, among other things: They err, then, who think that priests after a lapse, if they have done worthy penance, cannot minister to the Lord and enjoy their honours, if thereafter they lead a good life and duly keep their priesthood. And those who think so not only err, but also seem to despise the keys delivered to the Church, of which it is said: Whatever you loose on earth shall be loosed also in heaven.

units.la: Presbyteros fornicantes minus seren dos quàm vxorátos. Ex Conc. Neocæsa.
units.tr: Presbyters who fornicate are to be punished less severely than those who are married. From the Council of Neocaesarea.

units.la: Dist. 28. Presbyter.) Presbyter si vxorem du xerit, ab ordine deponi debet. Quòd si fornica- tus fuerit, vel adulterium commiserit, extra ec- clesiam abijci, & ad pœnitentiam inter laicos re digi oportet.
units.tr: Dist. 28, Presbyter. A presbyter who takes a wife must be deposed from his order. But if he has fornicated or committed adultery, he must be cast out of the church and must be restored to penance among the laity.

units.la: Concubinas sacerdotum non seren-das.
units.tr: Concubines of priests are not to be tolerated.

units.la: Dist.27.C.Presbyteris.) Presbyteris, diaco-nibus, & monachis, concubinas habere, seu matrimonia contrahere penitus interdicimus.
units.tr: Dist. 27, C. Presbyteris. We utterly forbid presbyters, deacons and monks to keep concubines or to contract marriages.

units.la: Item. Dist.28.C. Decernimus.) Decernimus ut hi qui in ordine subdiaconatus & supra uxores duxerint, aut concubinas habuerint, officio atque ecclesiastico beneficio careant. Cum enim ipsi templum & vasa Domini, sacrariū spiritus sancti debeant esse & dici, indignum eos est cubilibus & immunditijs deseruire. Innocentij II.
units.tr: Likewise. Dist. 28, C. Decernimus. We decree that those who, in the order of subdeacon or above, have taken wives or kept concubines shall be deprived of office and of ecclesiastical benefice. For since they ought to be and to be called the temple and vessels of the Lord, the sanctuary of the Holy Spirit, it is unworthy of them to serve bedchambers and uncleanness. Innocent II.

units.la: Castitatem servandam clericis.
units.tr: Chastity is to be observed by the clergy.

units.la: Dist.28.C.Priusquam.) Scribit Gregorius nobilibus civibus Neapolitanis de Ioanne quodam qui filiam habebat paruulam, & tamen ab illis electus erat in Episcopum, & nō vult eum confirmare, dicens, quòd nec ipsi eum eligere debuissent, nec ipse electioni consentire, cùm (filia teste) convincatur corporis sui continentiam non habuisse.
units.tr: Dist. 28, C. Priusquam. Gregory writes to the noble citizens of Naples about a certain John, who had a little daughter, and yet had been chosen by them as bishop. He does not wish to confirm him, saying that they ought not to have chosen him, nor he consented to the election, since (his daughter being the witness) he is convicted of not having kept the continence of his body.

units.la: Et mox. C.De his.) Subdiaconibus cum ad diaconatum promoti sint praecipitur, ne quando suæ sponsionis immemores, aut ad terrenas nuptias, aut ad furtivos concubitus ultro concurrant.
units.tr: And soon after. C. De his. Subdeacons, when they are promoted to the diaconate, are commanded that they never, forgetful of their promise, rush of their own accord either to earthly marriages or to furtive concubinage.

units.la: DE CONIUGIO, SECUNDIS nuptiis, & divortio. CAPUT XXVII.
units.tr: ON MARRIAGE, SECOND MARRIAGES, AND DIVORCE. CHAPTER XXVII.

units.la: De contemptoribus coniugii. Ex Concilio Gangrensi.
units.tr: On despisers of marriage. From the Council of Gangra.

units.la: Dist. 30. C. Si quis.) Si quis propter Deũ virginitatem professus, in coniugio positos per arrogantiam vituperaverit, anathema sit.
units.tr: Dist. 30, C. Si quis.) If anyone, having professed virginity for God's sake, shall disparage with arrogance those who are living in marriage, let him be anathema.

units.la: Ibidem. Si quis vel virginitatē vel continentiam professus in coniugio tanquam abominabiles nuptias judicat, & nō propter hoc solū, quod continentiæ & virginitatis bonum sanctum propositum sit, anathema sit.
units.tr: Ibid. If anyone, having professed either virginity or continence, judges marriage to be abominable, and not only for this reason, that the good of continence and virginity is a holy purpose, let him be anathema.

units.la: Et paulò post ibidem C. Si quis.) Si quis nuptias in accusationem duxerit, & mulierem fidelem ac religiosam cum viro suo dormientem abominandam crediderit, aut etiam accusandam, tanquam nō posse coniugatos in regnum Dei ingredi, anathema sit.
units.tr: And shortly after, in the same place, C. Si quis.) If anyone has brought marriage into accusation, and has believed a faithful and devout woman who sleeps with her husband to be abominable, or even to be accused, on the ground that married people cannot enter the kingdom of God, let him be anathema.

units.la: Item. Dist. 31. C. Si quis.) Ex Conc. Gangren. Si quis vituperat nuptias, & dormientem cum viro suo fidelem ac religiosam detestatur, aut culpabilem æstimat, velut quę regnum Dei introire non possit, anathema sit.
units.tr: Likewise, Dist. 31, C. Si quis.) From the Council of Gangra. If anyone disparages marriage, and detests or considers blameworthy a faithful and devout woman who sleeps with her husband, as one who cannot enter the kingdom of God, let him be anathema.

units.la: Item. Quicunq; virginitatē custodiens aut cōtinentię studens, vel ut horrescens nuptias, nec propter hoc quod bonũ & sanctũ est, nomę virginitatis assumit, anathema sit.
units.tr: Likewise: whoever, keeping virginity or devoting himself to continence, or from a shuddering dread of marriage, and not for the reason that it is good and holy, assumes the name of virginity, let him be anathema.

units.la: SENTENTIAE DE- Secundas nuptias non damnandas.
units.tr: SENTENCES CONCERNING SECOND MARRIAGES: that second marriages are not to be condemned.

units.la: Dist.23.C.Qui Episcopus.In examine Episcoporum inter alia requiritur etiam ab eo, si nuptias non prohibeat, si secunda matrimonia non damnet, si carnium perceptionem non culpet.
units.tr: Dist. 23, c. Qui Episcopus. In the examination of bishops, among other things, it is required of him also whether he does not forbid marriage, whether he does not condemn second marriages, and whether he does not blame the eating of meat.

units.la: De secundis nuptijs. Chryfoft.
units.tr: On second marriages. Chrysostom.

units.la: 31.q.1.Hac ratione.) Hac ratione & Apostoli præceperunt fecundas adire nuptias propter in continentiam hominum. Nam fecundam quidem accipere fecundum præceptum Apostoli licitum est. Secundum autem veritatis rationē verè fornicatio est. Sed cum permittente Deo publicè & licenter committitur, fit honesta fornicatio. Vide an sic de permissionibus diuinis loquendum fit?
units.tr: 31 q. 1, Hac ratione. For this reason the Apostles also ordered second marriages to be entered into, on account of men's incontinence. For to take a second wife is lawful according to the Apostle's precept. But by the reason of truth it is truly fornication. Yet when it is committed publicly and with permission from God, it becomes honourable fornication. Consider whether one should speak in this way of divine permissions.

units.la: Sed mox ibidem Auguft.ad Pammachium, in Apologetico contra Iouinianū, C.Aperiant.) Aperiant quæso aures obtrectatores mei, & videant me fecundas nuptias & tertias in Domino concessisse. Qui fecundas & tertias nuptias non damnaui, primum potuì damnare matrimonium?
units.tr: But soon after, in the same place, Augustine to Pammachius, in the Apology against Jovinian, c. Aperiant. Let my detractors, I beg, open their ears and see that I have conceded second and third marriages in the Lord. Since I have not condemned second and third marriages, could I first have condemned marriage itself?

units.la: Idem. Non damno bigamos, imò nec trigamos, & fi dici potest, octogamos.
units.tr: Again. I do not condemn bigamists, nor even trigamists, and, if one may say it, octogamists.

units.la: Idem. Ego nunc voce proclamo libera, non damnari in ecclesia bigamiam, imò nec trigamiam, & ita licere quinto & sexto & vltra, quomodo modo & secundo marito rectè nubere.
units.tr: Again. I now proclaim with a free voice that bigamy is not condemned in the Church, nor even trigamy, and that it is lawful to marry a fifth and a sixth time and beyond, just as it is right to marry a second husband.

units.la: Et mox. Deus masculum & foeminam pro-pagandi generis causa nuptiali castitate coniun-xit, & secundas nuptias, quae in utroque Testa-mento permittuntur, licitas esse monstravit.
units.tr: And soon. God joined male and female in nuptial chastity for the sake of propagating the race, and he showed that second marriages, which are permitted in both Testaments, are lawful.

units.la: Item idem. Quod si dormierit vir eius, non dicit primus, vel secundus, vel quartus, nec no-bis diffiniendū est, quod non diffiniuit Apofto-lus. Vnde nec villas debeo damnare nuptias, nec eis verecundiam inferre numerositatis. Domi-nus autem septemuirarii[?] non damnauit.
units.tr: Likewise the same. "But if her husband has fallen asleep, the Apostle does not say first, or second, or fourth. Nor must we define what the Apostle did not define. Hence I ought not to condemn marriages, nor cast shame upon them for their number. But the Lord did not condemn the woman who had seven husbands."

units.la: 23.q.4. Quod autem.) Post mortem Sarae Abraham Cethuram duxit uxorem, ne secundum Augusti. Christiani putarent esse peccatum post mortem uxoris aliam ducere. Et mox idem ex Augusti. lib.2. contra aduersarium Legis & Pro-phetarum.
units.tr: 23 q. 4, Quod autem. After Sarah's death Abraham took Keturah as his wife, lest, as Augustine says, Christians should think it a sin to take another wife after the death of a wife. And soon the same from Augustine, book 2 against the adversary of the Law and the Prophets.

units.la: Coniugium cum infidelibus non con-trahendum.
units.tr: Marriage with unbelievers is not to be contracted.

units.la: 28.q.1. Caue. (Caue Christiane gentili aut Iudaeo filiam tuam tradere. Caue inquit gentilem vel Iudaeam atq; alienigenam, hoc est, omnem haereticam & alienam à fide tua accipere tibi uxorem, &c.
units.tr: 28 q. 1, Caue. Beware, Christian, of giving your daughter to a Gentile or a Jew. Beware, he says, of taking as your wife a Gentile, a Jewess, or a foreigner, that is, any heretic and anyone alien to your faith, etc.

units.la: Parentum consensum in nuptiis re-quiri.
units.tr: The consent of parents is required in marriages.

units.la: 30[?].q.5. Aliter.) Aliter legitimum non sit con[?] iugium nisi ab his qui super ipsam fœminâ dominationem habere videntur, & à quibus custoditur uxor petatur, & à parétibus & propinquioribus sponsetur, &c.
units.tr: 30[?] q. 5, Aliter. Otherwise a marriage is not lawful unless it is sought from those who seem to have authority over the woman herself, and by whom the wife is guarded, and she is betrothed by her parents and nearer kin, etc.

units.la: Et mox. Aliter vero præsumpta, non coniugia, sed adulteria, vel cōtubernia vel stupra, aut fornicationes potius quā legitima coniugia esse non dubitatur.
units.tr: And soon. But when marriages are presumed otherwise, there is no doubt that they are not marriages but adulteries, or cohabitations, or debaucheries, or fornications rather than lawful marriages.

units.la: 32.q.2. Non omnis.) Gratianus. Paterno arbitrio fœminæ viris iunctæ carent culpa.
units.tr: 32 q. 2, Non omnis. Gratian. Women joined to men by their father's decision are free from fault.

units.la: Et mox. Cum ergo dicitur paterno arbitrio fœminæ iunctæ viris, datur intelligi, quòd paternus consensus desideratur in nuptijs, nec fine eo legitimæ nuptiæ habeantur, iuxta illud Euaristi Papæ, Aliter non fit legitimum coniugium, nisi à parentibus tradatur.
units.tr: And soon. When it is said that women are joined to men by their father's decision, it is given to understand that the father's consent is required in marriages, and that without it lawful marriages are not held to exist, according to that saying of Pope Evaristus: "Otherwise a lawful marriage is not made, unless the woman is handed over by her parents."

units.la: Item Ambrosius in libro de Patriarchis: Ho-norantur parentes Rebecæ muneribus consu-litur puella, non de sponsalibus, illa enim iudi-cium expectat parentum, non est enim virgina lis pudoris eligere maritum.
units.tr: Likewise Ambrose in the book on the Patriarchs: "The parents of Rebecca are honoured with gifts. The girl is consulted, not about the betrothal; for she awaits the judgment of her parents, since it is not becoming for a virgin's modesty to choose a husband."

units.la: 36.q.2. Placuit ut hi.) Ex lib.1. Institut. de Nu-ptijs. Iustas autem nuptias inter se cives Roma-ni contrahunt, qui secundum præcepta Legis coeunt: Masculi quidem puberes, fœminæ viri potentes, sive patresfamiliâs sint, sive filijfami-liâs, dum tamen filijfamiliâs consensum habeant parentum, quorum in potestate sunt.
units.tr: 36 q. 2, Placuit ut hi. From book 1 of the Institutes, on marriages: "Lawful marriages are contracted between one another by Roman citizens who come together in accordance with the precepts of the Law: males who have reached puberty and females who are capable of marriage, whether they are heads of households or sons of households, provided that sons of households have the consent of the parents in whose power they are."

units.la: Nam hoc fieri debere, & ciuilis & naturalis ra-tio persuadet.
units.tr: For that this should be done is persuaded both by civil and by natural reason.

units.la: Pueros non esse matrimonio iungen-dos.Nicolaus Papa.
units.tr: Boys are not to be joined in marriage. Pope Nicholas.

units.la: 30.q.2. Vbi non est.) Vbi non est consensus vtriusq;, ibi nō est coniugium. Ergo qui pueris dant puellas in cunabulis, & è conuerso, nihil faciunt,nisi vterq; puerorum postquam venerit ad annos discretionis consentiat. Nec est coniugium nisi sit consensus vtriusq;,etiamsi pater & mater hoc voluerint & fecerint.
units.tr: 30 q. 2, Vbi non est. Where there is no consent of both, there is no marriage. Therefore those who give girls to boys in the cradle, and conversely, do nothing, unless each of the boys, after they have come to years of discretion, consents. Nor is there a marriage unless there is consent of both, even if the father and mother have wished it and arranged it.

units.la: Non iudicem, sed crimen facere diuortium. Isidorus.
units.tr: Not a judge but a crime makes divorce. Isidore.

units.la: 33.q.2. Quos Deus.) Quos Deus coniunxit, homo non separet. Quaeris quomodo subaudi, violenter,sine lege,absq; ratione,quos Deus cō iunxit homo non separet. Non enim homo separat quos poena condemnat, quos reatus accusat,quos maleficium coartat.
units.tr: 33 q. 2, Quos Deus. "Whom God has joined, let not man separate." You ask how: understand, violently, without law, without reason, "whom God has joined, let man not separate." For man does not separate those whom punishment condemns, whom guilt accuses, whom wrongdoing constrains.

units.la: Sine culpa relinqui posse vxorē, quæ cum fideli marito habitare non vult.
units.tr: A wife who is unwilling to dwell with a faithful husband may be left without fault.

units.la: 28.q.1. Vxor.) Vxor legitima societate coniuncta, sine vlla culpa relinquitur, si cum viro Christiano permanere noluerit.
units.tr: 28 q. 1, Vxor. A wife joined in lawful partnership is left without any fault if she is unwilling to remain with a Christian husband.

units.la: Et mox. Si aliquē cogat vxor sacrificare idolis,qui talem dimittit,causa fornicationis eā dimittit,non tantū illius,sed etiā suæ. Illius, quia fornicatur,suæ,ne fornicetur.
units.tr: And soon. If a wife compels a man to sacrifice to idols, whoever dismisses such a wife dismisses her for the cause of fornication, not only of her but also of his own. Of hers, because she commits fornication; of his, lest he should commit fornication.

units.la: Item. Non solùm mœchatio est illius, quæ carnem suam coinquinat, sed etiam quæ simulachrum facit, mœchatur. Quòd si in his factis perseuerat, & pœnitentiam non agit, recede ab illa, & noli viuere cum illa. Sin autem, & tu particeps peccati illius eris.
units.tr: Likewise. It is not only adultery on the part of the woman who defiles her flesh; she also who makes an image commits adultery. But if she persists in these deeds and does not repent, withdraw from her and do not live with her. But if you do not, you too will be a partaker of her sin.

units.la: Item ibidem. Ambr. Si infidelis, dicit Apostolus discedit, discedat, non est seruituti subiectus frater aut soror in huiusmodi, id est, si infidelis, noluerit esse cum coniuge sua fideli. Hic co-gnoscat fidelis suam libertatem, nec ita se subie-ctum putet seruituti, ut ipsam dimittat fidem, ne coniugem amittat infidelem.
units.tr: Likewise in the same place, Ambrose. "If the unbeliever departs," says the Apostle, "let him depart; the brother or sister is not under bondage in such cases," that is, if the unbeliever is unwilling to live with his believing spouse. Let the believer here recognise his freedom, and let him not think himself so subject to bondage that he should abandon the faith, lest he lose an unbelieving spouse.

units.la: Et mox ex August. Coniunx fidelis relin-quere coniugem licitè potest infidelem.
units.tr: And soon from Augustine: a believing spouse may lawfully leave an unbelieving spouse.

units.la: Item.28.q.2.(Si infidelis.)Si infidelis discedit odio Christianæ fidei, discedat, non enim est frater aut soror subiectus seruituti in huiusmodi, NON EST ENIM DIMISSO PECCATUM PROPTER DEUM, SI ALII SE COPULAVERIT. Ergo post dimis-sionem alii se copulare licet.
units.tr: Likewise, 28 q. 2 (Si infidelis). "If the unbeliever departs out of hatred of the Christian faith, let him depart; for the brother or sister is not subject to bondage in such cases. FOR THE ONE WHO IS DISMISSED DOES NOT SIN BEFORE GOD IF HE JOINS HIMSELF TO ANOTHER." Therefore, after dismissal, it is lawful to join oneself to another.

units.la: DE CONIUGIO SACER-dotum. CAPUT XXVIII.
units.tr: On the Marriage of Priests. Chapter 28.

units.la: Continentiam ministrorum altaris non fuisse semper.
units.tr: That the continence of ministers of the altar has not always existed.

units.la: Dist.28.C. De Syracusane.) Gratianus confi-tetur tempore Neocaesarienfis Concilij & Anchiritanae Synodi nondum introductam fuisse continentiam ministrorum altaris. Item: Orientalem ecclesiam non suscipere generale votum castitatis.
units.tr: Dist. 28, C. De Syracusane.) Gratian confesses that at the time of the Council of Neocaesarea and the Synod of Ancyra, the continence of ministers of the altar had not yet been introduced. Likewise, the Eastern Church does not accept a general vow of chastity.

units.la: 12.q. Praecipimus.) Sed notandum est Episcopos Orientales vxores habere & filios.
units.tr: 12.q. Praecipimus.) But it must be noted that Eastern bishops have wives and sons.

units.la: Clericis licere vxores habere. Ex Concilio Toletano.
units.tr: That clerics may have wives. From the Council of Toledo.

units.la: 33.q.2. Placuit.) Dicitur, quòd clericis, si vxores ipsorum adulterium commiserint, liceat eas sine mortis acerbitate habere in custodia, & ad ieiunia eas cogere, non tamen vsq; ad necem affligere. Ex quo sequitur manifestè, licere illis vxores habere.
units.tr: 33.q.2. Placuit.) It is said that if the wives of clerics commit adultery, it is permitted to keep them in custody, without cruel death, and to compel them to fast, but not to afflict them unto death. From this it clearly follows that it is lawful for them to have wives.

units.la: Coniugatos olim fuisse sacerdotes. Gratianus dicit.
units.tr: Gratian says that priests were formerly married.

units.la: Dist.56.C.Cenomanensem.) Cum ergo ex sacerdotibus nati in summos Pontifices supra legantur esse promoti, non sunt intelligendi de fornicatione, sed de legitimis coiugijs nati, quae sacerdotibus ante prohibitionem vbiq; licita erant, & in Orientali ecclesia vsque hodie eis licere probantur.
units.tr: Dist. 56, C. Cenomanensem.) Since we read that those born of priests were promoted to the highest pontiffs, they are not to be understood as born of fornication, but of lawful marriages. Before the prohibition, such marriages were everywhere permitted to priests, and it is proved that they are still permitted to them in the Eastern Church today.

units.la: De concubinis ducendis Ambrosius.
units.tr: Ambrose on taking concubines as wives.

units.la: 33.q.4. Dicat aliquis.) Praesta concubinę tuę libertatem & nomen vxoris, ne adulter fis potius verus quàm maritus.
units.tr: 33.q.4. Dicat aliquis.) Grant your concubine freedom and the name of wife, lest you become a true adulterer rather than a true husband.

units.la: Vxoratus quidam in Episcopatū promotus.
units.tr: A married man promoted to a bishopric.

units.la: Dist.28. C. De Syracusanæ) Quidam habens vxorem & liberos à Pelagio P P.cum non esset alius magis idoneus, intercedete Cethego patritio prætore, confirmatur in Episcopatu Syracuf.
units.tr: Dist. 28, C. De Syracusanae) A certain man who had a wife and children was confirmed in the bishopric of Syracuse by Pope Pelagius, since there was no other more suitable man, with the intercession of Cethegus the patrician, praetor.

units.la: Olim promotos subdiaconos non promissa continentia.
units.tr: Subdeacons who were formerly promoted without a promise of continence.

units.la: Dist.31. C. Ante triennium.) Hic glossator dicit. Olim promouebantur subdiaconi non promissa continentia, & licitè vtebantur vxoribus & beneficijs. Postea Pelagius prædecessor Gregorij statuit, vt vel contenti essent vxoribus tantum vel beneficijs tantum. De qua constitutione Gregor. facit mentionem 27.q.2. Multorum. Postea idem Pelagius aliam edidit constitutionem, in qua præcisè prohibuit, vt subdiaconi nullo modo comisceri debeant à modo vxoribus suis. Et illam constitutionem quidà subdiaconi seruabant, quidam non. Sed quia illa constitutio fuit (N. quod ipsemet confitetur eam iniquam fuisse) retractatur à Gregorio loco prædicto, & statuitur, quòd si qui subdiaconi non sunt, non cogantur continere, nisi velint. Si qui autem in futurum sint ordinandi, non admittantur, nisi promittant continentiam. Coniugatos presbyteros nō discernen dos, nec ab eorum communione abstinen dum. Ex Concilio Gangren.
units.tr: Dist. 31, C. Ante triennium.) Here the glossator says: formerly subdeacons were promoted without a promise of continence, and they lawfully used wives and benefices. Later Pelagius, the predecessor of Gregory, decreed that they should be content either with wives only or with benefices only. Gregory mentions this decree in 27.q.2, Multorum. Afterwards the same Pelagius issued another decree, in which he absolutely forbade subdeacons to have any intercourse with their wives. Some subdeacons observed this decree, and some did not. But since that decree was unjust (as he himself confesses), it is retracted by Gregory in the place cited, and it is laid down that subdeacons who are already in office are not to be compelled to continence unless they wish it. But those who are to be ordained in future are not to be admitted unless they promise continence. Married presbyters are not to be rejected or shunned in their communion. From the Council of Gangra.

units.la: Dist.28. C. Si quis discernit.) Si quis discernit presbyterum coniugatum tanquam occasione nuptiarum, quòd offerre non debeat, & ab eius oblatione ideo abstinet, anathema sit.
units.tr: Dist. 28, C. Si quis discernit.) If anyone rejects a married presbyter, as though on account of his marriage he ought not to offer, and on that ground abstains from his offering, let him be anathema.

units.la: Castitatem esse cū propria vxore con cubitum, etiam in Episcopis & presby teris.
units.tr: Chastity is intercourse with one's own wife, even in bishops and presbyters.

units.la: Dist.31. C. Nicæna Synodus.) Nicæna Synodus volens corrigere hominum vitam in eccle-siis commorantium, posuit leges, quas canones vocamus. In quorum tractatu videbatur aliqui-bus introducere legem, vt Episcopi, presbyteri, diaconi, subdiaconi, cum coniugibus, quas ante consecrati onem duxerant, nō dormirent. Surgens autem Paphnutius professor contradixit, Honorabiles confessus nuptias, & castitatem di-cens esse cum propria coniuge concubitū. Sua fit itaq; Concilio, ne talem poneret legem, gra-uem esse afferens causam, quę aut ipsis aut eorū coniugalibus occasio fornicationis exisseret. Et hoc quidem Paphnutius (licet nuptiarum esset inexpertus) exposuit, Synodusq; laudauit sen-tentiam eius, & nihil ex hac parte sanciuit, sed in vniuscuiusq; voluntate non necessitate per-misit.
units.tr: Dist. 31, C. Nicaena Synodus.) The Synod of Nicaea, wishing to correct the lives of men who dwelt in the churches, enacted laws, which we call canons. In the discussion of these, it seemed to some that a law should be introduced by which bishops, presbyters, deacons and subdeacons should not sleep with the wives whom they had married before their consecration. But Paphnutius, a confessor, rose and objected, declaring that marriage is honourable and that intercourse with one's own wife is chastity. Therefore the Council was persuaded not to make such a law, bringing forward the serious reason that it might become an occasion of fornication for them or their spouses. Paphnutius, although he had no experience of marriage, set this out, and the Synod praised his opinion and decreed nothing in this matter, but left it to each man's will and not to necessity.

units.la: Propter religionem coniugium non dissolvendum esse. Ex Gangrensi Concilio.
units.tr: Marriage is not to be dissolved on account of religion. From the Council of Gangra.

units.la: Dist. 39. C. Si qua mulier. Si qua mulier deserto viro discedere voluerit, soluto vinculo coniugali, nuptias contemnendo, anathema sit.
units.tr: Dist. 39, C. Si qua mulier.) If any woman, having deserted her husband, wishes to depart, the marital bond being loosed, and by despising marriage, let her be anathema.

units.la: Causa religionis coniugia non soluenda esse.
units.tr: Marriages are not to be dissolved for the sake of religion.

units.la: 27. q. 2. Sunt qui dicunt religionis gratia coniugia debere dissolui. Verum sciendum est, si hoc lex humana concesserit, lex tamen divina prohibuit. Per se enim Veritas dicit, Quos Deus coniunxit, homo non separet. Qui etiam ait, Non licet dimittere uxorem, excepta causa fornicationis.
units.tr: 27. q. 2. Sunt qui dicunt religionis gratia coniugia debere dissolvi.) Yet it must be known that if human law has permitted this, divine law nevertheless forbids it. For Truth itself says, "What God has joined together, let not man put asunder." He also says, "It is not lawful to put away a wife, except for the cause of fornication."

units.la: Et mox ex VIII. Synodo, Si quis coniugatus vult converti ad monasterium, non est recipiendus, nisi prius a coniuge castitatem profitente fuerit absolutus. Nam si illo viuente illa per incontinentiam alteri nupserit, procul dubio adultera erit, nec recipietur apud Deum eius viri conuersio, cuius sequitur coniugalis foederis prostitutio.
units.tr: And soon afterwards, from the Eighth Synod: If a married man wishes to be converted to a monastery, he is not to be received unless he has first been released by his wife, who professes chastity. For if, while she is still alive, she marries another through incontinence, she will undoubtedly be an adulteress, and the conversion of that husband will not be received before God, since it results in the prostitution of the marriage covenant.

units.la: Item Augustinus. Si tu abstines sine uxoris voluntate, tribuis ei fornicandi licentiam, & peccatum illius tuae imputabitur abstinentiae.
units.tr: Likewise Augustine: If you abstain without your wife's consent, you grant her license to fornicate, and her sin will be imputed to your abstinence.

units.la: Uxorem propter religionem non contemnendam. Ex Canonibus Apostolorum.
units.tr: A wife is not to be despised on account of religion. From the Canons of the Apostles.

units.la: Dist.28.C.Si quis.) Si quis docuerit sacerdotem sub obtentu religionis propriā uxorem contemnere, anathema sit.
units.tr: Dist. 28, C. Si quis.) If anyone teaches that a priest should despise his own wife under the pretext of religion, let him be anathema.

units.la: Dist.10.C.Lege.) Beatus Gregorius scribes ad Theotistam patritium, ait inter cætera, Si religionis causa coniugia debere dissolui dicatur, sciendum est, quia etsi hoc lex humana concessit, lex tamen diuina prohibuit.
units.tr: Dist. 10, C. Lege.) Blessed Gregory, writing to the patrician Theotista, says among other things: If it is said that marriages ought to be dissolved for the sake of religion, it must be known that although human law has permitted this, divine law nevertheless forbids it.

units.la: Nubentes post votum etiam non esse se parandos. Augusti.in lib.de bono coniugali,
units.tr: Those who marry are not to be bound even after a vow. Augustine, in the book On the Good of Marriage.

units.la: Dist.27.C.Quidam.) Quidam nubentes post votum asserunt adulteros esse, ego autem dico vobis, quòd grauiter peccant qui tales diuidut.
units.tr: Dist. 27, C. Quidam.) Some say that those who marry after a vow are adulterers, but I tell you that those who separate such people sin grievously.

units.la: Et paulo ante ex Decreto Martini Papae. Tanta est vis in Sacramento coniugij, quòd nec ex violatione voti potest dissolui ipsum coniugium.
units.tr: And a little before, from a decree of Pope Martin: so great is the force of the sacrament of marriage that the marriage itself cannot be dissolved even by the violation of a vow.

units.la: Idem copiose tractatur 27. q. 1. Nuptiarum, & obiectiones refelluntur.
units.tr: The same matter is treated at length in 27 q. 1, "Nuptiarum", and the objections are refuted.

units.la: Presbyteri et diaconi nullo modo a legitimis dissoluantur uxoribus. Ex VI. Synodo,
units.tr: Presbyters and deacons are in no way to be separated from their lawful wives. From the Sixth Synod.

units.la: Dist.31.C.Quoniam.) Quoniam in Romani ordine canonis esse cognouimus traditum, eos qui ordinati sunt diaconi vel presbyteri, confite[?] si,quòd non suis iam copulentur uxoribus, antiquum sequentes canonem apostolicæ dili-gentiæ,& constitutiones sacrorum virorum,le-gales nuptias à modo valere volumus, nullo modo cum vxoribus suis eorū connubia dissol-uentes,aut priuantes eos familiaritate adinuicē in tempore opportuno. Quicunque ergo dili-gens inuetus fuerit in subdiaconali ordinatio-ne aut diaconali aut sacerdotali, hi nullo modo prohibentur ad talem ascendere gradum, pro vxoris suæ cohabitatione, nec etiam tempore ordinationis suæ profiteri castitatem cogatur, quod abstinere debeant à legalis vxoris familiaritate.
units.tr: Dist. 31, C. Quoniam.) Since we have learned that it is handed down in the order of the Roman canon that those who are ordained deacons or presbyters should profess that they are no longer joined to their own wives, we, following the ancient canon of apostolic diligence and the constitutions of holy men, wish lawful marriages to remain valid from now on. We in no way dissolve their marriages with their wives, nor deprive them of mutual intimacy at the appropriate time. Therefore whoever is found diligent in the ordination of subdeacon, deacon or priest is in no way prohibited from ascending to such a rank on account of living with his wife, nor is he compelled at the time of his ordination to profess continence, namely that he must abstain from the intimacy of his lawful wife.

units.la: Deponendum eum qui aliquem presbyterū aut diaconorū priuare vult communione legalis vxoris.
units.tr: The one who wishes to deprive any presbyter or deacon of communion with a lawful wife is to be deposed.

units.la: Ibidem. Si quis igitur pręsumpserit contra Apostolicos canones aliquos presbyterorum & diaconorum priuare à contactu & à com-munione legalis vxoris suæ, deponatur.
units.tr: In the same place: If anyone presumes, contrary to the apostolic canons, to deprive any presbyters and deacons of contact with and communion with their lawful wife, let him be deposed.

units.la: Excommunicandum presbyterum et diaconum, vxorem religionis causa expellentem.
units.tr: A presbyter or deacon who expels his wife for religion's sake is to be excommunicated.
