units.la: Ibidem. Similiter & presbyter aut diaconus, qui religionis causa vxorem suam expellit, ex-communicetur. Si vero in hoc permanserit, de-ponatur.
units.tr: In the same place: Likewise, if a presbyter or deacon expels his wife for religion's sake, let him be excommunicated. But if he persists in this, let him be deposed.

units.la: Subiungit his Gratianus. Hoc autē ex loco intelligendum est, Orientalis enim ecclesia, cui
units.tr: Gratian adds to these: this passage is to be understood in this way, for the Eastern Church, to which

units.la: VI. Synodus regulâ vivendi præscripsit, votū castitatis in ministris altaris non suscepit, &c. Quasi non Apostolus omnibus dixerit, Episcopus sit unius uxoris maritus, & Dominus: Qui potest capere, capiat.
units.tr: the Sixth Synod prescribed a rule of living, did not admit a vow of chastity in ministers of the altar, etc. As if the Apostle had not said to all, "A bishop must be the husband of one wife," and the Lord: "He who can receive it, let him receive it."

units.la: De virginitate.
units.tr: On virginity.

units.la: 32.q.1. Nuptiæ terrâ implent, virginitas para-disum. Sed mox Gratianus addit. Verū hoc ad exhortationem non ad necessitatem obseruan-dæ virginitatis refertur. Unde Ambrosius ait:
units.tr: 32 q. 1. Marriages fill the earth, virginity paradise. But Gratian soon adds: Yet this is referred to exhortation, not to the necessity of observing virginity. Hence Ambrose says:

units.la: Integritas corporis expetēda à nobis est, quá ego pro cōsilio suadeo, nō pro imperio præ-cepti est. Sola est enim virginitas, quę suaderi potest, imperari non potest, res magis voti quàm præ-cepti est.
units.tr: The integrity of the body is to be sought by us, which I urge as counsel, not as a command of precept. For virginity alone can be persuaded, it cannot be commanded; it is a matter of vow rather than of precept.

units.la: CAPUT XXIX. DE MONACHIS, MONIALI-bus & claustris.
units.tr: CHAPTER XXIX. ON MONKS, NUNS AND CLOISTERS.

units.la: Monachos solitarios esse debere. Ex Nicena Synodo.
units.tr: Monks ought to be solitaries. From the Council of Nicaea.

units.la: 16.q.1. Placuit.) Placuit omnib. refidetibus in sancta Nicæna synodo, ut monachorum conversatio & vita secundum etymologiam nominis ab omnibus discrepet. Monachus enim Græcè, latinè singularis dicitur. Unde Monachum per omnia singulariter agere oportet. Quamobré firmirer & indissolubiliter omnes præcipimꝰ, ut aliquis monach. pœnitetiā nomini tribuat, nisi sibi invicem, ut iussum est: mor[?] tuum non sepeliat, ni monachum in monaste-rio secum commorantem, vel si fortuitu quen-quam aduenientium fratrum ibi mori conti-gerit.
units.tr: 16 q.1. It has pleased. It has pleased all who sat in the holy Council of Nicaea that the way of life and conduct of monks should in every respect differ from that of others, according to the etymology of the name. For "monk" in Greek means in Latin "solitary." Hence a monk ought to live in every way as a solitary. Therefore we firmly and indissolubly command that no monk shall assign penance to anyone, nor bury a dead person, unless, as has been ordered, the one who dies is a monk living with him in the monastery, or unless it happens by chance that one of the brothers arriving there dies.

units.la: Ibidem. Si cupis. Hier. ad Paulinum. Si cu-pis esse quod diceris, monachus, id est, solus, quid facis in urbibus? quæ utique non sunt so-lorum habitacula, sed multorum, &c.
units.tr: Ibid. If you desire. Jerome to Paulinus: "If you desire to be what you are called, a monk, that is, a solitary, what are you doing in cities? These are surely not dwellings of solitaries but of many," and so on.

units.la: Abbates etiam ostiario subesse debe-re. Ex Synodo Sylvestri.
units.tr: Abbots too ought to be subject to the doorkeeper. From the Synod of Sylvester.

units.la: Dist.93. C. A Subdiacono.) Abbates etiā Ostiario subesse iubentur, Dicitur enim ostiario Abbas, Abbati monachus in omni loco præsentent obsequium.
units.tr: Dist. 93, c. A subdeacon. Abbots too are ordered to be subject to the doorkeeper, for the abbot is called the doorkeeper, and the monk must show obedience to the abbot in every place.

units.la: Monachos ecclesiasticis deseruire nō posse. Gregor.
units.tr: Monks cannot serve ecclesiastical offices. Gregory.

units.la: 16.q.1. Nemo potest.) Nemo potest ecclesiasticis deseruire officijs, & in monastica regula ordinate persistere. Et mox inde cōcludi[?]t Gratianus, quòd parochianis ecclesijs monachi pręfici non posint.
units.tr: 16 q.1. No one can. No one can serve ecclesiastical offices and at the same time persist in good order under the monastic rule. And from this Gratian soon concludes that monks cannot be set over parish churches.

units.la: Et mox. Hier. ad Piarium & Desiderium.
units.tr: And soon. Jerome to Riparius and Desiderius.

units.la: Monachus non docentis sed plangentis habet officium, ne vel se vel mundum lugeat, & Do-mini pauidus pręstoletur aduentum.
units.tr: The monk has the duty not of teaching but of mourning, so that he may lament either himself or the world, and wait in fear for the coming of the Lord.

units.la: Item. C. Adijcimus. Leo Papa, Adijcimus il-lud etiam, quod nobis propter improbitatem quoquorundam monachorum religionis vestræ verbis mandastis per vicarios vestros hoc specialiter statuentes, ut præter Domini sacerdotes nullus audeat prædicare, sive monachus, sive laicus ille sit, qui cuiuscunque scientiæ nomine glorietur.
units.tr: Likewise, c. We add. Pope Leo: "We add also this, which you, the religious of your order, have ordered us to establish, through your vicars, because of the wickedness of certain monks: that, apart from the priests of the Lord, no one shall dare to preach, whether he be monk or layman, whatever learning he may boast of."

units.la: Ité. C. Hinc est etiam. Hier. contra Vigilantium. Monachus non doctoris sed plangentis habet officium. Et ad Heliodorum. Alia causa est Monachi, alia clerici.
units.tr: Again, c. Hence it is also. Jerome against Vigilantius: "The monk has the duty not of teaching but of mourning." And to Heliodorus: "The condition of a monk is one thing, that of a cleric another."

units.la: Et mox. Monachos vero vsque ad tempus Eusebij, Zosimi & Syricij monachos simpliciter & nō clericos fuisse, ecclesiastica testatur historia.
units.tr: And soon: that monks, down to the time of Eusebius, Zosimus and Siricius, were simply monks and not clerics, is attested by ecclesiastical history.

units.la: Monasteria olim fuisse scholas, ex quibus ministri sumpti. Hier.
units.tr: That monasteries were formerly schools from which ministers were taken. Jerome.

units.la: 16.q.1.C.Sic vive.) Sic vive in monasterio, ut clericus esse mercaris. Multo tempore disce quæ postmodum doceas. Et inter bonos, semper sectare meliores. Quòd si populus vel Episcopus te in clericum elegerit, age ea quæ clerici sunt.
units.tr: 16 q.1, c. Live thus. "Live in the monastery in such a way that you deserve to be a cleric. Learn for a long time what you will afterwards teach. And among the good, always follow the better. But if the people or the bishop chooses you as a cleric, do the things that belong to clerics."

units.la: Et paulo ante ibidé. C. De præsentium. Faciat autem Deus, ut tales sint hi, vel qui à nobis in isto habitu nutriuntur, vel in monasteriis crescunt, ut perfecta ætate & vita probata, non ad litigiorum officia, sed ad sacerdotium valeant promoueri.
units.tr: And a little before, in the same place, c. Of the present. "May God grant that these, whether those who are brought up by us in this habit or those who grow up in the monasteries, be such that, with mature age and a proven life, they may be fit to be promoted not to the offices of lawsuits but to the priesthood."

units.la: Abbates & Monachos nihil proprij habere. Ex synodo VIII.
units.tr: That abbots and monks have nothing of their own. From the eighth synod.

units.la: Dist.54. C.Abbati.) Abbati vel Monacho Monasterij seruū nō licebit facere liberū. Qui enim nihil proprium habet, libertatem rei alienæ dare non potest.
units.tr: Dist. 54, c. To an abbot. It shall not be lawful for an abbot or a monk to make free a slave of the monastery. For one who has nothing of his own cannot give freedom to another's property.

units.la: Monachos lucri gratia de monasterio non debere egredi. Eugenius Papa.
units.tr: Monks ought not to leave the monastery for the sake of gain. Pope Eugenius.

units.la: 16.q.1. Placuit communi.) Placuit cōmuni nostro Cōcil.ut nullus monachorū pro lucro terreno de monasterio exire nefādissimo ausu prę sumat. Neq; pœnitētiā dare, neq; filiū de baptismo accipere, neq; baptizare, neq; infirmū visitare, neq; mortuū sepelire, neq; ad ecclesiā secu-larem transire, neq; alijs qualibuscunq; negotijs sese implicare. Sit claustro suo cōtentus, quia sicut piscis sine aqua caret vita, ita sine monasterio Monachus. Sedeat itaque solitarius & taceat, quia mundo mortuus est, Deo autem viuit. Agnoscat nomen suū. Monos enim græcè, latinè est vnus. Achos græcè, latinè est tristis. Vnde dicitur Monachus, id est, vnus tristis. Sedeat ergo tristis, & officio suo vacet.
units.tr: 16 q.1. It has pleased. It has pleased our common council that no monk, for the sake of earthly gain, presume with most wicked daring to leave the monastery; nor to give penance, nor to receive a son from baptism, nor to baptize, nor to visit the sick, nor to bury the dead, nor to go over to a secular church, nor to involve himself in any other business. Let him be content with his cloister, for as a fish without water lacks life, so a monk without the monastery. Let him therefore sit alone and be silent, for he is dead to the world but lives to God. Let him recognize his name: monos [μόνος] in Greek means "one" in Latin, and achos [ἄχος] in Greek means "sad." Hence he is called monachus, that is, "one sad." Let him therefore sit sad, and be free for his duty.

units.la: Item Paulo ante, C.si cupis. Quem senseris tibi aut semper aut crebro de nummis loquente (excepta eleemosyna, quæ indifferenter omnibus patet) institorem potius habeto quàm Monachum. Præter victum & vestimentum & magnas necessitates, nihil cuiquā tribuas, ne filiorum panem canes comedant.
units.tr: Likewise, a little before, c. If you desire. Whomever you perceive speaking to you of money always or often (except alms, which is open to all alike), regard as a merchant rather than a monk. Beyond food, clothing and great necessities, give nothing to anyone, lest dogs eat the bread of the children.

units.la: Monachos debere laborare.
units.tr: Monks ought to labour.

units.la: De Con. Dist. 5. Nunquam de manu.) In desiderijs est omnis otiosus. Ægyptiorum monasteria hunc ordinem tenent, ut nullum absq; opere & labore suscipiant, non tā propter victus necessaria, quàm propter animæ salute, ne vagetur perniciosis cogitationibus, & ad instar fornicantis Hierusalem omni transeunti diuaricét pedes suos.
units.tr: De Con. Dist. 5, Never from the hand. Every idler is in desires. The monasteries of the Egyptians keep this rule: they receive no one who is not occupied with work and labour, not so much for the necessities of food as for the salvation of the soul, lest he wander about with harmful thoughts, and, like the harlot Jerusalem, spread his feet apart for every passer-by.

units.la: Carnem Monacho gustare non licere.
units.tr: A monk may not taste meat.

units.la: Ibidé. Carnem.) Carnem cuiquâ Monacho nec gustandi nec fumendi est concessa licentia.
units.tr: Ibid. Meat.) No monk is granted permission either to taste or to eat meat.

units.la: Monachis non licere ad fœminas accedere.
units.tr: Monks may not approach women.

units.la: 18.q. 2. Peruenit.) Neque commatres sibi facere, neque ad fœminas accedere monacho licet.
units.tr: 18.q. 2. Peruenit.) A monk may neither make spiritual co-parents for himself nor approach women.

units.la: Episcopos monasteria frequenter visitare, & corrigenda corrigere debere.
units.tr: Bishops should visit monasteries frequently and correct what needs correcting.

units.la: Ex Concilio Agathen.
units.tr: From the Council of Agde.

units.la: 18.q.2. Non semel.) Non semel sed sæpius in anno Episcopi visitent monasteria Monachorum, & si aliquid corrigendum fuerit, corrigatur.
units.tr: 18.q.2. Non semel.) Bishops should visit the monasteries of monks not just once but several times a year, and if anything needs correcting, let it be corrected.

units.la: Duplicia monasteria fieri non debere. Ex VII. Synodo.
units.tr: Double monasteries must not be founded. From the Seventh Synod.

units.la: 18.q.2. Diffinimus.) Diffinimus minimè duplex monasterium fieri, quia scandalum, id est, offendiculum multis efficitur.
units.tr: 18.q.2. Diffinimus.) We decree that a double monastery must by no means be founded, because it becomes a scandal, that is, a stumbling block, to many.

units.la: Et iterum. C. In nullo loco. Ex Registro Gregorij. Monachos & Monachas non debere cohabitare simul, sed & duplicia monasteria tollenda.
units.tr: And again. C. In nullo loco. From the Register of Gregory. Monks and nuns must not live together, and double monasteries are also to be abolished.

units.la: Item ex Concilio Agathen. Monasteria puellarum longius à monasterio monachorum, aut propter insidias diaboli, aut propter oblocutionem hominum collocentur.
units.tr: Likewise from the Council of Agde: convents of girls should be situated farther from the monastery of monks, either because of the snares of the devil or because of the talk of men.

units.la: Qua ætate virgines sacræ velandæ & consecrandæ sint.
units.tr: At what age consecrated virgins are to be veiled and dedicated.

units.la: 20.C.q.1. Iuuenculas.) Ante sexagesimum ætatis suæ annum virgines non consecrentur.
units.tr: 20.C.q.1. Iuuenculas.) Virgins should not be consecrated before the sixtieth year of their age.

units.la: Et mox ex Concil. Carthaginen. II. Sācti-moniales[?] ante annum quadragesimum non velentur.
units.tr: And soon after, from the Council of Carthage II: nuns should not be veiled before the fortieth year.

units.la: Item ex Concil. Aphricano IIII. Placuit ut ante vigintiquinque annos nec diacones ordinentur, nec virgines consecrentur.
units.tr: Likewise from the Fourth Council of Africa: it has been resolved that deacons are not to be ordained, nor virgins consecrated, before the age of twenty-five.

units.la: Item Pius Papa. Virgines non velentur ante vigintiquinque annos.
units.tr: Likewise Pope Pius: virgins should not be veiled before the age of twenty-five.

units.la: De Monialibus, & his qui cum illis scortantur. Gregor.
units.tr: On nuns, and those who fornicate with them. Gregory.

units.la: 27.q.1. Si qua.) Si qua Monacharum, vel per antiquiorem licetiam, vel per impunitatis pra-vam consuetudinem ad lapsum adulterij dedu-cta fuerit, aut in stupri fuerit deducta[?] voraginé, hanc, post competentis seueritatem vindictæ, in aliud districtius monasterium virginum in pœnitentia volumus redigi, vt illic orationibus & ieiunijs vacet, & sic pœnitendo proficiat, & metuendum cæteris arctioris disciplinæ præstet exemplum. Is autem qui cum huiusmodi fœminis in aliqua fuerit iniquitate repertus, omni communione priuetur, si laicus est, si vero clericus, à suo quoque remotus officio, pro suis continuo lugendis excessibus in monasterium detrudatur.
units.tr: 27.q.1. Si qua.) If any nun, either through an older license or through the wicked custom of going unpunished, has been led into the fall of adultery, or has been drawn into the abyss of debauchery, we wish her, after a fitting severity of punishment, to be sent to another, stricter convent of virgins to do penance there, so that she may give herself to prayers and fasting, and by penitence make progress and offer the rest an example of stricter discipline that they should fear. But the man who is found in any wickedness with such women shall be deprived of all communion if he is a layman; if he is a cleric, he shall also be removed from his office and thrust into a monastery, there to lament his continual excesses.

units.la: Mulierem religionis gratia non tondendam. Ex Gangrensi Concilio.
units.tr: A woman should not be shorn for the sake of religion. From the Council of Gangra.

units.la: Dist.30. C. Quæcunque.) Quæcunque mulier religioni iudicans conuenire, comam sibi amputauerit, quam Deus ad velamen eius, & ad memoriam subiectionis illi dedit, tanquam resoluens ius subiectionis, anathema sit.
units.tr: Dist. 30. C. Quæcunque.) Any woman who, judging it fitting to religion, cuts off her hair, which God gave her as a veil and as a reminder of subjection, as though dissolving the right of subjection, let her be anathema.

units.la: De his qui astu circumuenti in Monasteria detrusi sunt. Ex Concilio Maguntien.
units.tr: Those who were cunningly deceived and shut up in monasteries. From the Council of Mainz.

units.la: 16.q.7. Constituit.) Constituit sanè sacer iste conuentus, vt Episcopi siue Abbates, qui non in fructum animarum, sed in auaritiam & turpe lucrum inhiantes, quoslibet homines circumueniendo totonderūt, & res eorum tali persua-K sione furripuerūt, pœnitentiæ canonicæ, ut po-te turpis lucri sectatores subiaceant. Hi verò qui illecti comam deposuerunt, in eo quod ceperunt perseuerare cogantur, res verò eorum hæredibus reddantur.
units.tr: 16.q.7. Constituit.) This holy assembly has indeed decreed that bishops or abbots who, not seeking the fruit of souls but gaping after avarice and shameful gain, have shorn whomever they could deceive and have stolen their property by such persuasion, shall be subject to canonical penance, as pursuers of shameful gain. But those who, being enticed, have put off their hair shall be compelled to persevere in what they have begun, and their property shall be returned to their heirs.

units.la: Pertrusi in monasteria, praeter voluntatem, non retineantur.
units.tr: Those thrust into monasteries against their will should not be kept there.

units.la: 20.q.1.C.Sicut qui.) Extra voluntatem pro-priam retrusi, in monasteriis, non retinean-tur.
units.tr: 20.q.1.C.Sicut qui.) Those shut up in monasteries against their own will shall not be kept there.

units.la: Non licet novos ordines constituere.
units.tr: It is not lawful to establish new orders.

units.la: Ne nimia religionis diversitas grauem in ecclesiam Dei confusionem inducat, firmiter prohibemus, ne quis de cætero novam Religione inveniat: Sed quicunque ad religionem con-verti voluerit, vnam de approbatis assumat. Similiter qui voluerit religiosam domū de no-vo fundare, regulā & institutionem accipiat de approbatis. Cur ergo Iesuitarum & aliorum quorundam ordines posterius sunt inventi?
units.tr: Lest an excessive diversity of religious life bring serious confusion into the Church of God, we firmly forbid anyone from now on to invent a new religion. Rather, whoever wishes to be converted to religion should take up one of the approved ones. Likewise, whoever wishes to found a new religious house should take its rule and constitution from the approved ones. Why then were the orders of the Jesuits and certain others invented afterwards?

units.la: Hoc decretum[?] est in Concilio generali Lateranensi, sub Innocentio 3. anno 1215. Et citatur à Gregorio in Decret. lib. 3. De Religiosis domibus. Et appenditur.
units.tr: This decree is from the general Council of the Lateran under Innocent III, in the year 1215. It is cited by Gregory in the Decretals, book 3, On religious houses. And it is appended to that.

units.la: Illud etiam prohibemus ne quis in diversis monasteriis locum monachi habere præsumat,
units.tr: We also forbid anyone to presume to hold the place of a monk in various monasteries,

units.la: NEC VNVS ABBAS PLVRIBVS MONASTERIIS PRAESIDERE.
units.tr: No single abbot may preside over several monasteries.

units.la: DE IEIVNIO. CAPVT. XXX.
units.tr: ON FASTING. CHAPTER 30.

units.la: Depœnit. Dist. 5. C. Sint tibi.) Sint tibi quotidiana ieiunia, & refectio satietatem fugiens. Nihil enim prodest tibi biduo vel triduo transmisso vacuum portare ventrem, si post pariter obstruatur.
units.tr: De paenitentia, Dist. 5, c. Sint tibi.) Let your fasts be daily, and your refreshment such as avoids satiety. For it profits you nothing, after passing two or three days with an empty belly, to stuff it afterwards all at once.

units.la: Et mox C. Sint tibi ieiunia pura, continua moderataque, id est, quotidie esurire, & quotidie prandere.
units.tr: And soon after, c. Sint tibi: Let your fasts be pure, continual and moderate; that is, to be hungry every day and to dine every day.

units.la: Item. C. Nihil enim prodest homini ieiunare & orare, & alia religionis bona agere, nisi mens ab iniquitate, & ab obtrectationibus prohibeatur.
units.tr: Likewise, c. Nihil enim: For it profits a man nothing to fast and pray, and to perform the other good works of religion, unless his mind is restrained from wickedness and from slander.

units.la: Item. C. Non mediocriter. Nonne rationabiliter homo dignitatem amittit, qui vel ieiunium charitati, aut vigilias praefert sensus integritati?
units.tr: Likewise, c. Non mediocriter: Does not a man rightly lose his dignity who prefers fasting to charity, or vigils to the integrity of the senses?

units.la: Item. C. Ieiunium. Ieiunium autem magnum & generale est abstinere ab iniquitatibus, & ab illicitis voluptatibus saeculi. Quod est perfectum ieiunium in hoc saeculo.
units.tr: Likewise, c. Ieiunium: Fasting, however, great and general, is abstaining from wicked deeds and from unlawful pleasures of the world. This is the perfect fast in this world.

units.la: 12.q.2. Gloria Episcopi.) Hier.ad Paulinum, Plenus venter facile de ieiunijs disputat.
units.tr: 12 q. 2, c. Gloria Episcopi.) Jerome to Paulinus: A full belly easily disputes about fasts.

units.la: Dist.4. C.Inistis.) Telesphorus instituit,ut nō à carnibus modo,sed & à delicijs clerici ab-stinerent. Et additur ibi. Quoniam moribus ventium hoc approbatum non est, aliter agen-tes,transgressionis nos non arguit.
units.tr: Dist. 4, c. Inistis.) Telesphorus laid down that clerics should abstain not only from meat but also from delicacies. And there is added there: Since this has not been approved by the customs of the people, the one who acts otherwise does not accuse us of transgression.

units.la: Et mox C.Sacerdotes. Cæterum piscium e-sus ita Christiano relinquitur,ut hoc ei infirmi-tatis solatium, non luxuriæ pariat incendium. Denique qui à carne abstinent, nequaquam sumptuosiora marinarum belluarum conuiuia pręparent. Vinum quoque ita bibere permitti-tur,ut ebrietatem omnino fugiamus, alioquin restat,ut omnia quæ corporibus libent, simili-ter faciamus.
units.tr: And soon after, c. Sacerdotes: Moreover, the eating of fish is left to the Christian in such a way that this may bring him a comfort of weakness, not a fire of luxury. Finally, those who abstain from flesh by no means prepare more sumptuous banquets of sea creatures. Wine too is permitted to be drunk in such a way that we altogether avoid drunkenness; otherwise it remains that we should do likewise with all the things that please the body.

units.la: Dist. 23.C. Qui Episcopws.) ab Episcopo in examine illius etiam requiritur, si carnium per ceptionem non culpet.
units.tr: Dist. 23, c. Qui Episcopus.) The bishop also asks of him at his examination whether he does not find fault with the eating of meats.

units.la: De pœnitentia. Dist.3.C.Nihil.) Nihil prodest homini ieiunare & orare, & alia religionis opera facere, nisi mens ab iniquitate reuocetur.
units.tr: De paenitentia, Dist. 3, c. Nihil.) Nothing profits a man to fast and pray and perform other works of religion, unless the mind is called back from wickedness.

units.la: De ieiunio superstitioso. August. de Doctrina Christ.
units.tr: On superstitious fasting. Augustine, De doctrina christiana.

units.la: Dist.41.C.Quisquis.) Quisquis rebus pręte-reuntibus restrictius vtitur, quàm sese habent mores eorum cum quibus vivit, aut intempe-rans aut superstitiosus est. Quisquis vero sic eis utitur, ut metas consuetudinis bonorum, inter quos versatur, excedat, aut aliquid signifi-cat, aut flagitiosus est. Vide ibidem plura.
units.tr: Dist. 41, c. Quisquis.) Whoever uses passing things more sparingly than the customs of those among whom he lives require is either intemperate or superstitious. But whoever uses them in such a way as to exceed the bounds of the customs of the good among whom he dwells either signifies something or is shameless. See there for more.

units.la: DE CONFESSIONE AV-riculari.
units.tr: ON AURICULAR CONFESSION.

units.la: CAPVT XXXI.
units.tr: CHAPTER XXXI.

units.la: Confessionem auricularem non esse ad salutem necessariâ multis authorita-tibus Gratianus probat De pœniten-tia. Dist.1. mox ab initio sic scribens.
units.tr: Gratian proves by many authorities that auricular confession is not necessary for salvation. He writes thus, at the very beginning of De poenitentia, Dist. 1.

units.la: Sunt qui dicunt, quamlibet criminis veniâ sine confessione facta ecclesiæ & sacerdotali iudicio posse promereri, iuxta illud Ambrosij super Lucam: Petrus doluit & fleuit quia erravit ut homo. Non invenio quid dixerit, scio quòd fleuit, lachrymas eius lego, satisfactionem non lego.
units.tr: There are some who say that whatever crime is forgiven without confession made to the Church and a priestly judgment can be merited, in line with Ambrose on Luke: "Peter grieved and wept because he had erred as a man." I do not find what he said; I know that he wept, I read of his tears, but I do not read of satisfaction.

units.la: Item Chrysost. Lachrymæ lauant delictum quod pudor est confiteri.
units.tr: Likewise Chrysostom: "Tears wash away the sin which is shameful to confess."

units.la: Item propheta. Sacrificium Deo spiritus co-tribulatus, cor contritum & humiliatum Deus non despicies.
units.tr: Likewise the prophet: "A sacrifice to God is a contrite spirit; a broken and humbled heart God will not despise."

units.la: Item Dauid. Dixi confitebor aduersum me iniustitiam meam Domino, & tu remisisti impietatem peccati mei. Quod Augusti. exponens ait, Magna pietas Dei, ut ad solam promissione peccata dimiserit. Nondum pronunciat ore, & tamen Deus jam audivit in corde, quia ipsum dicere quasi quoddam pronunciare est. Votum enim pro opere reputatur.
units.tr: Likewise David: "I said, I will confess my iniquity against myself to the Lord, and you forgave the wickedness of my sin." Expounding this, Augustine says: "Great is the mercy of God, that by promise alone he forgave sins. He has not yet spoken with his mouth, and yet God has already heard him in his heart, because to say it is almost to pronounce it. For a vow is counted as a deed."

units.la: Et aliquato post. Scindite. Scindite corda vestra & non vestimenta, ostendens contritionem cordis, quae in eiusdem scissione intelligitur, nō in confessione oris (quae pars est exterioris satisfactionis, quâ scissuram vestium nominavit, à parte totum intelligens )peccata dimitti.
units.tr: And a little later: "Rend your hearts and not your garments." This shows that sins are forgiven through the contrition of the heart, which is understood in that rending, and not through confession of the mouth. (That is a part of outward satisfaction, and by naming the rending of garments he has named the part for the whole.)

units.la: Hinc etiam per eundem prophetam ait, dicens: Covertimini ad me in toto corde vestro, & ego convertar ad vos, conversio autem dicitur, quasi cordis undique versio. Si autem cor nostrum undique à malo ad Deum vertitur, mox suae conversionis fructum meretur, ut Deus ab ira sua ad misericordiam conversus, peccati pręstet indulgentiam, cuius primo præparabat vindictam. Unde datur intelligi, quod etiam ore tacente, veniam cosequi possumus.
units.tr: Hence also through the same prophet he says: "Turn to me with all your heart, and I will turn to you." Now conversion is so called as if it were a turning of the heart on every side. If our heart is turned from evil to God on every side, it at once merits the fruit of its conversion, so that God, turned from his anger to mercy, grants forgiveness of sin, the vengeance of which he had been preparing. Whence it is clear that even with the mouth silent we can obtain pardon.

units.la: Hinc etiam leprosi illi, quibus Dominus præ-cepit ut ostenderent se sacerdotibus, in itinere antequam ad sacerdotes venirent mundati sunt. Ex quo facto nimirum datur intelligi., quòd antequam sacerdotibus ora nostra ostendamus, id est, peccata confiteantur, àle-pra peccati mundamur, &c. Vide ibidem plura.
units.tr: Hence also those lepers, whom the Lord commanded to show themselves to the priests, were cleansed on the way before they came to the priests. From this fact it is surely understood that before we show our mouths to the priests, that is, confess our sins, we are cleansed from the guilt of sin, etc. See there for more.

units.la: Ibidem. C. Omnis. Non ergo in confessione peccatum remittitur, quod iam remissum esse probatur. Fit itaque confessio ad ostensionem pœnitentiæ, non ad impetrationé veniæ. Et sicut circumcisio data est Abrahæ in fignū iustitiæ, non in causam iustificationis, sic confessio sacerdoti offertur in signum veniæ acceptæ, non in causam remissionis accipiendæ.
units.tr: In the same place, canon "Omnis": Sin is therefore not remitted in confession, since it is shown to have been already remitted. Confession is made, then, as a display of repentance, not to obtain pardon. And just as circumcision was given to Abraham as a sign of righteousness, not as the cause of justification, so confession is offered to the priest as a sign of pardon already received, not as the cause of remission to be obtained.

units.la: Item. C. Verbum Dei. Verbum Dei dimittit peccata, sacerdos est iudex. Sacerdos quidé suum officium exhibet, & nullius potestatis iura exercet. Ibi Glossa addit. Iudex, id est, mini-ster, Ministerio enim non authoritate habet dimittere.
units.tr: Likewise, canon "Verbum Dei": The word of God forgives sins; the priest is the judge. Indeed the priest performs his office and exercises the rights of no power of his own. The gloss there adds: "Judge, that is, minister, for he has the power to forgive by ministry, not by authority."

units.la: Item C. Quis aliquando. Chryfoft. super epi-stolam ad Heb. Non dico tibi ut te prodas in pu-blicum, neque apud alios te excuses (aliàs ac cuses) sed obedire te volo prophetæ dicenti, Revela ante Deum viam tuam. Ergo tua confi-tere peccata apud Deum verum iudicem, cum oratione delicta tua pronuncia, non lingua, sed conscientiæ tuæ memoria, & tunc demum spe-ra te misericordiam posse consequi.
units.tr: Likewise, canon "Quis aliquando": Chrysostom, on the Epistle to the Hebrews: "I do not tell you to expose yourself in public, nor to excuse yourself before others, but I want you to obey the prophet who says, 'Reveal your way before God.' So confess your sins to God, the true judge; declare your offences with prayer, not with the tongue but by the memory of your conscience; and then at last you may hope to obtain mercy."

units.la: In eandem tamen distinctione Gratianus diversas quoque colligit authoritates. Dicit enim C. Omnis. Alij è contra testantur, dicentes sine Confessione oris & satisfactione Operis neminem à peccato posse mundari, si tempus satisfaciendi habuerit. Tandem Distinctionem hanc Gratianus his fermè verbis concludit. Quibus authoritatibus, vel quibus rationum firma mentis utraque sententia satisfactionis & confessionis innitatur, in medium breviter expo-suimus. Cui autem harum potius adhærendū sit, lectoris iudicio reseruatur. Utraque enim fautores habet sapientes & religiosos viros. Quibus verbis mox subiungit verba Theodori Cantuariensis Episcopi, qui utramque quoque probat sententiam. Deo autem confiteri, perfectorum esse dicit.
units.tr: In the same distinction, however, Gratian also gathers various authorities on the other side. For he says, canon "Omnis": Others, on the contrary, bear witness, saying that no one can be cleansed from sin without confession of the mouth and satisfaction of work, if he has had time to make satisfaction. Finally Gratian concludes this distinction in roughly these words: "By what authorities, or by what firm reasons of the mind, each opinion, of satisfaction and of confession, rests, we have briefly set out in the middle. Which of these ought rather to be adhered to is left to the judgment of the reader, for each has wise and religious men as its supporters." Immediately after these words he adds the words of Theodore, Bishop of Canterbury, who also approves both opinions. But he says that to confess to God is the mark of the perfect.

units.la: De pœnit. Dist. 5. C. )In pœnitentia. Glossator in margine dicit. Videndum est quando oris confessio sit instituta, utrum necessaria sit, vel tantum voluntaria, qualiter sit facienda, & cui, & quando. Dicunt quidam instituta fuisse in paradiso, statim post peccatum, dicente Domino ad Adam, Adam ubi es? Ideo enim quæsiuit, ut ipso confitente peccatum, daretur forma alijs in posterum confitendi. Sed quia in illa interrogatione Dominus minus expresse videbatur ad conconfitendum monuisse, ideo postea exquisiuit à Cain fratricida expressius, Vbi est Abel frater tuus [?] Alij dicunt quòd sub Lege fuit primò instituta, quando Iosue præcepit Achor crimen suum confiteri & lapidatus est 45. Dist. Sed & illud. Alij dicunt quòd in Nouo Testamento à Iacobo dicente, Confitemini alterutrum peccata vestra, &c. SED MELIVS DICITVR eam institutam fuisse à quadam vniuersalis ecclesiæ traditione potius,quàm ex Noui vel Veteris testamenti authoritate. Et traditio ecclesiæ obligatoria est (vt præceptum ar. ii. Dist. In his rebus.) Ergo necessaria est confesio in mortalibus apud nos. APVD GRAECOS NON, QVIA NON EMANAVIT APVD ILLOS TRADITIO TALIS. Sicut nec conficiunt in azymis, sed in fermentatis. Illud ergo Iacobi, Confitemini alterutrum peccata vestra, fuit consilij primò, alioquin ligaret & Græcos, non obstante eorum consuetudine.
units.tr: De poenitentia, Dist. 5, canon "In poenitentia." The glossator says in the margin: "It must be considered when oral confession was instituted, whether it is necessary or only voluntary, how it is to be made, and to whom and when. Some say it was instituted in paradise, immediately after the sin, when the Lord said to Adam, 'Adam, where are you?' For he asked this so that, Adam confessing his sin, a form might be given to others to confess in future. But because in that question the Lord seemed to advise confession less clearly, therefore he afterwards asked Cain the fratricide more plainly, 'Where is Abel your brother?' [?] Others say that it was first instituted under the Law, when Joshua commanded Achan to confess his crime, and he was stoned (45 Dist., 'Sed et illud'). Others say that in the New Testament it was instituted by James saying, 'Confess your sins to one another,' etc. BUT IT IS BETTER SAID that it was instituted by a certain tradition of the universal Church rather than by the authority of the New or Old Testament. And the tradition of the Church is binding (as the precept in article 2, Dist., 'In his rebus'). Therefore confession of mortal sins is necessary among us. AMONG THE GREEKS IT IS NOT SO, BECAUSE NO SUCH TRADITION HAS COME DOWN TO THEM, just as they do not consecrate in unleavened bread but in leavened. So that saying of James, 'Confess your sins to one another,' was first a counsel; otherwise it would bind the Greeks too, notwithstanding their custom."

units.la: DE FERIIS.
units.tr: ON FERIAE.

units.la: De die Dominico.
units.tr: On the Lord's Day.

units.la: CAPVT XXXII.
units.tr: CHAPTER XXXII.

units.la: De Con. Dist. 3. C. Peruenit.) Aliud quoque ad me perlatum est vobis à peruersis hominibus esse prædicatum, vt Dominico die nullus debeat lauari. Et quidem si pro luxuria & pro voluptate quis lauari appetit, hoc fieri nec reliquo quolibet die concedimus. Si autem pro necessitate corporis, hoc nec die Dominico prohibemus.
units.tr: (De Con. Dist. 3. C. Peruenit.) Word has also been brought to me, by you, that perverse men preach that on the Lord's day no one ought to wash. Indeed, if anyone desires to wash for the sake of luxury or pleasure, we do not permit this on any other day either. But if it is for the necessity of the body, we do not forbid it even on the Lord's day.

units.la: Et mox infra C. Iciunia. Die autem Dominica nihil aliud agendum est, nisi Deo vacandum, nulla operatio in illa die sancta agatur, nisi tantùm hymnis & Psalmis & canticis spiritualibus dies illa transfigatur.
units.tr: And shortly after, in C. Iciunia: On the Lord's day nothing else is to be done than to be free for God; no work is to be carried out on that holy day, but the day is to be spent only in hymns, Psalms and spiritual songs.

units.la: De ferijs humanis.
units.tr: On human holidays.

units.la: 24.q.1.Odi & proieci.) Hieronymus. Odit autem Deus, & non solùm odit, sed proijcit festiuitates eorum, qui non celebrant festiuitates Dei, sed suas.
units.tr: (24.q.1. Odi & proieci.) Jerome. God hates, and not only hates but casts away, the festivals of those who do not keep the festivals of God but their own.

units.la: De saltationibus in diebus festis.
units.tr: On dancing on feast days.

units.la: De Con. Dist. 3. C. Irreligiosa) Irreligiosa consuetudo est, quam vulgus per sanctorum solennitates & festiuitates agere consueuit. Populi qui debent diuina officia attendere, saltationibus turpibus inuigilant, cantica non solùm mala canentes, sed etiam religiosorum officiis perstrepunt. Hoc enim utab omnibus prouincijs depellatur, sacerdotum & iudicum à Concilio sancto curæ committitur.
units.tr: (De Con. Dist. 3. C. Irreligiosa.) It is an irreligious custom which the common people are accustomed to practise during the solemnities and festivals of the saints. The people, who ought to attend to the divine offices, give themselves to shameful dances, singing not only wicked songs but also drowning out the services of the religious. This custom is to be driven out from all provinces, and its suppression is committed to the care of the holy Council and of the judges.

units.la: DE ELEEMOSYNIS ET OBLA-tionibus ex rebus iniuste acquisitis.
units.tr: ON ALMS AND OFFERINGS FROM UNJUSTLY ACQUIRED GOODS.

units.la: CAPUT XXXIII.
units.tr: CHAPTER XXXIII.

units.la: 14.q.5. Quòd verò.) Quòd verò eleemosynæ non sint faciendæ ex fœnore vel vsuris, nec quolibet malè acquisito, Augustinus testatur in li-bro de Verbis Domini Tract. 35. Nolite velle eleemosynas facere de fœnore & vsuris.
units.tr: 14 q.5. That indeed) That alms must not be given from usury or interest, nor from anything wrongly acquired, Augustine bears witness in his book on the Words of the Lord, Tractate 35: "Do not wish to make alms from interest and usury."

units.la: Item Augustinus. Immolans ex iniquo, oblatio est maculata. Dona iniquorum non probat altissimus, nec respicit in oblationibus iniquo-rum, nec in multitudine sacrificiorum eorum propitiabitur peccatis. Qui offert sacrificium de substátia pauperis, quasi qui victimat filium in conspectu patris sui.
units.tr: Likewise Augustine: "Whoever sacrifices from what is unjust, his offering is defiled. The Most High does not approve the gifts of the unrighteous, nor does he regard their offerings, nor will he be propitiated for their sins by the multitude of their sacrifices. He who offers a sacrifice from the substance of the poor is like one who slays a son in his father's sight."

units.la: Item. C. Denique. Denique si non potest subveniri alteri, nisi alter lædatur, commodius est neutrum iuvari, quàm gravari alterum.
units.tr: Likewise, C. Finally) Finally, if one cannot help another without injuring a third, it is better that neither be helped than that one be burdened.

units.la: Item. C. Scriptum est. Scriptum est, Victimæ impiorum abominabiles sunt Deo, Vota iustorum placabilia. Neque enim in omnipoten-tis Dei iudicio quid, sed à quo detur inspicitur. Hinc est enim quod scriptum est, Respexit Deus ad Abel & ad munera eius, ad Cain autem & ad munera eius non respexit. Dicturus quippe quia Dominus respexit ad munera, premisit sollicitè quia respexit ad Abel. Ex qua re patenter ostenditur, quia non offerens à munieribus, sed munera ab offerente placuerunt. Dona quippe iniquorum non probat altissimus, nec respicit in oblationibus eorum, nec in multitudine sacrificiorum propitiabitur peccatis eorum.
units.tr: Likewise, C. It is written) It is written: "The sacrifices of the wicked are abominable to God, but the prayers of the righteous are pleasing." For in the judgment of almighty God it is not what is given that is examined, but by whom it is given. Hence it is written: "God looked upon Abel and upon his gifts, but upon Cain and his gifts he did not look." For since he was about to say that the Lord looked upon the gifts, he carefully premised that he looked upon Abel. From this it is plainly shown that the gifts did not please because of the one offering, but the one offering pleased because of the gifts. Indeed, "the Most High does not approve the gifts of the unrighteous, nor does he regard their offerings, nor will he be propitiated for their sins by the multitude of their sacrifices."

units.la: 1. q.1. Non est putanda.) Leo Siagrio Episcopo.
units.tr: 1 q.1. It should not be thought) Leo to Bishop Siagrius.

units.la: Non est putanda eleemosyna, si pauperibus dispensetur, quod ex illicitis rebus acquiritur, quia qui hac intentione mala accipit, vt bene dispenset, grauatur etiam potius quàm iuuetur. Vnde etiam certum est, quia etsi monasteria vel xenodochia, vel aliquid aliud ex pecunia, quæ pro sacris ordinibus datur, construantur, nō proficit mercedi. Ne ergo sub ob tentu eleemosynæ cum peccato aliquid studeamus accipere, prohibet scriptura, dicens: Hostiæ impiorum abominabiles sunt Domino, quæ offeruntur ex scelere. Quicquid enim in Dei sacrificio ex scelere offertur, omnipotentis Dei nō placat iracundiam sed irritat. Hinc rursum scriptum est: Honora Deum de tuis iustis laboribus. Qui ergo malè tollit, vt quasi bene præbeat, constat quia sine dubio Dominum non honorat. Hinc quoque per Solomonem dicitur : Qui offert sacrificium de substantia pauperis, idem est ac si victimet filium in conspectu patris. Quantus autem dolor sit patris perpendamus, si in eius conspectu filius victimetur, & hinc facilecognoscitur, quantus apud Deum dolor exasperatur, quando ei sacrificiu ex rapina tribuitur.
units.tr: Alms should not be thought of as alms if what is acquired from unlawful goods is distributed to the poor, because one who receives with this evil intention, that he may dispense it well, is burdened rather than helped. Hence it is also certain that even if monasteries or hospices, or anything else, are built from money that is given for holy orders, it does not profit the giver for reward. Therefore, lest under the pretext of almsgiving we strive to receive anything with sin, Scripture forbids it, saying: "The sacrifices of the wicked are abominable to the Lord, those offered from wickedness." For whatever is offered from wickedness in the sacrifice of God does not appease the anger of almighty God but provokes it. Again it is written: "Honour God with your just labours." Therefore whoever takes wrongly, so as to give as if rightly, clearly does not honour the Lord. Hence also Solomon says: "He who offers a sacrifice from the substance of the poor is the same as one who slays a son in the sight of his father." Let us weigh how great the father's grief is if his son is slain before his eyes, and from this it is easily recognised how great the grief that is roused before God when a sacrifice is made to him from plunder.

units.la: DE PEREGRINATIONIBVS religionis ergò & locis sacris.
units.tr: ON PILGRIMAGES for the sake of religion and to holy places.

units.la: CAPVT XXXIIII.
units.tr: CHAPTER XXXIIII.

units.la: 12.q.2. Gloria Episcopi.) Hieronymus ad Paulinum. Non Hierosolymis fuisse, sed Hierosolymis bene vixisse, laudandum est.
units.tr: 12 q. 2, Gloria Episcopi. Jerome to Paulinus: It is to be praised not to have been at Jerusalem, but to have lived well at Jerusalem.

units.la: Dist.4o. C. Non est facile.) Hier. Non sanctorum filij sunt, qui tenent loca sanctorum, sed sed qui exercent opera eorum.
units.tr: Dist. 4, c. Non est facile. Jerome: They are not the children of the saints who hold the places of the saints, but those who perform their works.

units.la: Et mox. Gregorius. Nos qui præsumus, non ex locorum vel generis dignitate, sed morum nobilitate innotescere debemus, nec urbium claritate, sed fidei puritate.
units.tr: And soon after, Gregory: We who preside ought to become known not by the dignity of places or of birth, but by the nobility of our morals, and not by the brightness of cities, but by the purity of faith.

units.la: Idem Anastasio presbytero. Non loca vel ordines creatori nostro nos proximos faciunt, sed nos aut merita bona ei coniungunt, aut mala disiungunt.
units.tr: The same, to the presbyter Anastasius: Places or ranks do not make us near to our Creator; rather, good deeds join us to him, or evil deeds separate us from him.

units.la: Item Ambrosius ibidem. Extra paradisum, hoc est, inferiori loco, vir factus, melior inve-nitur: & illa quæ in meliori loco, hoc est, in paradiso facta est, inferior invenitur.
units.tr: Likewise Ambrose, in the same place: A man made outside paradise, that is, in a lower place, is found better; and she who was made in the better place, that is, in paradise, is found inferior.

units.la: Item Gregorius. Loth in ipsa perversa civi-tate fuit justus, in monte peccavit.
units.tr: Likewise Gregory: Lot was righteous in that very wicked city, and he sinned on the mountain.

units.la: Et mox. Quid enim paradiso jucundius, quid cœlo securius? & tamen homo ex paradi-so, & angelus de cœlo peccando cecidit.
units.tr: And soon after: What is more pleasant than paradise, what is more secure than heaven? And yet man fell from paradise, and the angel fell from heaven, by sinning.

units.la: Item Chrysost. ibidem. Multi sacerdotes & pauci sacerdotes, multi in nomine, & pauci in opere. Videte ergo fratres quomodo sedetis super cathedram, quia non cathedra facit sacerdotem, sed sacerdos cathedram. Non locus san-ctificat hominem, sed homo sanctificat locum. Non omnis sacerdos sanctus, sed omnis sanctus sacerdos. Qui bene sederit super cathedrā, honorem accipit, qui male sederit injuriam facit cathedræ, ideoq; malus sacerdos de sacerdo-tio suo crimen acquirit, non dignitatem.
units.tr: Likewise Chrysostom, in the same place: There are many priests and few priests; many in name, and few in deed. See therefore, brethren, how you sit upon the chair: for it is not the chair that makes the priest, but the priest that makes the chair. A place does not sanctify a man, but a man sanctifies the place. Not every priest is holy, but every holy man is a priest. He who sits well upon the chair receives honour; he who sits badly does injury to the chair, and therefore a bad priest acquires guilt, not dignity, from his priesthood.

units.la: DE SEPULTURA, PURGATO-rio, & defunctorum exequijs. CAPUT XXXV.
units.tr: On burial, purgatory, and the funeral rites of the dead. Chapter 35.

units.la: Nihil prodesse sepulturas & exequias operosas.
units.tr: That elaborate burials and funeral rites profit nothing.

units.la: 13.q.2. Animæ.) Curatio vero funeris, conditio sepulturę, pompa exequiarum, magis sunt viuorum solatia, quàm subsidia mortuorum. Si aliquid prodest impio sepultura pretiosa, oberit pio vilis aut nulla.
units.tr: 13.q.2. Animæ.) The care taken over a funeral, the manner of the burial, and the pomp of the rites are rather comforts for the living than aids for the dead. If an costly burial benefits the impious, a cheap burial or none will not harm the pious.

units.la: Nihil referre ubicunque sepeliamur.
units.tr: That it makes no difference where we are buried.

units.la: 13.q.2. Ubicunq.) Chryfost in epist.ad Heb. Ubicunque sepeliamur, Domini est terra & plenitudo eius.
units.tr: 13.q.2. Ubicunq.) Chrysostom on the Epistle to the Hebrews: Wherever we are buried, the earth and its fullness belong to the Lord.

units.la: Sacra loca impios defunctos nihil invare.
units.tr: Holy places do not help impious dead.

units.la: 13. q.2. Quibus peccata.) Augustinus. Quibus peccata dimissa non sunt, à sacris locis post mortem adiuvari non possunt, quia quos peccata graviora deprimunt, si in sacris locis se sepelire faciunt, restat vt de sua pręsumptione judicentur, quia eos sacra loca non liberant, sed de culpa temeritatis accusant.
units.tr: 13.q.2. Quibus peccata.) Augustine: Those whose sins have not been forgiven cannot be helped after death by holy places. For those whom grave sins weigh down, if they have themselves buried in holy places, remain to be judged for their presumption, since holy places do not free them but accuse them of the fault of rashness.

units.la: Et mox Gregorius. Quos peccata gravia deprimunt, ad majorem cumulum damnationis potius quàm ad solutionem eorum corpora in ecclesijs ponuntur.
units.tr: And soon after, Gregory: Those whom grave sins weigh down have their bodies placed in churches to increase their damnation, not to win their release.

units.la: De sepulturis nihil exigendum esse.
units.tr: Nothing is to be demanded for burials.

units.la: § 13.q.2. Quæritur, an pro sepultura mortuorum aliquid sit exigendum? Vbi inter alia. C. Quæsta est. Gregor. in Registro Ianuario Episcopo Sardiniæ scribit.
units.tr: § 13.q.2. The question is whether anything may be demanded for the burial of the dead. Among other things, see C. Quæsta est, where Gregory writes in his Register to Ianuarius, bishop of Sardinia.

units.la: Quæsta est nobis Nereida fœmina clarissima, quòd ab ea solidos pro filiæ suæ sepultura fraternitas vestra velit exigere. Hoc autem vitium & nos, postquam Deo authore ad Episcopatus honorem accessimus, de ecclesia nostra omnino vetuimus, & per prauam dénuo consuetudinem nequaquam vsurpari permisimus, memores quia dum Abraham à filijs Ephron hoc est, à filijs Seor, sepulchrum pretio ad humandum corpus coniugis postularet, pretium accipere renuit, ne commodum de cadauere vi deretur consecutus. Si ergo tantæ considerationis paganus vir fuit, quanto magis nos qui sacerdotes dicimur, hoc facere non debemus? Vnde, hoc auaritiæ vitium, ne in alienis denuo tentari præsumatur, admoneo, sed si quando aliquem in ecclesia vestra sepeliri concedteritis, aliquidem parentes ipsius, proximi, vel hæredes, pro luminaribus spōte quid offerre voluerint, accipere non vetamus. Peti verò aut aliquid exigi omnino prohibemus, ne quod valdè irreligiosum est, aut venalis, quod absit, dicatur ecclesia, aut vos de humanis videamini mortibus gratulari, si ex eorum cadaueribus studeatis quærere quolibet modo compendium.
units.tr: A most distinguished woman, Nereida, has complained to us that your fraternity wishes to exact solidi from her for the burial of her daughter. Now, since by God's authority we have come to the honour of the episcopate, we have entirely forbidden this vice in our church, and we have not permitted it to be reintroduced through the bad custom of recent times, mindful that when Abraham asked the sons of Ephron (that is, the sons of Seor) for a tomb at a price, in order to bury his wife's body, he refused to accept payment, lest he seem to have gained some advantage from the corpse. If, then, a pagan man was of such consideration, how much more ought we, who are called priests, not to do this? Therefore I admonish you about this vice of greed, lest it be presumed to be attempted again in the affairs of others. But if you grant that anyone be buried in your church, we do not forbid that the parents, relatives or heirs of the dead person accept whatever they freely wish to offer for the lights. But we utterly prohibit that anything be asked or exacted, lest the church be called (which God forbid) greedy and mercenary, or you seem to rejoice in human deaths if you seek by any means to gain profit from their corpses.

units.la: Ibidem, ex Concilio Triburiensi. Quid terra terram vendis? Memento quòd terra es, & in terrā reuerteris. Et alibi de homine dictum est, Terram teris, terram geris, & in terram conuerteris, qui de terra sumeris. Domini est terra & plenitudo eius, non hominis.
units.tr: In the same place, from the Council of Trebur: Why do you sell earth for earth? Remember that you are dust, and into dust you shall return. And elsewhere it is said of man: You trample earth, you bear earth, and into earth you shall be turned, you who were taken from earth. The earth is the Lord's and its fullness, not man's.

units.la: Item ex Concilio Varen. Præcipiendum est secundum canonum authoritatem, vt de sepulchris & hominibus sepeliendis nihil muneris exigant.
units.tr: Likewise from the Council of Varennes: It must be enjoined, according to the authority of the canons, that they take no fee at all for tombs or for burying people.

units.la: De purgatorio igne.
units.tr: On the purgatorial fire.

units.la: 27.q.1.C. Impudicus. Pœnitentia purificatorius vocatur ignis. Et est Canon Concilij Triburiensis.
units.tr: 27.q.1.C. Impudicus. Penitence is called a purifying fire. And this is a canon of the Council of Trebur.

units.la: Defunctos ignorare res nostras.
units.tr: The dead do not know our affairs.

units.la: 13.q.2. Qui diuina.) De mortuis autem quaeritur vtrum sciant ea quæ à viuis geruntur. Esaias ex persona populi afflicti ait, Abraham pater noster nescsiuit.
units.tr: 13.q.2. Qui diuina.) But concerning the dead it is asked whether they know what is done by the living. Isaiah, speaking in the person of the afflicted people, says: Abraham our father did not know us.

units.la: Augustinus quoque in libro de Agenda cura pro mortuis illud idem testatur, dicens. C. Fatendum est.) Fatendum est nescire quidem mortuos quid hic agatur dum hic agitur. Postea verò audire ab eis qui hinc ad eos morientes pergunt, non quidem omnia, sed quæ sinuntur etiam isti meminisse, & quæ illos, quibus hæc indicantur oportet audire, &c.
units.tr: Augustine also attests the same thing in his book On the Care to Be Taken for the Dead, saying: It must be admitted that the dead indeed do not know what is done here while it is being done here. Afterwards, however, they hear from those who die and go to them from here, not indeed everything, but what they are permitted to remember, and what those to whom these things are reported ought to hear, and so on.

units.la: De exequijs. August.in lib.de Cur[?] pro mortuis agenda.
units.tr: On funeral rites. Augustine, in his book On the Care to Be Taken for the Dead.

units.la: 13. q.2. Non æstimemus.) Corpori humano quicquid impenditur, non est præsidium salu-tis, sed humanitatis officium.
units.tr: 13.q.2. Non æstimemus.) Whatever is spent on the human body is not a safeguard of salvation but a duty of humanity.

units.la: Orationes viuentium defunctis non prodesse. Hier.
units.tr: The prayers of the living do not profit the dead. Jerome.

units.la: 13. q.2. In præsenti.) In præsenti seculo sci-mus siue orationibus siue consilijs inuicem posse nos adiuuari, cum autem ante tribunal Chri-sti venerimus, nec Iob, nec Daniel, nec Noe rogare posse pro quoquam, sed unumquenque portare onus suum.
units.tr: 13.q.2. In præsenti.) In the present age we know that we can help one another both by prayers and by counsels. But when we have come before the judgement seat of Christ, neither Job, nor Daniel, nor Noah can intercede for anyone, but each shall bear his own burden.

units.la: Quòd defuncti non possint nec excommunicari nec absolui.
units.tr: That the dead can be neither excommunicated nor absolved.

units.la: 24. q.2. Quod autem.) Quòd autem post mortem nullus excommunicari valeat vel absolui, ex verbis Euangelij monstratur, quibus dicitur: Quodcunque ligaueris super terram, &c. Super terramquit, non sub terra, &c.
units.tr: 24.q.2. Quod autem.) That after death no one can be excommunicated or absolved is shown from the words of the Gospel, where it is said: Whatever you bind on earth, etc. It says on earth, not under the earth, etc.

units.la: Et mox. C. Legatur.) Gelasius Papa. Mortuos suscitasse Christum legimus, in errore mortuos absoluisse non legimus. Et quia hoc tantum faciendi solus habuit potestatem, beato Petro Apostolo principaliter mandauit : Quodcunque[?] solueris super terram, erit solutum & in cœlis, & quodcunq; ligaueris super terram, &c. Super terram inquit, nam in ligatione de-functum, nunquam dixit absoluendum.
units.tr: And soon after, C. Legatur.) Pope Gelasius: We read that Christ raised the dead; we do not read that he absolved the dead who were in error. And since he alone had the power to do this, he principally commanded the blessed Apostle Peter: Whatever you loose on earth shall be loosed in heaven also, and whatever you bind on earth, etc. He said on earth; for in binding he never said that the dead person was to be absolved.

units.la: Sunt hæc validissima contra indulgentias Pontificias, & Purgatorij figmentum.
units.tr: These arguments are most powerful against the Papist indulgences and the fiction of Purgatory.

units.la: FINIS.
units.tr: THE END.

units.la: SVMMA LIBRORVM IVRIS QVOD VOCANT CANONICI.
units.tr: SUMMARY OF THE BOOKS OF LAW WHICH THEY CALL CANONICAL.

units.la: Primò continent Decretum à Gratiano collectum, Quod habet partes tres.
units.tr: First, they contain the Decretum collected by Gratian, which has three parts.

units.la: 1. Continet Distinctiones 101.
units.tr: 1. It contains 101 Distinctions.

units.la: 2. Causas 36. intermixto tractatu de poenitentia septem distinctiones continente. In causis tractatur non nisi iuridica.
units.tr: 2. Causes, 36, with an interspersed treatise on repentance containing seven distinctions. Only juridical matters are treated in the Causes.

units.la: 3. Tractatum de consecratione. Is habet distinctiones quinque.
units.tr: 3. A treatise on consecration. It has five distinctions.

units.la: Secutus Gregorius IX. libros quinque Decretalium compilavit.
units.tr: Following him, Gregory IX compiled five books of Decretals.

units.la: 1. De summa Trinitate & fide Catholica
units.tr: 1. Of the supreme Trinity and the Catholic faith.

units.la: 2. De Iudiciis.
units.tr: 2. Of Judgments.

units.la: 3. De vita & honestate clericorum.
units.tr: 3. Of the life and honesty of clerics.

units.la: 4. De sponsalibus & matrimoniis.
units.tr: 4. Of betrothals and marriages.

units.la: 5. De accusationibus, inquisitio-nibus & denuntiationibus.
units.tr: 5. Of accusations, inquisitions and denunciations.

units.la: Postea Bonifacius VIII. Sextum Decretalium edidit in Concilio Lugdunensi. Is habet libros quinque ut supra.
units.tr: Afterwards Boniface VIII published the Sixth book of Decretals at the Council of Lyons. It has five books, as above.

units.la: 1. De summa Trinitate & fide catholica, Titulos habet.22.
units.tr: 1. Of the supreme Trinity and the Catholic faith; it has 22 titles.

units.la: 2. De Iudicijs Tit.15.
units.tr: 2. Of Judgments, title 15.

units.la: 3. De vita & honestate clericorum Tit.24.
units.tr: 3. Of the life and honesty of clerics, title 24.

units.la: 4. De sponsalibus & matrimonijs Tit.3.
units.tr: 4. Of betrothals and marriages, title 3.

units.la: 5. De Accusationibus, Inquisitio-nibus, & Denuntiationibus.
units.tr: 5. Of accusations, inquisitions and denunciations.

units.la: Inde sequuntur Clementis V. constitutiones in Concilio Vienensi editae, quae Clementinae vocantur. Habent libros quinque.
units.tr: Next come the constitutions of Clement V issued at the Council of Vienne, which are called the Clementines. They have five books.

units.la: 1. De summa Trinitate & fide catholica.
units.tr: 1. Of the supreme Trinity and the Catholic faith.

units.la: 2. De Iudicijs.
units.tr: 2. Of Judgments.

units.la: 3. De vita & honestate clericorū.
units.tr: 3. Of the life and honesty of clerics.

units.la: 4. De consanguinitate & affinita-te.
units.tr: 4. Of consanguinity and affinity.

units.la: 5. De magistris, & ne aliquid exi-gatur pro licentia docendi.
units.tr: 5. Of teachers, and that nothing be exacted for the licence to teach.

units.la: Postremò Extravagantes Ioannis XXII.
units.tr: Lastly, the Extravagants of John XXII.
